one_liner: Point-prompt jitter variance of SAM masks predicts human inter-annotator disagreement per object.
problem: SAM outputs change under tiny prompt displacements, but nobody has established what this instability measures. It is treated as a nuisance rather than a signal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the variance of SAM masks under small point jitter (e.g. 5-15 px perturbations) correlates strongly (rank r>0.6) with human inter-annotator mask disagreement on the same object, i.e. prompt sensitivity is an intrinsic object-ambiguity meter, not model noise.
why_important: Would give a free, model-based ambiguity estimator usable for annotation routing, QA, and uncertainty without any labels.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt sensitivity is usually reported as a robustness defect; recasting it as a calibrated measurement of stimulus ambiguity is a different scientific claim. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take a multi-annotator dataset (e.g. LVIS double annotations or a multi-rater medical set), compute SAM jitter-variance per object, correlate with inter-rater IoU. One GPU-day.
main_risk: Correlation may be driven trivially by object size or boundary length; must partial these out.

one_liner: Test whether SAM's three ambiguity heads implement a stable part/object/group hierarchy or an arbitrary mode split.
problem: SAM returns 3 masks for ambiguous prompts. The community assumes they represent whole/part/subpart levels, but this has not been verified across categories.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the identity of each output head is not semantically stable; head-to-granularity assignment flips across categories and even across prompt positions within one object, refuting the implicit 'hierarchy heads' assumption.
why_important: Many pipelines pick a fixed head or trust head order; if assignment is unstable, those pipelines have a silent failure mode.
why_possibly_novel: Papers use the multimask output constantly but rarely audit what each head means. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For 1k objects with part annotations (PartImageNet, PACO), classify each head output as part/object/group by IoU and measure head-assignment consistency statistics.
main_risk: Result may be 'mostly stable', a weaker but still publishable calibration finding.

one_liner: SAM thin-structure failure is caused by patch-grid aliasing, not decoder capacity.
problem: SAM notoriously breaks wires, poles, and thin legs. The default explanation is decoder capacity or training data, but thin structures alias against the 16-px patch grid.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for structures thinner than ~1 patch, SAM mask quality is a strong function of the structure's sub-patch phase and orientation relative to the tokenization grid; phase-averaging inputs (sub-patch shifts) recovers a large fraction of the error without any retraining.
why_important: Locates the failure in tokenization physics rather than learning, which changes what fixes are rational.
why_possibly_novel: Aliasing analyses exist for CNN downsampling (KNOWN: Zhang, 'Making Convolutional Networks Shift-Invariant Again'), but a phase-sweep causal study on promptable ViT segmenters is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Render synthetic bars of controlled width/orientation, sweep sub-pixel translation, plot SAM IoU vs phase; then test phase-jitter ensembling on real wire/pole classes.
main_risk: Failure may be dominated by training-data scarcity of thin objects, with aliasing a minor term.

one_liner: Box prompts act as scale priors that override image evidence when box and object conflict.
problem: Box-prompted SAM is assumed to segment 'the object in the box', but boxes also carry scale/aspect information the model may trust more than pixels.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: when a box is systematically inflated or squashed (e.g. 1.5x width), SAM's mask follows the box geometry rather than the true object boundary in a predictable, measurable way (mask aspect regresses toward box aspect), demonstrating that boxes are priors, not just localizers.
why_important: Auto-labeling pipelines feed detector boxes into SAM; detector box errors would then be copied into masks, correlated and invisible.
why_possibly_novel: Box-perturbation robustness is reported as a scalar; the directional 'mask follows box geometry' regression law is unquantified. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On COCO GT boxes, apply controlled aspect/scale perturbations, fit mask-aspect vs box-aspect response curves per category.
main_risk: Effect may be small for well-textured objects and only matter for low-contrast ones; need stratified analysis.

one_liner: Negative clicks carve masks asymmetrically: exclusion near boundaries works, exclusion inside homogeneous regions fails.
problem: Interactive SAM correction assumes positive and negative clicks are symmetric information. Practitioners observe negatives often do nothing or overshoot.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the information gain of a negative click is a strong function of local feature contrast: negatives placed in feature-homogeneous regions (same texture as the object) reduce error far less per click than positives of matched placement, making click budgets asymmetric.
why_important: Click-budget benchmarks (NoC) average over this; interfaces could route users toward the click type with higher expected gain.
why_possibly_novel: Click simulators treat clicks symmetrically; a measured positive/negative information asymmetry law would be new. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On DAVIS/COCO objects, exhaustively grid-place a single corrective negative vs positive click, map per-pixel error reduction, compare distributions.
main_risk: Asymmetry might be an artifact of one model version; verify on SAM-HQ and SAM2 image mode.

one_liner: SAM snaps to luminance edges even when the semantic boundary is texture- or material-defined; quantify the edge-snapping bias.
problem: SAM boundaries look crisp, but crispness may come from locking onto intensity gradients rather than the true semantic boundary (e.g. shadow edges, printed patterns).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on stimuli where the semantic boundary and the strongest local intensity edge are deliberately separated (shadow crossing an object, texture-defined figure), SAM boundary placement is biased toward the intensity edge by a measurable offset that scales with edge contrast ratio.
why_important: Explains a family of confident-but-wrong boundaries (shadow inclusion, pattern following) that boundary metrics currently lump into generic error.
why_possibly_novel: Edge-snapping is folklore; a psychophysics-style controlled quantification with synthesized conflict stimuli appears missing. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Composite objects with controllable shadow/texture edges (cut-and-paste with relighting), sweep contrast, measure boundary displacement toward distractor edge.
main_risk: Synthetic conflict stimuli may be out-of-distribution in ways that exaggerate the bias.

one_liner: SAM's predicted-IoU head is miscalibrated in a shape-dependent way: overconfident on concave and perforated objects.
problem: Predicted IoU is widely used to filter auto-generated masks (SA-1B itself was built this way), but its calibration as a function of object geometry is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: predicted-IoU error is systematically structured by shape statistics (convexity, genus, boundary tortuosity): calibration is good for convex blobs and degrades monotonically with concavity/holes, so IoU-filtered datasets are silently biased toward simple shapes.
why_important: If true, every dataset distilled through SAM confidence filtering under-represents complex shapes, and models trained on them inherit a simplicity prior - a compounding ecosystem bias.
why_possibly_novel: Connects mask-confidence calibration to dataset evolution/inbreeding; per-geometry calibration audits of SAM are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On COCO/ADE GT, bin objects by convexity and genus, plot predicted vs actual IoU per bin; then measure shape statistics of SA-1B vs a human-annotated reference.
main_risk: SA-1B shape bias could stem from its prompting grid rather than the IoU filter; needs an ablation to attribute.

one_liner: Iterative click sequences are path-dependent: the same click set in different orders yields different SAM masks.
problem: Interactive segmentation evaluation assumes the final mask depends on the set of corrections, but SAM conditions on previous mask state, making the process a dynamical system.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: permuting the order of an identical set of 4-6 clicks changes final mask IoU by a nontrivial margin (>5 IoU on ambiguous objects), and there exist 'trap' orders from which no small click set recovers - i.e. interactive SAM has attractor states.
why_important: Path dependence means NoC benchmarks measure simulator policy as much as model quality, and real users can get stuck through no fault of their own.
why_possibly_novel: Framing interactive segmentation as a dynamical system with attractors and measuring order effects is not standard. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sample 200 hard objects, enumerate permutations of a fixed 4-click set, report IoU dispersion and identify absorbing bad states.
main_risk: Effect may vanish on easy objects, limiting scope to the ambiguous tail (which is arguably where it matters).

one_liner: Predict SAM failure before decoding from encoder attention statistics alone.
problem: Failure detection for SAM currently uses output-side signals (predicted IoU, stability score). Whether failure is already legible in the encoder is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a linear probe on encoder attention-map statistics (entropy, sink mass, head disagreement) at the prompt location predicts mask failure (IoU<0.5) with AUROC>0.8, i.e. most failures are encoder-representation failures, not decoder mistakes.
why_important: Locates the failure stage (representation vs readout), and gives a cheap abort/route-to-human signal that does not require running multiple decodes.
why_possibly_novel: Stage-attribution of promptable segmentation failures is largely unexplored. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Log encoder statistics + outcome over 20k prompts on 3 datasets, train the probe, compare AUROC vs predicted-IoU baseline.
main_risk: Probe may just re-learn object size/contrast correlates of difficulty rather than model-internal evidence.

one_liner: SAM merges instances of periodic textures (fences, railings, book spines) when spatial period is below token resolution.
problem: Repeated near-identical instances are a known annoyance, but the quantitative relationship between texture period and instance-merging has not been mapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: instance-level prompting accuracy on periodic arrays collapses sharply when the array period drops below ~2 patch widths, and the collapse point shifts predictably with input resolution - a measurable 'instance Nyquist limit'.
why_important: Defines a hard operating boundary for promptable segmentation in retail, agriculture (crop rows), and document images, and predicts exactly when zooming will fix it.
why_possibly_novel: A Nyquist-style law for instance separability in promptable models is a crisper claim than 'small objects are hard'. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Procedurally render object arrays with controlled period/count, prompt the center instance, plot single-instance IoU vs period/patch ratio across resolutions.
main_risk: Real scenes add occlusion and perspective; the clean law may blur in the wild.

one_liner: Sub-patch objects get quantized to the token grid: measure the staircase floor of SAM on <16 px objects.
problem: SAM small-object failure is usually attributed to semantics or data. A simpler mechanical explanation: masks cannot express detail below feature-map resolution regardless of semantics.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for objects below ~16 px, SAM's best-achievable IoU (even with oracle prompts and oracle head choice) is bounded by a resolution floor computable from the mask-decoder upsampling path, and observed errors match this floor - meaning small-object failure is mostly resolution, not recognition.
why_important: Separates 'model cannot see it' from 'model cannot draw it'; the fix differs completely (zoom pipelines vs retraining).
why_possibly_novel: An explicit computed-vs-observed error floor comparison for promptable segmenters is missing. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take objects at many scales, segment at native + digitally zoomed resolution, compare the error decomposition against the theoretical decoder floor.
main_risk: Decoder nonlinearity may make the 'theoretical floor' hard to define cleanly; may need an empirical oracle-upsampler proxy.

one_liner: Cluster SAM's mask-token embeddings across millions of prompts to test whether text-free training induced a latent semantic taxonomy.
problem: SAM was trained without labels. Whether its object-level tokens organize into semantic structure (animal vs artifact, etc.) or purely geometric structure is an open representational question.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mask-token embeddings cluster by geometry (shape, size, texture) and NOT by semantic category - i.e. semantic clustering accuracy will be near chance once shape covariates are controlled, contradicting casual claims that 'SAM knows objects'.
why_important: Clarifies what class-agnostic pretraining actually learns, informing when SAM features can and cannot substitute for semantic backbones.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled geometry-vs-semantics decomposition of SAM token space (with shape covariates regressed out) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Extract mask tokens for 50k labeled COCO/ADE objects, run category linear probe before/after regressing out shape descriptors; compare with a CLIP-feature control.
main_risk: Shape and semantics are naturally confounded; the covariate control must be convincing.

one_liner: Define 'prompt compressibility' - the minimum click set reproducing a GT mask - as a measurable object complexity scale.
problem: There is no principled per-object measure of how hard an object is for promptable segmentation; NoC conflates simulator policy with intrinsic difficulty.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the minimal sufficient prompt set size (found by search, not by a fixed simulator) forms a stable complexity measure that (a) is consistent across SAM variants and (b) predicts real human annotation time better than object area, boundary length, or NoC from standard simulators.
why_important: Would give datasets an intrinsic difficulty axis and annotation-cost predictor, useful for budgeting and curriculum design.
why_possibly_novel: Kolmogorov-style 'description length in clicks' framing of segmentation difficulty appears new. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Beam-search minimal click sets on 500 objects, correlate with logged human annotation times (e.g. from an internal labeling session).
main_risk: Search cost per object; and minimality may be model-specific despite the cross-variant claim.

one_liner: Map the phase diagram of prompt positions that flip SAM mask topology - the 'topological instability atlas' of an image.
problem: Some single-pixel prompt moves cause categorical mask changes (object vs part vs background leak). Where these cliff edges live and what image structure creates them is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: topology-flip boundaries in prompt space concentrate along medial-axis and low-contrast corridors of the underlying objects, so the instability atlas is predictable from image structure without running SAM densely.
why_important: Predictable instability zones let interfaces warn users, let simulators sample fairly, and reveal what the decoder's implicit object model is.
why_possibly_novel: Dense prompt-space mapping exists in robustness papers as averages; structural prediction of instability geography is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Densely evaluate prompts on 100 images, compute flip boundaries, test prediction from medial axis + local contrast features.
main_risk: Atlas may be high-frequency noise rather than structured, making prediction fail (itself an informative negative).

one_liner: Attribute SAM small-object errors to resolution vs recognition with a zoom-oracle: how much failure survives perfect zoom?
problem: Zoom-in cascades are the standard small-object fix, but nobody has cleanly measured what fraction of failure is unfixable by resolution alone.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: with an oracle crop centered on each small object at optimal zoom, SAM recovers >70% of the IoU gap on natural images, but a hard residual remains concentrated in low-contrast and cluttered contexts where recognition, not resolution, is the limit.
why_important: Quantifies the ceiling of all zoom-based engineering fixes and identifies the residual scientific problem.
why_possibly_novel: The oracle-zoom decomposition, reported per failure type, is a cleaner attribution than existing multi-scale ablations. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVIS-small and xView-like imagery, run SAM native vs oracle-crop, decompose the gap by contrast/clutter strata.
main_risk: Oracle crops change context available to the model, conflating context loss with resolution gain; needs padded-crop controls.

one_liner: SAM draws sharper boundaries than humans do on intrinsically fuzzy objects - measure the sharpness mismatch distribution.
problem: On hair, fur, foliage, and smoke-like regions, ground truth is soft but SAM outputs hard crisp curves. The statistical mismatch between model boundary sharpness and human boundary width is undocumented.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM's boundary transition width is near-constant (a decoder property) regardless of the stimulus' physical edge width, whereas human annotations widen with stimulus fuzziness - so a single scalar 'sharpness mismatch' per class predicts where SAM boundary metrics are meaningless.
why_important: Identifies where binary mask evaluation stops being well-posed and matting-style evaluation must take over.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-width statistics as a function of stimulus edge width, compared human-vs-model, appears unmeasured. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate edge transition widths from alpha mattes (Adobe matting datasets), compare with SAM logit transition widths per stimulus.
main_risk: Logit sharpness may be an artifact of the final threshold rather than the representation; inspect pre-threshold logits.

one_liner: SA-1B's auto-mask pipeline imprinted a closed-compact-region prior on SAM; open curves and wiry objects are structurally outside its output space.
problem: SAM fails on wires, cracks, and open contours. This is usually attributed to rarity, but SA-1B's generation process (grid prompts + IoU filtering) may have structurally excluded non-blob masks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the shape-statistics gap between SA-1B masks and a reference human-annotated distribution (elongation, genus, solidity tails) quantitatively predicts SAM's per-shape-class failure rates - data-generating-process bias, not visual difficulty, explains wiry-object failure.
why_important: Reframes a famous failure mode as an auditable dataset-construction artifact with a testable fingerprint, guiding what data (not architecture) to fix.
why_possibly_novel: Causal linking of SA-1B pipeline choices to specific inference-time failure geometry is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute shape-statistic histograms of SA-1B (public) vs OpenImages/ADE masks; regress SAM failure rate per shape bin against representation gap.
main_risk: Correlation not causation; a small targeted fine-tune on synthetic wiry masks would be needed for the causal leg.

one_liner: At high JPEG compression, SAM boundaries snap to 8x8 block-grid artifacts; quantify compression-boundary coupling.
problem: Deployment images are heavily compressed; block artifacts create fake edges aligned to a fixed grid. Whether promptable models lock onto them is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: as JPEG quality decreases, the phase histogram of SAM boundary positions modulo 8 px develops peaks at block boundaries, and this grid-snapping accounts for a measurable share of the compression-induced IoU drop.
why_important: A concrete, correctable deployment failure (choose compression settings / add dither) with a clean forensic signature.
why_possibly_novel: Compression robustness is studied as an aggregate score; the grid-phase forensic analysis of boundary placement appears new. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep JPEG quality on COCO, compute boundary-position phase histograms and IoU deltas; test dithered decompression as mitigation.
main_risk: Modern webp/HEIC pipelines differ; scope must include them to stay relevant.

one_liner: Test compositionality of SAM's image embedding: does masked-object feature subtraction behave algebraically?
problem: SAM's encoder embedding is treated as a black box. Whether object presence is encoded additively (removable by subtraction, movable by translation in feature space) is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM embeddings are NOT compositional - subtracting the pooled feature of an object region does not suppress its segmentability, showing objectness is encoded relationally rather than additively (falsifiable: if subtraction works, hypothesis is dead).
why_important: Determines whether feature-space editing (fast object removal, counterfactual segmentation) is possible without pixel-space editing, and probes the representation's algebra.
why_possibly_novel: Feature-arithmetic tests are common for word/CLIP embeddings, rare for dense promptable encoders. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For 500 objects: embed image, ablate object features (zero/subtract/shuffle), re-run decoder with same prompt, measure mask persistence.
main_risk: Decoder may re-hallucinate objects from context, confounding 'representation holds object' with 'decoder guesses'.

one_liner: Grid-prompted 'segment everything' mode has a recall geometry: elongated and off-grid objects are systematically missed as a function of grid density.
problem: Everything-mode uses a regular point grid + NMS; its recall is assumed to rise smoothly with density, but object geometry interacts with the grid non-uniformly.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at fixed grid density, per-object recall is predicted by the probability that a grid point lands in the object's 'promptable core' (a computable region smaller than the mask), so everything-mode recall can be forecast per dataset without running the model, and elongated objects need quadratically denser grids.
why_important: Everything-mode underlies many auto-annotation pipelines; a predictive recall law would let people budget grid density instead of guessing.
why_possibly_novel: Treats prompt-grid coverage as a geometric sampling problem with a testable analytic form. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate promptable cores on 1k objects (dense prompting), derive predicted recall vs grid density, verify against actual everything-mode runs.
main_risk: NMS interactions between neighboring objects may break the independent-coverage approximation.

one_liner: Disagreement among SAM's three heads beats its predicted-IoU score as an out-of-distribution failure detector.
problem: Pipelines filter SAM outputs by predicted IoU, but that head was trained in-distribution and may be blind to OOD failure; the multimask heads provide a free ensemble signal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: inter-head mask disagreement (pairwise IoU among the 3 outputs) is a better OOD failure predictor than predicted IoU on shifted domains (medical, thermal, art), with the gap growing with shift severity.
why_important: A zero-cost reliability signal for the most common filtering decision in SAM pipelines.
why_possibly_novel: Using ambiguity-head disagreement specifically as an OOD detector, benchmarked against the IoU head, is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On 5 shifted datasets with GT, compute AUROC of both signals for predicting IoU<0.5; one GPU-day.
main_risk: Both signals may fail together on strong shift, leaving no winner (still a useful negative result).

one_liner: The Jacobian of SAM's mask w.r.t. prompt location is a label-free edge/structure detector - characterize what it computes.
problem: Differentiating mask output with respect to prompt coordinates yields a sensitivity field over the image. What classical quantity this field approximates (edges, medial axis, affordance boundaries) is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the prompt-Jacobian field concentrates on object-ownership boundaries rather than photometric edges, so it matches human-annotated occlusion/ownership boundaries (BSDS-style) better than Canny or learned edge detectors that use photometry alone.
why_important: Would extract a new dense output (boundary ownership) from a frozen model for free, and reveal what geometric structure prompt conditioning learned.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt-space differentiation as a readout mechanism appears unexplored. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Finite-difference the prompt over a coarse grid on BSDS500 images, evaluate against boundary GT vs Canny/HED baselines.
main_risk: Field may be too noisy at feasible grid resolutions; smoothing may destroy the claimed specificity.

one_liner: A dataset-level 'promptability score' measured on unlabeled images predicts downstream annotation cost and model fine-tuning difficulty.
problem: Teams choose datasets/domains to annotate with no quantitative predictor of how much SAM-assisted annotation will actually save.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: an unlabeled-data statistic built from SAM behavior (jitter stability, head agreement, everything-mode mask density entropy) predicts realized human correction time per image with r>0.7 across domains, enabling annotation budgeting before any labeling starts.
why_important: Converts anecdotal 'SAM works/doesn't work on our data' into a forecastable quantity with direct economic value.
why_possibly_novel: Dataset-level meta-prediction of assisted-annotation cost is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Across 8 public datasets with known annotation protocols, compute the score and correlate with measured correction effort on 50 images each.
main_risk: Ground-truth 'annotation cost' is hard to standardize across domains; needs a controlled labeling study.

one_liner: SAM has an orientation anisotropy: elongated vertical vs horizontal objects segment differently, inherited from photo statistics.
problem: Natural photo datasets have anisotropic orientation statistics (gravity, horizons). Whether promptable segmenters are measurably anisotropic - and whether that transfers as failure on rotated/aerial imagery - is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM IoU on matched elongated objects differs by orientation (e.g. worse for diagonal orientations), the anisotropy profile mirrors SA-1B orientation statistics, and it predicts a large share of SAM's aerial/rotated-image degradation.
why_important: Aerial, microscopy, and document images have no canonical orientation; an inherited gravity prior would be a systematic transfer failure with a cheap fix (orientation TTA).
why_possibly_novel: Orientation-anisotropy audits exist for CN classifiers; for promptable segmentation with a data-statistics linkage, UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Rotate a fixed object set through 24 angles (with anti-aliased resampling controls), plot IoU vs angle; compare with SA-1B mask orientation histogram.
main_risk: Resampling artifacts can masquerade as model anisotropy; controls must be strict.

one_liner: SAM is biased toward simply-connected masks: objects with holes get their holes filled, at a rate predictable from training statistics.
problem: Donut-topology objects (mugs seen through handles, rings, fences around gaps) require genus>0 masks. Whether promptable models can express and choose them is unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM fills genus>0 regions at a high rate even when photometric evidence for the hole is strong, and the fill rate tracks the (near-zero) frequency of holed masks in SA-1B - an expressivity-through-data limitation, falsifiable by fine-tuning on synthetic holed masks and watching the rate drop.
why_important: Topology errors corrupt measurement applications (porosity, occlusion reasoning) and are invisible in IoU at small hole sizes.
why_possibly_novel: Genus-statistics audit linking training-mask topology to inference topology bias is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate 300 holed-object images, measure hole preservation vs hole size/contrast; count genus>0 masks in SA-1B sample for the comparison.
main_risk: Annotated GT for holes is scarce; may need manual curation effort.

one_liner: Masklet drift rate in SAM2 is predictable from first-frame single-image ambiguity before any tracking happens.
problem: Video object segmentation failures appear frame-by-frame, but the community treats drift as a temporal phenomenon; it may be pre-determined by initial mask ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-object drift rate (IoU decay slope over frames) is predicted (r>0.6) by frame-0 measurements alone (prompt-jitter variance, head disagreement), meaning drift is mostly ambiguity amplification, not accumulating temporal error.
why_important: Enables pre-flight triage of which objects need human keyframing before wasting tracking compute, and reorients drift research from temporal machinery to initial disambiguation.
why_possibly_novel: Prediction of temporal failure from purely static initial measurements is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On DAVIS/MOSE, regress observed drift slopes on frame-0 ambiguity features; compare against motion-based predictors.
main_risk: Drift may be dominated by discrete events (occlusions) that no frame-0 signal can foresee.

one_liner: SAM2 re-identification after occlusion falls off a cliff, not a slope: map the memory-horizon discontinuity.
problem: How re-acquisition probability depends on occlusion duration is unmeasured; a cliff vs gradual decay implies different mechanisms (buffer eviction vs feature fade).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-ID success is roughly flat until an occlusion-length threshold tied to the memory-bank capacity/eviction rule, then collapses discontinuously - and the threshold moves when memory size is reconfigured, causally implicating eviction policy rather than appearance change.
why_important: A sharp, configurable failure boundary is exactly what deployment safety cases need, and the causal knob test tells us what to redesign.
why_possibly_novel: Occlusion-duration response curves with memory-size interventions are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Procedurally insert variable-length full occlusions into videos, plot re-ID rate vs duration for 3 memory configurations.
main_risk: Entangled confound: longer occlusion often co-occurs with more scene change; synthetic occluders control this.

one_liner: Test whether SAM2 tracks appearance or location: teleport experiments separating the two.
problem: When target and distractor swap positions between frames, does SAM2 follow the pixels or the place? The relative weighting of location prior vs appearance matching is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at low frame rates or after cuts, SAM2 follows spatial location over appearance (segmenting whatever now occupies the old position) with probability rising as inter-frame displacement grows - i.e. its memory attention degrades into a location prior under temporal sparsity.
why_important: Determines trustworthiness on cut-heavy or low-fps footage (surveillance, wildlife cameras, medical cine loops).
why_possibly_novel: Teleport/swap causal probes are standard in psychology, rare for VOS models. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct swap/teleport clips from static images (two similar objects exchanging positions with controlled gaps), measure follow-the-object vs follow-the-place rates.
main_risk: Synthetic cuts may be OOD; validate on natural cut footage with manual GT.

one_liner: SAM2 masklets shrink over time: an erosion bias in memory-conditioned decoding.
problem: Anecdotally, tracked masks lose thin parts and extremities over long sequences. Whether there is a systematic signed area bias (erosion vs dilation) and what causes it is unstudied.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the signed relative-area error of SAM2 masklets trends negative over time, concentrated at high-curvature and thin regions, because memory features average over past masks and act as a low-pass shape filter - falsifiable by measuring area drift on constant-size rigid objects.
why_important: Systematic bias (unlike variance) is correctable post-hoc if characterized; also matters for measurement uses (lesion tracking, plant growth).
why_possibly_novel: Signed morphological bias analysis of memory-based VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Track rigid constant-scale objects (fixed camera) for 500+ frames, plot signed area and per-curvature-bin boundary offset vs time.
main_risk: Bias might be dataset-specific (motion blur correlates with extremities), needs controlled rigid-object footage.

one_liner: Distractor-swap probability in SAM2 is a logistic function of feature-space similarity between target and distractor - fit the curve.
problem: Identity switches to similar-looking instances are the canonical multi-object failure, but there is no quantitative model of when they happen.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: swap probability during a crossing event follows a logistic curve in embedding cosine similarity between target and distractor, with a threshold that is stable across videos - giving a predictive, per-scene identity-risk score computable before tracking.
why_important: Predictive risk scoring for identity switches would let pipelines pre-allocate human checks in crowded scenes (cell tracking, sports, herds).
why_possibly_novel: A fitted psychometric-style swap curve for memory-based VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mine crossing events in MOSE/OVIS, log embedding similarity and swap outcome, fit and cross-validate the logistic.
main_risk: Similarity measured with the model's own embedding may be circular; test external embeddings too.

one_liner: SAM2 accuracy is non-monotonic in frame rate: temporal aliasing hurts fast periodic motion at intermediate fps.
problem: Everyone assumes more fps is better or at worst neutral. For periodic or oscillating motion, intermediate sampling may alias into confusing pseudo-motion.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for objects with periodic motion (wings, wheels, machinery), tracking quality vs frame rate has a dip where sampling aliases the motion (near integer ratios of motion period), recoverable by either higher fps or, counter-intuitively, lower fps.
why_important: Frame-rate is a controllable deployment knob; a non-monotonic law changes how people configure cameras and subsample videos for annotation.
why_possibly_novel: Temporal-aliasing analysis of memory-based segmentation trackers is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: High-fps source videos of periodic motion, subsample at many rates, plot J&F vs rate; look for aliasing dips at predicted ratios.
main_risk: Effect may be confined to a narrow class of scenes; scope must be honest.

one_liner: Memory poisoning: quantify how one corrupted frame propagates through SAM2's memory bank - is error injection sub- or super-linear?
problem: Robustness of memory-augmented trackers to single-frame corruption (glare, compression burst, occluder) is unmeasured; the memory could either dilute or amplify a bad write.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a single adversarially bad mask written to memory degrades subsequent frames super-linearly in time for ambiguous targets (self-reinforcing retrieval) but is diluted for distinctive targets - the bifurcation is predicted by target-distractor similarity.
why_important: Determines whether memory needs write-gating/quarantine, and defines a concrete attack surface for safety-critical tracking.
why_possibly_novel: Error-injection response analysis of segmentation memory banks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Inject controlled mask corruptions at frame t, measure IoU trajectories after t vs matched controls across target types.
main_risk: Injection method may not represent natural corruption; use both synthetic and natural (glare/blur) events.

one_liner: Which frame you prompt matters more than how well you prompt it: middle-frame prompting beats first-frame in long videos.
problem: The universal convention prompts frame 0. Information-theoretically the best anchor frame is the one minimizing appearance distance to the rest of the video.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: prompting the medoid frame (closest to all others in feature space) improves whole-video J&F more than upgrading the frame-0 prompt from 1 click to a perfect mask - anchor selection dominates prompt quality beyond a video-length threshold.
why_important: Zero-cost accuracy gains for every SAM2 pipeline, and reframes interactive video annotation as a frame-selection problem first.
why_possibly_novel: Anchor-frame optimality vs prompt-quality tradeoff quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVOS/long videos, compare first-frame perfect-mask vs medoid-frame single-click prompting under matched budgets.
main_risk: Medoid selection needs the whole video (offline only); streaming variant may lose the effect.

one_liner: VOS metrics reward temporal smoothness, not correctness: an oracle temporal smoother improves J&F without new information.
problem: If post-hoc smoothing of masks (no access to images) improves benchmark scores, the metric partially measures smoothness style rather than segmentation quality.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a model-free temporal mask smoother (shape-consistent filtering of existing predictions) improves J&F on standard VOS benchmarks by a nontrivial margin for many methods, and method rankings change when evaluation adds unsmoothable per-frame probes - demonstrating metric gaming headroom.
why_important: If rankings are partially smoothness rankings, years of architecture conclusions need re-reading; also a cheap test-time trick that should be disclosed.
why_possibly_novel: Smoothing-only ablation as a metric audit for VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply temporal morphological smoothing to frozen predictions of 5 public methods, report J&F deltas and rank flips.
main_risk: If gains are negligible the audit vindicates the metric (still worth publishing as a check).

one_liner: Recency-based memory is provably wrong for periodic scenes: diversity-sampled memory should beat recency at equal size.
problem: SAM2-style memories favor recent frames. For periodic or revisiting content (orbiting views, back-and-forth motion), recency discards the most predictive exemplars.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched memory budget, exemplar selection by appearance-diversity (k-center over frame features) outperforms recency on videos with periodicity/revisits, while recency wins on smooth-drift videos - a measurable regime split that current fixed policies straddle badly.
why_important: Identifies a principled scene-conditional memory policy question rather than a bigger-memory arms race.
why_possibly_novel: Regime-mapped comparison of memory selection policies in promptable video segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Reconfigure SAM2 memory selection at inference (no retraining) with diversity sampling; evaluate on periodic vs drift video subsets.
main_risk: Inference-time policy swap without retraining may be off-manifold for the memory attention.

one_liner: Does temporal context help or hurt on static camouflaged objects? SAM2 vs per-frame SAM on motionless targets.
problem: Temporal models are assumed to help always. For a static camouflaged animal, memory frames add no new information but may add noise accumulation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on static targets in moving-texture scenes (wind, water), SAM2's memory hurts relative to independent per-frame segmentation of the anchor mask, because background texture change is misread as object change - temporal context has a sign-flipping value depending on motion source.
why_important: Establishes when video machinery should be bypassed - important for camouflage, surveillance, and medical cine where targets barely move.
why_possibly_novel: Signed value-of-temporal-context analysis conditioned on motion source is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: MoCA-Mask static-segment subset: compare SAM2 propagation vs frozen anchor mask + per-frame refinement under matched prompts.
main_risk: Truly static targets are rare in benchmarks; may need curated clips.

one_liner: Topology-change events (splitting, merging, pouring) are an unhandled event class in video segmentation - build the taxonomy and measure failure.
problem: Masklets assume persistent object identity, but real objects split (dough, cells, liquids) and merge. What trackers do at these events is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at split events, memory-based trackers deterministically follow the larger fragment (area-weighted attention), losing the smaller one at a rate predicted by fragment area ratio - a simple law that a fragment-aware evaluation would expose.
why_important: Cell biology, cooking/robotics, and material handling all need split/merge tracking; knowing the default failure law is step one.
why_possibly_novel: An event-taxonomy benchmark for topology changes in VOS is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate 100 split events (cell videos, cutting food), measure which fragment retains identity vs area ratio.
main_risk: Annotation ambiguity about which fragment 'is' the original; needs a convention.

one_liner: Joint multi-object tracking in SAM2 degrades per-object accuracy vs independent runs: measure memory contention.
problem: SAM2 tracks multiple objects with shared compute/memory. Whether objects interfere (contention) or help (context) compared to isolated single-object runs is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-object J&F drops as tracked-object count rises even without spatial interaction, and the drop concentrates on objects sharing appearance clusters - evidence of representational contention in shared memory attention rather than mere occlusion effects.
why_important: Determines scaling behavior for dense-instance video annotation and whether parallel independent runs (costly) are secretly necessary.
why_possibly_novel: Contention-vs-context decomposition with non-interacting object sets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On multi-object videos, compare joint tracking vs one-object-at-a-time runs on identical prompts; stratify by pairwise similarity.
main_risk: Implementation details (per-object memory in SAM2) may already isolate objects; verify against the actual architecture first (KNOWN: SAM2 keeps per-object state; contention could still arise via shared backbone resolution and NMS-like interactions).

one_liner: Camera-zoom sequences reveal scale lag: memory features anchor to old object scale and delay mask growth.
problem: During zoom (optical or dolly), object scale changes smoothly, but memory frames encode stale scales. Scale-adaptation dynamics of memory trackers are unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under monotonic zoom, SAM2 mask area lags true object area with a measurable time constant proportional to memory length, producing systematic under-segmentation during zoom-in and over-segmentation during zoom-out.
why_important: Zoom is ubiquitous (broadcast, drones, microscopy autofocus); a signed predictable lag is correctable but only if characterized.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-lag time-constant measurement for memory trackers is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Synthesize exact-zoom sequences from high-res stills (crop pyramids), measure mask-area lag vs zoom rate and memory length.
main_risk: Synthetic zoom lacks parallax; confirm on real dolly footage subset.

one_liner: Forward-backward tracking asymmetry as a free uncertainty signal: where the two directions disagree, the tracker is wrong.
problem: Tracking a video forward vs backward should ideally give the same masks; divergence indicates unreliability, but this self-consistency signal is not exploited or characterized for modern VOS.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: forward-backward mask disagreement per frame predicts actual error (AUROC>0.85) better than model confidence outputs, and the asymmetry is directional - errors accumulate on the direction that first encounters ambiguity - enabling label-free error localization in time.
why_important: Gives annotation pipelines an automatic 'inspect here' signal, cutting human video-QA cost.
why_possibly_novel: Cycle-consistency is classic for optical flow (KNOWN); its calibration as an error detector for memory-based masklets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run SAM2 both directions on DAVIS/MOSE from the same anchor, correlate disagreement with per-frame IoU error.
main_risk: Backward tracking may fail identically on the same hard segments, blinding the signal exactly where needed.

one_liner: Occlusion boundary ownership errors: SAM2 assigns the occluder's edge to the occluded object during partial occlusion.
problem: When object A passes in front of B, B's visible-region boundary is A's silhouette. Whether video segmenters represent this distinction (boundary ownership) is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: during partial occlusions, the tracker's boundary error on the shared edge is asymmetric - the occluded object's mask systematically 'sticks' to the occluder's silhouette even after separation begins (measurable hysteresis in boundary release), revealing absence of ownership representation.
why_important: Boundary ownership is the core of amodal reasoning; a measurable hysteresis gives a concrete probe for whether models have any occlusion model at all.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-release hysteresis as an amodal-representation probe is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate crossing events with GT, measure shared-edge error before/during/after separation, quantify release lag in frames.
main_risk: Requires accurate GT at occlusion boundaries, the noisiest annotation region.

one_liner: Micro-motion as a segmentation cue: can temporal aggregation segment objects invisible in any single frame (breathing, vibration)?
problem: Some objects are single-frame-invisible but reveal themselves through sub-pixel periodic motion. Current video segmenters aggregate over time yet nobody tests whether they exploit micro-motion.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2 and peers extract near-zero information from sub-pixel periodic motion (performance equals static-frame baseline), while an explicit temporal-amplification preprocessing (Eulerian-style) makes the same targets segmentable - locating a concrete representational gap between possible and actual temporal use.
why_important: Defines an entire class of targets (hidden animals, machinery defects, breathing patients under blankets) where temporal information is the ONLY signal.
why_possibly_novel: Micro-motion segmentation as a benchmark task is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search; motion magnification itself is KNOWN (Wu et al., Eulerian Video Magnification).
minimal_experiment: Collect/synthesize clips with sub-pixel oscillating targets, compare SAM2 vs SAM2-on-motion-amplified input.
main_risk: Amplification also amplifies noise; careful SNR-controlled synthesis needed.

one_liner: Once lost, always lost: quantify whether SAM2 failure is an absorbing state and what spontaneous recovery requires.
problem: Practitioners report that after a tracker loses its target, it rarely recovers without re-prompting, but recovery statistics have never been formalized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2's per-frame recovery probability after a loss event is <5% and roughly constant (memoryless), so expected lost-time is geometric and long - and recovery events are almost exclusively triggered by the object re-entering high-similarity poses to memory exemplars, not by search behavior (the model has no search).
why_important: Absorbing-state failure changes deployment math: the metric that matters is time-to-loss, not average IoU; also motivates re-detection modules with clear expected value.
why_possibly_novel: Survival-analysis treatment of masklet life/death/recovery is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run long videos (LVOS), detect loss events (IoU<0.1), fit survival and recovery hazard curves.
main_risk: Loss definition threshold shapes conclusions; report sensitivity across thresholds.

one_liner: Fit the memory-size vs drift power law: how much memory buys how much tracking longevity?
problem: Memory capacity is a compute knob without a published scaling relationship; teams size it by folklore.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: median time-to-loss scales as a power law in memory slots with exponent <1 (diminishing returns), and the exponent differs by scene type (crowded vs sparse), so optimal memory allocation is scene-conditional and mostly small.
why_important: Turns an arbitrary hyperparameter into a budgeted engineering decision with published curves.
why_possibly_novel: Scaling-law methodology applied to tracking memory rather than model/data size is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep memory configurations on LVOS/MOSE, fit time-to-loss curves per scene category.
main_risk: Architecture may not expose memory size cleanly without retraining; may need the open-source variants.

one_liner: Equal-budget video annotation: sparse clicks on many frames beats a perfect mask on one frame.
problem: The standard video annotation protocol (dense mask on frame 0, then propagate) has never been tested against spreading the same human-time across the video as sparse corrections.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched human-seconds, K single-click corrections spread over the video outperform one dense frame-0 mask by a growing margin with video length, because temporal information (where drift happens) is worth more than spatial precision (pixel-perfect anchor).
why_important: Could halve real-world video annotation cost with zero model changes - protocol science rather than architecture.
why_possibly_novel: Budget-matched protocol comparisons for video annotation are rare; UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Simulate both protocols with timed human cost models on DAVIS/LVOS + SAM2, then a small real-annotator study (5 people).
main_risk: Human time models for clicks vs masks vary; the real-annotator confirmation is essential.

one_liner: Ultrasound video breaks SAM2's memory attention because speckle decorrelates: modality-specific drift signature.
problem: SAM2 memory matches features across frames. Ultrasound speckle decorrelates within milliseconds while anatomy persists - the opposite statistics of natural video.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2 drift on ultrasound cine is dominated by speckle decorrelation (drift correlates with speckle decorrelation rate, not anatomical motion), so mild despeckling preprocessing improves tracking MORE than fine-tuning the model on ultrasound masks at matched effort.
why_important: Ultrasound is the highest-volume medical video modality; identifying the true bottleneck (input statistics vs model weights) redirects adaptation effort.
why_possibly_novel: Attribution of medical-video tracking failure to speckle statistics vs anatomy is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On CAMUS/echo videos, correlate frame-pair feature similarity with speckle decorrelation; compare despeckled input vs LoRA-tuned model at matched cost.
main_risk: Despeckling may destroy diagnostic boundaries; need boundary-quality co-evaluation.

one_liner: Self-diagnosing drift onset: within-track feature statistics detect the exact frame where a masklet starts failing.
problem: Drift detection currently needs ground truth or human review. The track's own feature stream (memory attention entropy, mask-embedding velocity) may mark failure onset.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a change-point detector on the masklet's internal statistics localizes drift onset within +-5 frames for a majority of failures, without images or GT - failure has an internal signature preceding visible error.
why_important: Automatic QA for large-scale video auto-annotation (SA-V style) - review only flagged spans instead of whole videos.
why_possibly_novel: Change-point analysis on tracker internals as self-diagnosis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Log internal statistics over DAVIS/MOSE runs, train change-point detector, evaluate onset localization against GT-derived failure times.
main_risk: Gradual drifts may lack a change point; report by failure type.

one_liner: Shot-change as a natural memory-reset probe: what SAM2 retains across cuts tells us what its memory encodes.
problem: Across a hard cut, low-level correspondence dies but object identity may persist (same object, new view). SAM2 behavior at cuts is an untested window into memory content.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM2 survival across cuts is predicted almost entirely by pose/scale similarity of the object across the cut and not by scene continuity, showing memory encodes object-centric appearance templates rather than scene context.
why_important: Edited video (film, broadcast, social media) is most of watched video; cut robustness defines applicability, and the probe clarifies representation content.
why_possibly_novel: Using editing structure as a controlled representational probe is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble cut pairs with graded object-pose and scene changes (from multi-view datasets), measure survival rates per condition.
main_risk: SAM2 may fail at essentially all cuts, flattening the analysis (still a clean negative result).

one_liner: Sub-frame mask interpolation: do memory features support generating masks BETWEEN frames (temporal super-resolution)?
problem: Applications need masks at higher temporal rates than compute allows (or between saved keyframes). Whether tracker features interpolate linearly in time is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: interpolating SAM2 memory/mask embeddings between frames yields valid intermediate masks whose error grows sub-linearly with gap size for smooth motion - i.e. the learned representation is approximately temporally linear, enabling 4-10x cheaper video segmentation via keyframing + latent interpolation.
why_important: Direct compute savings for video pipelines and a fundamental finding about temporal geometry of the learned space.
why_possibly_novel: Latent temporal interpolation for masklets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On high-fps videos, decode masks from interpolated embeddings at held-out timestamps, compare vs true frames and vs mask-space (pixel) interpolation baselines.
main_risk: Embedding space may be far from linear; pixel-space interpolation might trivially win.

one_liner: Background persistence pollution: in fixed-camera streams, background objects entering memory create recurring false positives.
problem: Surveillance-style fixed cameras repeatedly show the same background structures; if any frame's mask leaks onto background, memory can immortalize the leak.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in fixed-camera long streams, false-positive persistence (same wrong region recurring across frames) accounts for the majority of accumulated error - unlike moving-camera video where errors are transient - implying stationarity is a distinct and unmodeled failure regime for memory trackers.
why_important: Fixed cameras dominate real deployments (traffic, retail, wildlife, factory QA) yet benchmarks are handheld/moving; a regime-specific error structure would show benchmarks mis-sample reality.
why_possibly_novel: Error-recurrence analysis conditioned on camera stationarity is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run SAM2 on fixed-camera datasets (VIRAT-like), measure spatial autocorrelation of errors over time vs handheld controls.
main_risk: Fixed-camera GT for masks is scarce; may need semi-automatic GT with heavy review.

one_liner: Train on rater-disagreement-preserving labels instead of consensus: does keeping disagreement improve calibration more than it costs accuracy?
problem: Medical segmentation datasets collapse multiple expert opinions into one consensus mask, discarding the disagreement structure that encodes true ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models trained on the full rater distribution (sampling raters per example, not averaging) produce uncertainty maps that match held-out expert disagreement far better than consensus-trained models with post-hoc uncertainty, at <2 Dice cost - the disagreement is learnable signal, not noise.
why_important: Clinical decisions need to know WHERE experts would disagree; consensus training makes models confidently arbitrary exactly there.
why_possibly_novel: Multi-rater modeling exists (KNOWN: probabilistic U-Net line of work); the specific calibration-vs-Dice tradeoff quantification against held-out raters across modalities is less established. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: LIDC-IDRI (4 raters): train consensus vs rater-sampling models, evaluate uncertainty against held-out rater disagreement maps.
main_risk: Rater identity confounds (systematic rater styles) may dominate genuine case ambiguity.

one_liner: CT models secretly depend on window/level preprocessing conventions: randomized windowing collapses them, revealing intensity brittleness.
problem: CT pipelines bake in windowing presets (e.g. soft-tissue window). Models may learn the preset, not the anatomy, making them fragile to any acquisition/preprocessing change.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: state-of-the-art CT segmenters lose disproportionate Dice under clinically-plausible window/level perturbations (which preserve all diagnostic information a radiologist needs), and a model trained window-agnostic recovers the gap with no in-distribution cost - proving the fragility is a preprocessing artifact, not a capacity limit.
why_important: Windowing varies across hospitals and PACS exports; this is a silent, ubiquitous deployment shift nobody benchmarks.
why_possibly_novel: Windowing as a formal domain-shift axis with an information-preservation argument is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take 3 public CT models, sweep window/level within radiologically-valid ranges, plot degradation; retrain one with randomized windows.
main_risk: Some windows genuinely destroy information for specific organs; must define validity ranges with a radiologist.

one_liner: Slice-direction inconsistency of 2D models on 3D volumes scales with through-plane anisotropy: derive the consistency-spacing law.
problem: 2D slice-wise segmentation (including SAM-based) produces jagged 3D shapes. How inconsistency scales with slice spacing/anisotropy has not been formalized, so nobody knows when 2D is 'good enough'.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: inter-slice mask inconsistency grows linearly with slice spacing up to an organ-dependent correlation length, beyond which 2D and 3D models converge in quality - giving a per-organ spacing threshold that predicts when 3D context stops helping.
why_important: Answers the perpetual 2D-vs-3D question with a measurable law instead of anecdote, guiding architecture choice per dataset.
why_possibly_novel: An explicit anatomical correlation-length framing of the 2D/3D tradeoff is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Downsample isotropic CT volumes to various spacings, train/evaluate matched 2D and 3D models, fit the crossover per organ.
main_risk: Confounded by training-data volume differences between 2D slices and 3D patches; must match supervision bits.

one_liner: MedSAM-style box prompting leaks organ-size priors: models segment the expected organ size, failing on pathological sizes.
problem: Box prompts encode expected extents. Medical models fine-tuned with GT boxes may learn organ-size priors that break precisely on the abnormal cases that matter clinically (atrophy, hypertrophy, tumors).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: MedSAM-style models' error grows sharply with an organ's deviation from population-median size (controlling for boundary difficulty), and prompting with deliberately wrong-size boxes drags predictions toward the box size - demonstrating prior leakage that inflates benchmark scores on normal anatomy while hiding failure on pathology.
why_important: Clinical value concentrates in abnormal cases; a size prior is exactly the wrong inductive bias, and current benchmarks (mostly normal-ish anatomy) cannot see it.
why_possibly_novel: Size-deviation-stratified evaluation of promptable medical models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Stratify public organ datasets by size percentile, plot Dice vs deviation; run wrong-box perturbation response curves.
main_risk: Extreme sizes correlate with genuinely harder boundaries; needs matched-difficulty controls.

one_liner: Is ultrasound speckle noise or signal? Despeckling ablation to test whether models use speckle texture as anatomical cue.
problem: Speckle is treated as noise to be removed, but speckle statistics are tissue-dependent - models may rely on it as discriminative texture, in which case despeckling harms segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: segmentation models trained on raw ultrasound lose significant accuracy when tested on despeckled inputs (and vice versa), and per-tissue analysis shows speckle statistics carry class information comparable to boundary information for homogeneous organs - speckle is signal.
why_important: Resolves a preprocessing controversy with direct consequences for every ultrasound pipeline and for cross-device generalization (speckle is device-dependent).
why_possibly_novel: Information-content quantification of speckle for segmentation (not detection/denoising) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train/test 2x2 (raw/despeckled) on CAMUS + thyroid datasets; add a texture-only probe (boundary-masked patches) for class information.
main_risk: Results may be despeckling-algorithm dependent; use 3 different filters.

one_liner: Stain normalization in pathology helps less than stain-diverse training: an assumption audit with controlled compute.
problem: Stain normalization is near-universal in computational pathology, assumed necessary for cross-lab transfer. Modern augmentation/diverse pretraining may have made it redundant or harmful.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched compute, stain augmentation dominates stain normalization for cross-site segmentation transfer, and normalization actively destroys discriminative chromatic information for some tissue classes (measurable per-class sign flips).
why_important: Normalization is a preprocessing tax on every pathology pipeline; if it is obsolete or harmful, the field should know. KNOWN: augmentation-vs-normalization comparisons exist in classification contexts; segmentation-specific and per-class sign analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
why_possibly_novel: Per-class harm analysis of normalization for segmentation, rather than aggregate AUC comparisons.
minimal_experiment: CAMELYON-derived segmentation with multi-site splits: 2x2 normalization/augmentation factorial at matched budgets.
main_risk: Conclusions may not transfer across stain types (H&E vs IHC); scope both.

one_liner: Text-report-derived weak labels vs 5 minutes of scribbles: the annotation-economics showdown for medical segmentation.
problem: Two weak-supervision currencies compete - mining radiology reports (free but noisy/indirect) vs minimal expert scribbles (costly but spatial). Their exchange rate has never been measured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per unit of final Dice, expert scribble-seconds outperform report-derived labels by an order of magnitude for spatially-precise structures, but report labels win for presence/coverage of diffuse pathology - the modality of weak supervision must match the spatial statistics of the target.
why_important: Hospitals sit on millions of reports; knowing when they are worth mining vs when to just pay for scribbles is a real resource-allocation question.
why_possibly_novel: A quantified exchange rate between supervision types under matched outcomes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On a chest CT dataset with reports, train (a) report-mined weak labels, (b) budget-matched scribbles, (c) mixtures; compare Dice-per-dollar curves.
main_risk: Report-mining quality depends heavily on NLP extraction quality, a moving target.

one_liner: Tumor boundary uncertainty is directionally structured (infiltration axes); isotropic uncertainty models are wrong in a measurable way.
problem: Infiltrative tumors grow along anatomical corridors (white-matter tracts, tissue planes), so true boundary ambiguity is anisotropic - but every uncertainty method outputs isotropic per-pixel variance.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: held-out multi-rater disagreement on glioma boundaries is significantly anisotropic (aligned with local tissue orientation), and current uncertainty methods' outputs are near-isotropic - a representational mismatch that directional evaluation will expose and that matters for radiotherapy margins.
why_important: Radiotherapy margin expansion is currently isotropic partly because tools are; demonstrating structured anisotropy could change margin design.
why_possibly_novel: Directional decomposition of segmentation uncertainty against anatomical orientation fields is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: BraTS-style multi-rater subset + DTI atlas orientations: measure disagreement anisotropy; compare uncertainty-method outputs directionally.
main_risk: Multi-rater glioma data with enough raters is scarce; may need to commission a small re-annotation.

one_liner: Longitudinal self-supervision: same-patient scan pairs give free consistency labels that beat generic pretraining for segmentation.
problem: Hospitals have massive longitudinal archives (same patient, months apart) that are unused for pretraining; stable anatomy between visits is a free correspondence signal stronger than augmentation-based SSL.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: pretraining with cross-visit anatomical correspondence objectives (predicting stable vs changed regions without registration GT) transfers to downstream segmentation better than in-modality SimCLR/MAE at matched data and compute, especially for small-structure Dice.
why_important: Uses data hospitals already have with zero extra annotation; targets the medical-specific structure (longitudinal stability) generic SSL ignores.
why_possibly_novel: Longitudinal-pair pretraining for dense medical tasks appears under-explored. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble public longitudinal MRI (ADNI/OASIS), pretrain correspondence vs MAE at matched compute, fine-tune on hippocampus/lesion segmentation.
main_risk: Registration shortcuts could let the model cheat; objective design must prevent trivial solutions.

one_liner: Partial-label multi-dataset training silently teaches 'organ X is background': quantify negative-transfer from unlabeled structures.
problem: Combining datasets where each labels different organs means every dataset actively teaches that other organs are background - a contradiction that everyone works around ad hoc.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: naive multi-dataset training suppresses each organ's recall proportionally to how often it appears unlabeled in partner datasets (a measurable dose-response 'background poisoning' curve), and the effect size exceeds architecture-choice effects in typical setups.
why_important: Multi-dataset training is how everyone scales medical models now; an unmeasured poisoning law means the ecosystem's scaling curves are bent by label sociology, not learning capacity.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: partial-label learning methods exist (e.g. marginal losses); the quantified dose-response poisoning law is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Controlled mixes of 3 abdominal datasets with disjoint labels; vary the fraction of poisoning images per organ, fit recall vs poisoning-dose.
main_risk: Effect confounds with dataset appearance shift; use single-source synthetic label-hiding as the clean control.

one_liner: Vessel and airway models optimize Dice but break topology: measure the Dice-topology Pareto frontier and show current models sit at its wrong end.
problem: For tubular structures, a 1-voxel break destroys downstream use (flow simulation, navigation) while barely moving Dice; the field optimizes and reports the wrong quantity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: across public vessel/airway models, topology error (Betti number mismatch, broken-branch count) is nearly uncorrelated with Dice above Dice=0.8, and models selected by validation Dice are strictly dominated on the topology axis by differently-selected checkpoints of the SAME training run - the problem is checkpoint selection, not capacity.
why_important: If correct, large topology gains are available for free (different model selection), and benchmark rankings for tubular tasks are misleading.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: clDice and topology losses exist; the checkpoint-selection reframing (topology is lost at selection time, not training time) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Retrain a standard vessel model, log Dice and topology metrics for ALL checkpoints, test whether topology-selected checkpoints dominate.
main_risk: May be true only near convergence for specific architectures; test 3 architectures.

one_liner: Find the through-plane spacing threshold where 3D convolution stops beating 2D - a reusable crossover law for the field.
problem: Whether to use 2D, 2.5D, or 3D models is re-litigated in every medical paper without a governing quantitative rule.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the 3D-over-2D Dice advantage decays monotonically with slice spacing normalized by structure diameter, crossing zero near spacing~0.5x structure diameter, consistently across organs and modalities - a dimensionless law that predicts the right architecture from dataset metadata alone.
why_important: Would eliminate a whole genre of redundant ablation studies and guide architecture choice from acquisition parameters.
why_possibly_novel: Dimensionless scaling analysis (spacing/diameter) for the 2D-3D question is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Resample 5 isotropic datasets to a spacing grid, train matched 2D/3D models, fit the crossover in dimensionless units.
main_risk: Anisotropic acquisition artifacts (slice profile, gap) differ from clean downsampling; validate on natively anisotropic data.

one_liner: Annotation fatigue leaves order signatures in public medical datasets: label quality drifts within annotation sessions and is detectable post hoc.
problem: Medical labels are made by humans in long sessions; fatigue and drift should leave statistical traces (boundary quality vs slice index / case order), but no one audits datasets for it.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in public volumetric datasets, boundary smoothness and model-vs-label disagreement vary systematically with slice order within volumes (start vs end of stacks) and with case ID order, revealing session-position effects large enough to bias per-region evaluation (e.g. organ ends are labeled worse).
why_important: If label quality is spatially/temporally structured, benchmark errors attributed to models are partly annotation fatigue - affecting especially the apex/base slices clinicians care about.
why_possibly_novel: Forensic fatigue analysis of existing datasets (no new labels needed) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For 5 public datasets, regress label-quality proxies (curvature statistics, inter-slice coherence, model consensus disagreement) on slice position and case order.
main_risk: Proxies for 'label quality' without re-annotation are indirect; commission spot re-annotations for validation.

one_liner: Low-level statistics distance (power spectrum, noise model) predicts MedSAM transfer failure better than semantic/anatomical distance.
problem: Foundation medical models fail unpredictably on new modalities/protocols. The community assumes semantic novelty drives failure; it may be mundane signal statistics.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: transfer performance of promptable medical models across 20+ dataset pairs is predicted (r>0.7) by low-level statistics divergence (radially-averaged power spectra, noise floor, intensity histogram transport cost) and only weakly by anatomy/modality labels - most 'domain gap' is signal-processing gap.
why_important: A cheap pre-deployment compatibility test from unlabeled images, plus redirection of adaptation research toward signal harmonization.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic low-level-vs-semantic attribution of medical transfer failure is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate MedSAM/SAM across the modality grid of public datasets, regress performance drops on statistics divergences vs semantic dummies.
main_risk: Low-level and semantic distances correlate across natural dataset pairs; needs synthetic-perturbation legs to break the confound.

one_liner: Clinician clicks differ from simulated clicks: measure the sim2real prompting gap that inflates interactive medical benchmarks.
problem: Interactive medical segmentation is evaluated with simulated prompts (center-of-error clicks). Real clinicians click based on anatomical salience and diagnostic habit, not error geometry.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: real clinician click distributions differ measurably from simulators (clicks favor anatomically meaningful landmarks and avoid ambiguous tissue), and evaluating with real click traces drops reported model performance by a clinically meaningful margin, reordering methods - simulator choice is a hidden hyperparameter of the entire subfield.
why_important: If benchmark rankings do not survive real users, the field is optimizing simulator-fit; protocols must change before clinical deployment claims.
why_possibly_novel: Collected clinician-click corpora for evaluation replay are rare/absent. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Record 3 clinicians x 100 cases of real interactive use, replay traces against 4 models, compare with simulator-based rankings.
main_risk: Small-N clinician study; click styles may vary more between clinicians than between simulators (itself a finding).

one_liner: Contrast-polarity invariance test: can one model segment T1 and T2 (inverted tissue contrast) without contrast-specific features, and what does it cost?
problem: MRI sequences flip which tissue is bright. Models either specialize per sequence or are claimed 'sequence-agnostic' without a controlled test of what invariance costs.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: enforcing polarity invariance (training with random contrast inversions consistent with tissue physics) costs little on seen sequences but roughly doubles zero-shot transfer to unseen sequences - i.e. most cross-sequence failure is polarity/contrast coding, a low-dimensional and fixable factor, not anatomy understanding.
why_important: Sequence proliferation is the main practical obstacle to universal MRI models; identifying the failure as low-dimensional makes it tractable.
why_possibly_novel: Physics-consistent contrast-inversion invariance analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train on T1 with physics-based contrast remapping augmentation, test zero-shot on T2/FLAIR; compare against multi-sequence-trained upper bound.
main_risk: Some pathologies are only visible in specific sequences; invariance may erase pathology signal - stratify by lesion visibility.

one_liner: Below a lesion-size threshold, segmentation-first pipelines beat detection-first: locate the crossover.
problem: Tiny lesion pipelines either detect-then-segment or segment-then-group. Which paradigm wins at which size regime is undocumented, so teams choose by habit.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-lesion recall of detection-first pipelines collapses below a size threshold (relative to receptive-field stride) where dense segmentation-first retains sensitivity, producing a crossover point measurable in voxels that generalizes across modalities when normalized by resolution.
why_important: Metastasis screening and microbleed detection live exactly in the tiny regime; the field needs the regime map.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head paradigm comparison stratified by object size in physical units is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On microbleed/metastasis datasets, run matched detection-first and segmentation-first pipelines, plot per-lesion recall vs size.
main_risk: Implementation quality asymmetry between paradigms could masquerade as a paradigm effect; use strong tuned baselines for both.

one_liner: Extreme class imbalance has a phase transition: below a foreground-fraction threshold, per-lesion recall decouples from Dice and both metrics stop constraining each other.
problem: At foreground fractions below ~0.1%, standard metrics and training dynamics enter a regime the field treats with the same tools as moderate imbalance; whether this regime is qualitatively different is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: as foreground fraction decreases, there is a measurable transition where (a) the correlation between Dice and per-lesion recall across checkpoints drops toward zero, and (b) training becomes bimodal (models either find lesions or ignore them entirely, seed-dependent) - a phase structure implying different evaluation and early-stopping rules are needed in the extreme regime.
why_important: Screening applications live in the extreme regime; if metric decoupling and seed-bimodality are real, current papers' single-seed Dice claims there are close to meaningless.
why_possibly_novel: Phase-transition framing with checkpoint-level correlation analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Synthetic imbalance ladder (subsample lesion voxels progressively), train 10 seeds per level, measure metric decoupling and outcome bimodality.
main_risk: Transition may be gradual, not sharp - report as regime change rather than critical point if so.

one_liner: Simulate cross-vendor MRI shift from k-space physics and test how much of the real vendor gap physics-only augmentation closes.
problem: Cross-vendor generalization is attacked with generic augmentation or adaptation, but vendor differences are substantially physics (k-space filtering, coil combination, reconstruction) that can be forward-simulated.
