core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: augmenting a single-vendor training set with physics-simulated vendor transforms closes >60% of the measured cross-vendor Dice gap, and the residual gap localizes to protocol (not reconstruction) differences - decomposing 'vendor shift' into simulable and non-simulable parts.
why_important: Would replace data-hungry multi-vendor collection with physics simulation for a large fraction of the problem, and produce the first quantitative decomposition of vendor shift.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: MRI physics augmentation exists in reconstruction literature; the segmentation-gap decomposition claim is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use multi-vendor brain datasets, implement k-space filter/noise/bias-field simulation, measure gap closure per component.
main_risk: Faithful vendor simulation requires proprietary details; approximate simulation may cap the closure fraction for reasons unrelated to the hypothesis.

one_liner: Probe-pressure deformation is the dominant unmodeled augmentation for ultrasound: geometric, physics-parameterized, and testable.
problem: Ultrasound anatomy deforms under operator probe pressure. No standard augmentation models this; models may fail across operators simply due to compression states.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a biomechanically-plausible compression augmentation (depth-dependent anisotropic strain) improves cross-operator segmentation transfer more than any standard photometric/geometric augmentation at matched strength, because compression is the leading axis of real operator variation.
why_important: Operator dependence is ultrasound's defining weakness; naming and modeling its main geometric factor would be broadly reusable.
why_possibly_novel: Compression-specific augmentation validated on cross-operator splits is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Datasets with repeated sweeps by different operators (or phantom studies): augmentation ablation over cross-operator splits.
main_risk: Cross-operator datasets are scarce; a phantom + small clinical validation may be the only path.

one_liner: Benchmarks reporting Dice above the inter-rater ceiling are fitting annotator style: audit which medical leaderboards have crossed their own noise floor.
problem: Each dataset has a Dice ceiling given by expert-vs-expert agreement. Leaderboard scores near or above single-rater agreement indicate style overfitting, not superhuman accuracy - but ceilings are rarely computed or compared.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: several prominent medical segmentation leaderboards have SOTA scores within noise of (or above) the inter-rater ceiling for their structure types, and the models' residual 'errors' correlate with rater-style dimensions rather than anatomy - meaning further leaderboard progress there is epistemically empty.
why_important: Redirects effort away from saturated benchmarks and toward datasets/metrics with real headroom; protects clinical claims from style-fitting artifacts.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-benchmark systematic ceiling audit is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (individual inter-rater studies are KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Collect published inter-rater figures per structure, compare with leaderboard SOTA; for 2 datasets, commission small re-rating to measure style-vs-anatomy error decomposition.
main_risk: Published inter-rater numbers use varying protocols; harmonization needed before comparison.

one_liner: Anatomy-relative coordinates transfer prompts across patients: one expert prompt reused on a thousand scans.
problem: Promptable models need per-image prompts. In medical imaging, anatomy provides a shared coordinate system that could let one prompt (defined relative to landmarks) transfer across patients - turning interactive into automatic segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: prompts expressed in anatomy-normalized coordinates (via cheap landmark detection, no deformable registration) retain >90% of per-patient manual-prompt Dice on organs with stable topology, and the transfer failure cases are exactly the clinically abnormal anatomies - making prompt-transfer failure itself an anomaly detector.
why_important: Amortizes expert interaction across cohorts (huge for population studies), and the failure-as-anomaly-signal is a free second product.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt-space anatomical normalization (rather than image registration) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Abdominal CT cohort: define prompts on 5 template patients, transfer via landmark alignment, measure retained Dice and abnormality enrichment among failures.
main_risk: Landmark detectors fail on the same abnormal cases, entangling the anomaly signal.

one_liner: Site fingerprints in federated medical segmentation: features encode hospital identity, and removing it costs accuracy - measure the privacy-performance coupling.
problem: Features of medical segmentation models may encode acquisition-site identity (scanner, protocol), which is simultaneously a privacy leak, a shortcut-learning risk, and possibly useful signal. The three roles have not been jointly quantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: site identity is linearly decodable from mid-level features of standard models with high accuracy; enforcing site-invariance degrades in-site accuracy only marginally but improves cross-site transfer - i.e. the site code is mostly shortcut, not signal, and its removal is nearly free.
why_important: Directly informs federated learning design and shortcut mitigation in the setting where regulatory stakes are highest.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: site effects in radiomics are documented; the joint decodability-invariance-transfer quantification for segmentation features is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-site public data (e.g. multi-site prostate MRI): site probes on features, invariance-constrained retraining, transfer matrix comparison.
main_risk: Site correlates with population case-mix; invariance may remove genuine epidemiological signal - needs case-mix controls.

one_liner: Volume measurements inherit uncalibrated uncertainty from segmentation: are downstream tumor-volume confidence intervals valid even when masks look good?
problem: Clinical endpoints are derived quantities (volumes, diameters), yet uncertainty is evaluated at pixel level. Pixel-calibrated models can still yield badly mis-calibrated volume estimates because errors are spatially correlated.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: volume confidence intervals derived from per-pixel uncertainties are anti-conservative by large factors (2-5x too narrow) because pixel errors are positively correlated along boundaries, and a boundary-correlation-aware propagation restores near-nominal coverage without changing the model.
why_important: RECIST-style measurements drive treatment decisions; invalid CIs are a direct clinical safety issue that pixel metrics cannot reveal.
why_possibly_novel: Coverage analysis of derived clinical quantities from segmentation uncertainty is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-rater lesion datasets: compare nominal vs empirical coverage of volume CIs across uncertainty methods; measure boundary error correlation lengths.
main_risk: Multi-rater 'true volume' is itself uncertain; use synthetic lesions with exact GT as the anchor condition.

one_liner: Consensus fusion (STAPLE-style) systematically erases minority-expert detections that are disproportionately correct on rare pathologies.
problem: Multi-rater fusion assumes the majority is right. For rare or subtle findings, the specialist minority may carry the correct signal, and consensus training deletes it.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on cases with confirmed outcomes (pathology/follow-up), regions flagged by exactly one expert (majority-rejected) contain true findings at a rate far above chance and concentrated in rare disease subtypes - so consensus-trained models are structurally biased against the rare cases that matter most, in a measurable, outcome-anchored way.
why_important: Challenges the default label-fusion practice for the exact case class (rare, subtle) where AI assistance is most valuable.
why_possibly_novel: Outcome-anchored audit of minority-rater regions is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Dataset with rater annotations + outcome verification (e.g. screening cohorts with follow-up): measure precision of minority-only regions vs chance.
main_risk: Outcome-linked multi-rater datasets are rare and access-restricted; may require collaboration for data.

one_liner: Smoke has no true binary boundary: model rankings on smoke benchmarks flip when evaluated against density (alpha) labels instead of binary masks.
problem: Smoke segmentation benchmarks use binary masks over a physically continuous density field; annotator thresholds are arbitrary, so benchmarks may rank annotator-style-matching, not smoke understanding.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: inter-annotator agreement on smoke binary masks is lower than model-model agreement (benchmarks measure style), and re-evaluating existing models against soft density references (from synthetic smoke composites with known alpha) produces materially different rankings.
why_important: If rankings are unstable under label formulation, published progress in smoke segmentation is partly an artifact - and safety systems are being selected on the wrong criterion.
why_possibly_novel: Density-referenced re-evaluation of binary smoke benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Composite real smoke plumes (alpha known from studio capture or simulation) onto scenes; evaluate public smoke models against binary vs alpha references; run a 5-annotator agreement study on 100 frames.
main_risk: Synthetic composites may not represent real smoke edge statistics; include a small real multi-annotator set.

one_liner: Reformulate smoke segmentation as alpha-matte regression: binary masks impose a measurable performance ceiling.
problem: Binary segmentation of translucent media discards the concentration information that downstream users (fire response, emissions monitoring) actually need.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a density-regression formulation trained on composited data with true alpha outperforms binary-mask models even when both are evaluated on the binary task (thresholded density beats direct binary prediction), because the continuous target regularizes the ill-posed boundary - falsifiable by direct comparison.
why_important: Would show binary supervision is not just lossy for users but actively harmful for learning on translucent classes.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: matting exists as a field; the claim that regression supervision dominates binary supervision ON the binary metric for smoke is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train matched models (same backbone/budget) with binary vs alpha supervision on composited smoke, evaluate both on binary IoU + downstream density error.
main_risk: Compositing realism gap; validate on held-out real annotated smoke.

one_liner: Fire segmentation models exploit sensor blooming and saturation artifacts, so they collapse across cameras: quantify the artifact reliance.
problem: Fire is a light emitter that saturates sensors, causing blooming/streaks that are camera-specific. Models may key on these artifacts rather than fire appearance, predicting cross-camera fragility.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: masking saturated pixels and blooming halos at test time degrades fire-segmentation models far more than masking equal-area random regions, and cross-camera transfer loss correlates with inter-camera differences in saturation behavior - most 'fire recognition' is sensor-artifact recognition.
why_important: Fire detection is deployed across wildly heterogeneous cameras; artifact reliance would explain field failures that benchmarks never show.
why_possibly_novel: Artifact-reliance decomposition for emissive phenomena is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Occlusion-based attribution on saturation regions across 3 fire datasets; cross-camera evaluation where saturation statistics are matched vs mismatched.
main_risk: Saturation is also genuine signal (fires do saturate); the question is reliance degree - needs careful counterfactuals with HDR captures.

one_liner: Fire flicker has a characteristic temporal frequency signature: a 1-second temporal window beats any single-frame architecture at matched compute.
problem: Flame combustion produces documented flicker (~1-15 Hz region, KNOWN from combustion literature). Whether video fire segmentation actually needs or uses this cue is untested against strong single-frame baselines.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: adding a short temporal window with explicit frequency-band features improves fire/no-fire pixel discrimination against hard negatives (sunsets, reflective orange surfaces, foliage in wind) more than scaling the single-frame model by the equivalent compute - temporal spectrum is the discriminative axis, not appearance.
why_important: Hard negatives are the practical fire-alarm problem (false positives); a physically-grounded cue that separates them is directly deployable.
why_possibly_novel: Frequency-domain evaluation against curated hard negatives at matched compute is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble hard-negative video set (sunsets, brake lights, reflections), compare single-frame vs temporal-spectral models at matched FLOPs.
main_risk: Camera compression may destroy flicker at typical bitrates - itself an important deployment finding.

one_liner: Smoke-vs-cloud/fog discrimination is context-borne, not appearance-borne: source-region occlusion collapses model accuracy.
problem: Smoke, cloud, and fog patches can be locally indistinguishable; humans disambiguate by source attribution (rising from a point) and context. What information models actually use is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: occluding the plume's source region (bottom of plume, fire location) reduces smoke-vs-cloud discrimination accuracy to near chance for current models, showing classification is source-context-based, while texture-only patches carry <20% of the decision information - a measurable information decomposition.
why_important: Determines minimum viable input context for wildfire early-warning crops/tiles - a deployed-system design constraint derived from science.
why_possibly_novel: Context-vs-texture information decomposition for atmospheric classes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Patch-occlusion and crop-size sweeps on smoke/cloud datasets; report accuracy vs available context radius.
main_risk: Dataset biases (smoke images differ from cloud images in irrelevant ways) can inflate texture-only accuracy; control with matched-scene pairs.

one_liner: Optical-flow divergence detects smoke before appearance does: advection physics as a detection signal for incipient smoke.
problem: Early smoke is nearly transparent - appearance models fail at exactly the high-value moment. But smoke's motion field (expanding, buoyant, divergent) differs from scene motion from the very first frames.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: divergence/curl statistics of dense optical flow in smoke regions differ measurably from all common scene motions (foliage, water, crowds) even at contrast levels where appearance models are at chance, moving time-to-detection earlier by a measurable margin on ignition videos.
why_important: Time-to-detection is THE metric for wildfire monitoring; a physics-grounded earliness gain matters more than IoU gains.
why_possibly_novel: Flow-topology (divergence) statistics as an early smoke feature, evaluated on time-to-detect, is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On ignition-time videos (controlled burns), plot detection latency of flow-based vs appearance-based signals at matched false-positive rates.
main_risk: Optical flow is noisy exactly at low contrast; may need long temporal integration that erodes the earliness advantage.

one_liner: Measure the annotator alpha-threshold distribution: at what transparency do humans stop labeling smoke, and how much benchmark variance does it explain?
problem: Every smoke/fog annotation implicitly chooses a transparency cutoff. The distribution of these cutoffs across annotators and datasets has never been measured, though it defines what the labels mean.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: annotator alpha cutoffs vary widely (roughly 2x range in implied alpha) across individuals and datasets, and this single scalar explains the majority of inter-dataset label inconsistency for translucent classes - cutting cross-dataset training gains when unharmonized.
why_important: Provides the missing calibration constant for merging translucent-class datasets, and a general method for auditing implicit label thresholds.
why_possibly_novel: Psychophysical measurement of implicit annotation thresholds is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Show annotators composited smoke with known alpha ramps, elicit boundaries, estimate individual cutoffs; compare dataset-level implied cutoffs via composite probes.
main_risk: Cutoffs may be context-dependent (background luminance), making the scalar model too simple - the richer model is still measurable.

one_liner: Synthetic-fog robustness does not transfer to real fog because real fog is heterogeneous: quantify the homogeneity gap.
problem: Fog robustness is benchmarked with homogeneous Koschmieder-model synthetic fog (KNOWN: standard in robustness suites). Real fog has patchiness, depth-correlated density, and scattering halos.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models hardened on homogeneous synthetic fog gain little or nothing on real fog scenes (transfer coefficient <30%), and the residual failure correlates with fog spatial heterogeneity statistics - synthetic-fog benchmarks systematically overstate robustness progress.
why_important: Autonomous-driving robustness claims rest partly on synthetic corruption suites; a measured transfer coefficient recalibrates those claims.
why_possibly_novel: Direct synthetic-to-real fog transfer measurement for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train/harden on synthetic fog ladders, evaluate on real foggy datasets (ACDC fog split), regress residual error on measured heterogeneity indices.
main_risk: Real-fog GT is limited; heterogeneity indices from single images are approximate.

one_liner: Background luminance flips smoke difficulty: dark-smoke-on-sky vs light-smoke-on-ground asymmetry as an untested dataset bias.
problem: Smoke visibility depends on the sign of contrast with background (scattering vs shadowing regimes). Datasets may over-sample one regime, biasing models trained on them.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: public smoke datasets are dominated by positive-contrast configurations (bright smoke against dark ground or dark smoke against bright sky in fixed proportions), and model performance collapses on the under-represented contrast-sign regime - a bias measurable and correctable via regime-stratified evaluation.
why_important: Wildfire cameras see both regimes daily (sun angle changes); a hidden regime bias means diurnal reliability swings in deployment.
why_possibly_novel: Contrast-sign regime analysis for translucent classes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Auto-classify contrast regimes in 4 smoke datasets, report regime distributions and per-regime model performance.
main_risk: Regime auto-classification itself needs validation; start with manual labeling of a subset.

one_liner: Smoke shadows are systematically mislabeled as smoke in aerial datasets: an audit with atmospheric-geometry verification.
problem: From aerial/satellite view, dense smoke casts dark shadows displaced by sun angle; annotators plausibly include shadows in smoke masks. Nobody has audited for this confusion.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a geometrically verifiable fraction (sun-angle-consistent displacement) of 'smoke' pixels in public aerial smoke datasets are actually shadow, and models trained on them systematically over-segment in the shadow direction - a directional error signature reproducible from sun metadata.
why_important: Burned-area and plume-volume estimates feed emissions science; a shadow contamination bias propagates into climate-relevant numbers.
why_possibly_novel: Sun-geometry forensic auditing of smoke annotations is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For datasets with timestamps/geolocation, compute sun vectors, test whether label boundaries show sun-aligned asymmetry vs plume physics.
main_risk: Smoke and its shadow genuinely overlap when viewed off-nadir; geometry must handle view angle carefully.

one_liner: Rain streak and snowflake segmentation depends on exposure time, not weather intensity: the shutter-speed confound in weather datasets.
problem: The image of falling precipitation is determined jointly by physical rate and camera shutter speed (streak length ~ exposure). Datasets ignore shutter metadata, confounding weather severity with camera settings.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: model performance and even class definition ('rain streak' vs 'rain fog') vary more with exposure-time differences than with actual precipitation-rate differences at matched rates - weather segmentation datasets encode camera physics as much as meteorology.
why_important: Weather robustness claims should transfer across cameras; if not, deployed reliability varies with shutter policies (auto-exposure), a controllable but ignored factor.
why_possibly_novel: Exposure-time-controlled analysis of precipitation appearance in segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Capture matched scenes at multiple shutter speeds under controlled sprinkler 'rain'; test models across shutter conditions.
main_risk: Controlled precipitation capture is logistically heavy; simulation (streak rendering with exposure models) can substitute initially.

one_liner: Models segment reflections on water as if they were the reflected objects: quantify the reflection-confusion rate and its structure.
problem: Water surfaces mirror the scene; segmentation models may label reflected trees/people as real ones. The error rate and its dependence on water roughness is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on calm-water scenes, mainstream models assign real-object classes to reflection pixels at high rates, and the confusion rate drops sharply with surface ripple amplitude (a measurable psychometric-style curve) - revealing that reflection rejection is driven by high-frequency distortion cues, not scene reasoning.
why_important: Waterside deployment (drones, boats, flood monitoring) needs reflection rejection; knowing the operative cue tells us when it fails (calm dawn water = worst case).
why_possibly_novel: Ripple-amplitude-controlled reflection confusion curves are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate calm-to-rippled water scene ladder, measure per-class confusion into reflection regions across models.
main_risk: GT for 'reflection region' needs annotation, but polygon-level water masks make it tractable.

one_liner: Steam vs smoke as the minimal-pair discrimination task for translucent media: what cue actually separates them?
problem: Steam (condensed water) and smoke (combustion aerosol) look similar but have different dynamics, color temperature, and dissipation. Alarm systems must separate them; the discriminative cue set is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the separating information is temporal (dissipation rate, buoyancy profile) rather than static appearance - static-frame classifiers plateau near chance-plus-context, while short-clip models separate well; and the temporal advantage survives across cameras (unlike appearance cues).
why_important: False alarms from steam are a leading cause of fire-system distrust in kitchens/industry; a validated minimal cue set enables robust designs.
why_possibly_novel: Steam-smoke minimal-pair benchmark with cue ablation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect matched steam/smoke clips (kitchen + controlled sources), run static vs temporal models, ablate color/motion/context channels.
main_risk: Collection diversity (steam types vs smoke types) drives conclusions; needs deliberate source variety.

one_liner: Exposure bracketing beats model scaling for fire scenes: sensor dynamic range, not model capacity, is the current bottleneck.
problem: Fire scenes span extreme dynamic range (flame core to dark smoke); single-exposure images clip both ends. The community scales models on clipped data instead of asking whether the sensor is the binding constraint.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched total cost, adding exposure-bracketed/HDR input to a small model outperforms scaling a single-exposure model by 10x parameters on fire-region segmentation and near-fire structure delineation - the information is destroyed before the model, and no capacity recovers clipped photons.
why_important: Would redirect investment from model scale toward capture policy for safety-critical fire perception - a cheap, actionable systems conclusion.
why_possibly_novel: Sensor-vs-model marginal-value comparison for fire segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Capture bracketed fire footage (controlled burns), train matched models on single vs bracketed inputs, compare against a parameter-scaling ladder.
main_risk: HDR capture is unavailable on legacy deployed cameras, limiting immediate applicability (but informing procurement).

one_liner: Time-to-detect as the primary smoke metric: temporal-accumulation detectors dominate spatial models in the sub-visible regime.
problem: Smoke benchmarks report IoU on established plumes; the deployment task is detecting the transition from nothing to barely-something, which is a change-detection problem, not a segmentation problem.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on ignition sequences, simple long-horizon temporal accumulation (background modeling over minutes) detects smoke minutes earlier than frame-wise segmentation models at equal false-alarm rates - the field is optimizing the wrong problem formulation for the highest-value use case.
why_important: Minutes of earliness in wildfire detection have enormous real value; showing the formulation (not the model) is wrong would redirect the subfield.
why_possibly_novel: Ignition-anchored time-to-detect benchmarking of segmentation models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble ignition-timestamped fixed-camera videos (controlled burns, tower cameras), compare detection-latency ROC of accumulation vs segmentation approaches.
main_risk: Fixed-camera assumption; moving-camera earliness is a different, harder problem.

one_liner: IoU is the wrong loss surface for amorphous regions: measure human-judgment vs IoU ranking disagreement on smoke/fog masks.
problem: For amorphous media, many different masks are equally 'right'. Whether IoU-style metrics agree with expert human quality judgments on such classes has not been tested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for smoke/fog masks, human expert pairwise preferences disagree with IoU-based rankings on a large fraction of comparisons (>30%), and the disagreement is systematic (humans forgive boundary variation but punish topology/coverage errors) - implying a validated perceptual metric would reorder the field's results.
why_important: Metric validity precedes all benchmarking; a documented human-metric divergence forces metric reform for a whole class family.
why_possibly_novel: Human-preference validation of segmentation metrics for amorphous classes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect 1k expert pairwise preferences over model masks on smoke scenes; fit which metric family predicts preferences.
main_risk: Expert preference may be application-dependent (emissions vs alarm); collect per-use-case preferences.

one_liner: Layered translucency compositions (smoke behind glass, fog over water) break single-layer models: a compositional generalization test for translucent classes.
problem: Datasets contain single translucent phenomena; reality composes them (smoke seen through a window). Whether models generalize compositionally to stacked translucency is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models trained on isolated smoke and isolated glass fail on their composition at rates far exceeding the product of individual error rates (super-multiplicative failure), demonstrating absence of compositional structure in learned translucency representations.
why_important: Compositional failure modes are silent in standard evaluation but common in deployment (indoor fires seen through windows are THE fire-alarm case).
why_possibly_novel: Compositional stress testing for translucent phenomena is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Composite controlled stacks (real captures through glass with/without smoke machine), evaluate single-phenomenon models on compositions.
main_risk: Physical capture effort; partial substitution with principled rendering possible.

one_liner: Is fire scale-invariant for segmentation? Test transfer from candle to wildfire along a pure scale ladder.
problem: Flames are quasi-fractal; if their image statistics are scale-invariant, small-fire data (cheap, safe to collect) should train large-fire models. Nobody has measured the transfer curve along scale.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: fire-region segmentation transfers across ~2 orders of magnitude of physical scale with <10% relative loss (supporting scale-invariance), but smoke does NOT (buoyancy regime changes plume morphology qualitatively) - a clean split between the two phenomena's scaling behavior.
why_important: Data-collection economics: if candle/bonfire data trains wildfire models, safe cheap data replaces dangerous expensive data.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-transfer curves for combustion phenomena are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble scale-ladder dataset (candle, campfire, bonfire, controlled burn, wildfire footage), train at one scale, test across the ladder.
main_risk: Scale confounds with camera distance/atmosphere; normalize by apparent size and control compression.

one_liner: What matters in synthetic smoke: factor-ablate density-field realism vs lighting realism vs background realism for sim2real transfer.
problem: Fluid-simulated smoke is a promising data source, but rendering has many realism axes and nobody knows which one pays. Teams max out all axes at great cost.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: transfer performance is dominated by illumination/scattering realism (single-vs-multi-scatter, correct sun/sky) with density-field fidelity (simulation resolution) contributing little beyond coarse plume shape - i.e. cheap simulations with expensive lighting beat the reverse at matched render budget.
why_important: Defines the cost-optimal synthetic data recipe for all translucent media, transferable to fog/steam/dust.
why_possibly_novel: Factorial realism ablation for participating-media training data is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: 2x2x2 factorial render (density res x scattering model x background source), train per cell, evaluate on real smoke benchmarks.
main_risk: Interaction effects may defeat the factorial simplification; the design still detects them.

one_liner: Smoke motion vs camera motion entanglement in aerial footage: drone ego-motion masquerades as plume dynamics and vice versa.
problem: Drone-based wildfire monitoring adds ego-motion that corrupts the temporal cues (drift, divergence) that smoke detection depends on; how much of temporal-model advantage survives ego-motion is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the accuracy advantage of temporal smoke models over static ones disappears almost entirely under drone ego-motion unless flow is ego-compensated, and compensation via cheap homography recovers most (not all) of it - the residual loss localizes to parallax-heavy terrain.
why_important: Quantifies exactly what stabilization/compensation infrastructure aerial fire systems need, and where terrain will still defeat them.
why_possibly_novel: Ego-motion ablation for temporal smoke cues is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take fixed-camera smoke videos, synthetically inject ego-motion (crop-path animation), measure temporal-model degradation with/without compensation.
main_risk: Synthetic ego-motion lacks true parallax; complement with real paired drone/tower footage if available.

one_liner: Cloud-shadow vs smoke-plume confusion in satellite imagery: which spectral bands are actually load-bearing?
problem: Satellite smoke products confuse smoke with cloud shadows and haze. Band-importance for this specific confusion (not general segmentation) is unquantified in modern learned models.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the smoke-vs-shadow decision in learned models rests almost entirely on 1-2 SWIR bands, and models degrade to near chance on this confusion pair when those bands are ablated - making sensor-band availability (differs across satellites) the primary cross-satellite transfer factor, above resolution.
why_important: Cross-satellite model reuse is constrained by band sets; knowing the load-bearing bands turns transfer failure from mystery to checklist.
why_possibly_novel: Confusion-pair-specific band attribution is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Band-ablation study on Sentinel/Landsat smoke datasets, scored specifically on smoke-vs-shadow confusion subsets.
main_risk: Band ablation in-model differs from retraining without the band; do both for the key bands.

one_liner: Heat shimmer (refractive turbulence) as a segmentable phenomenon: detecting invisible hot-air regions from background distortion alone.
problem: Hot air above fires/engines/roads is invisible in RGB appearance but visibly distorts the background. No benchmark or method targets refractive-media segmentation, though it precedes visible flame/smoke.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: temporal distortion statistics (local nonrigid displacement variance with characteristic frequency) suffice to segment shimmer regions with useful IoU on fixed cameras, and shimmer onset precedes visible smoke in a measurable fraction of ignition videos - a genuinely new early-fire channel.
why_important: Adds a new physical channel to early fire detection and defines a novel task class (segmenting media visible only through their distortion field).
why_possibly_novel: Refractive-region segmentation as a task is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (Schlieren imaging is KNOWN but requires special optics; this is passive RGB).
minimal_experiment: Collect fixed-camera footage over heat sources, compute distortion-field features, label shimmer regions, benchmark simple classifiers; check shimmer-before-smoke timing on ignition clips.
main_risk: Wind and camera vibration create confusable distortions; needs vibration controls.

one_liner: Koschmieder-law self-supervision: single-image fog density fields learnable from depth-luminance coupling without any fog labels.
problem: Fog density estimation lacks labels almost entirely. But atmospheric physics (KNOWN: Koschmieder attenuation model) couples scene depth, luminance shift, and fog density in a testable way that could supervise itself.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: enforcing consistency between a monocular depth estimate and the physically-implied luminance attenuation yields per-pixel fog-density maps that correlate strongly with transmissometer/visibility ground truth - label-free fog quantification from ordinary cameras.
why_important: Every traffic/airport camera becomes a visibility sensor; also provides dense fog supervision for downstream robustness training.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: dehazing uses these physics; closing the loop as self-supervised density REGRESSION validated against meteorological ground truth is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use webcam archives near airports (with METAR visibility records), fit the self-supervised model, validate against recorded visibility.
main_risk: Depth estimators are themselves fog-sensitive - circularity must be broken with clear-day depth priors of fixed scenes.

one_liner: Auto-exposure dynamics leak global fire evidence: models 'detect' fire from image-wide brightness adaptation, not fire pixels.
problem: When a camera auto-exposes to a bright flame, the whole image changes. Models may exploit this global cue, inflating benchmark scores and failing on manually-exposed or HDR cameras.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: fire-classification/segmentation models retain substantial accuracy when fire pixels are fully masked (evidence of global-cue reliance), and this reliance predicts their failure rate on constant-exposure footage - a shortcut with a measurable deployment cost.
why_important: Shortcut detection with direct deployment implications; also a general warning for any emissive-target dataset collected with auto-exposure cameras.
why_possibly_novel: Auto-exposure shortcut analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mask fire regions on test sets, measure retained accuracy; compare model performance on auto- vs fixed-exposure paired captures.
main_risk: Masked-region inpainting artifacts can themselves leak information; use multiple masking strategies.

one_liner: Deduplicate smoke/fire benchmarks by video provenance: same-event frames in train and test inflate scores, and rankings change after cleanup.
problem: Smoke/fire datasets are assembled from scraped videos; frames of the same event often land in both train and test splits, making benchmarks partially a memorization test.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: provenance-level deduplication (event/video-level splits) drops reported performance substantially (>10 points for some methods) and reorders methods, with the biggest drops for highest-capacity models - current smoke/fire SOTA is partly leakage measurement.
why_important: Safety-critical procurement decisions cite these benchmarks; leakage-corrected numbers are the ones that predict field performance.
why_possibly_novel: Provenance-forensic re-splitting of fire/smoke benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (leakage audits in other domains are KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Perceptual-hash + temporal correlation clustering across 4 public datasets to find leaked pairs; re-evaluate public models on clean splits.
main_risk: Aggressive dedup may over-merge distinct-but-similar events; manual verification of clusters needed.

one_liner: Glass segmentation models are frame detectors in disguise: frameless glass collapses them, quantifying boundary-cue dependence.
problem: Glass region datasets are dominated by framed windows/doors. Models may segment the frame context, not glass itself - a decomposable and testable reliance.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: occluding frames (while keeping glass interiors visible) collapses glass-detection accuracy toward chance, while occluding glass interiors (keeping frames) barely hurts - the learned representation contains almost no glass-intrinsic evidence.
why_important: Frameless glass (glass walls, barriers, shower doors) is precisely where collisions and robot failures happen; benchmark scores hide this.
why_possibly_novel: Interior-vs-frame information decomposition for glass models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Region-swap occlusion tests on GDD/GSD datasets across 3 public glass models; report interior-only vs frame-only accuracy.
main_risk: Occlusion masks introduce artifacts; use both blur-fill and inpainting controls.

one_liner: Mirror detection relies on scene-duplication matching: mirrors reflecting textureless regions become invisible to current models.
problem: Mirror segmentation models are believed to detect reflected-content correspondence with the surrounding scene. If so, mirrors showing featureless content (white walls, sky) should fail catastrophically - untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mirror-detection accuracy is a monotonic function of feature-correspondence density between mirror interior and visible scene, approaching chance for low-texture reflections - and this single variable explains most inter-image difficulty variance in mirror benchmarks.
why_important: Predictable failure conditions (bathroom mirrors reflecting blank walls) matter for robot navigation; and the analysis reveals the actual algorithm learned.
why_possibly_novel: Correspondence-density difficulty law for mirror detection is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute cross-region feature-match counts on mirror datasets, regress per-image accuracy on match density; validate causally with controlled captures (same mirror, varied reflected content).
main_risk: Confounds with mirror size and frame visibility; include them as covariates.

one_liner: Estimate the background refraction-distortion field as a pretext task: transparency becomes visible through what it does to the background.
problem: Transparent objects lack own-appearance; their signature is the distortion they impose on background. No mainstream method explicitly measures its usable information content.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a model trained to regress the local background-warp field (self-supervised from paired with/without-object captures or synthetic refraction) segments transparent objects with accuracy competitive with fully-supervised appearance methods, and generalizes better across object types because refraction physics is object-independent.
why_important: Physics-grounded signals should transfer where appearance signals do not - the central hope for robotic manipulation of glassware.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: refraction cues appear in classic vision; a warp-field pretext for transparent segmentation with cross-category transfer measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Render synthetic refractive objects over textured backgrounds, train warp-regression, transfer to real ClearGrasp-style data; compare cross-category generalization vs supervised baseline.
main_risk: Textureless backgrounds carry no warp signal - method has a principled blind spot to characterize honestly.

one_liner: Two-frame parallax separates glass from mirror: highlight/reflection motion direction is a deterministic physical discriminator.
problem: Static images confuse transmissive (glass) and reflective (mirror) surfaces. Under camera motion, transmitted and reflected content move with opposite parallax signs relative to the surface - a clean physical signature nobody benchmarks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a simple two-frame parallax-sign test resolves glass-vs-mirror with >90% accuracy where single-frame SOTA models are near chance, using no learning beyond flow estimation - physics beats appearance learning for this decision.
why_important: Robots move anyway; exploiting mandatory ego-motion for free surface-type disambiguation is immediately usable.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: layer separation via motion exists (reflection removal literature); its use as a surface-type CLASSIFIER benchmarked against segmentation SOTA is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Capture short baseline pairs of glass/mirror scenes, implement parallax-sign voting, compare with single-frame models.
main_risk: Small parallax + distant reflected content weakens the signal; characterize the operating envelope.

one_liner: A $30 polarizer beats architecture research for glass segmentation: quantify the sensor-vs-model marginal value.
problem: Specular reflections from dielectric surfaces are strongly polarized (KNOWN physics). The field pursues architectural gains on RGB while ignoring that a rotating polarizer may deliver larger gains for trivial cost.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: two-shot cross-polarized capture + a small model outperforms the best RGB-only architectures by a larger margin than 3 years of published architectural progress on glass/mirror segmentation - the field's bottleneck is sensing, not modeling.
why_important: A cost-benefit result that could redirect the subfield's effort allocation and immediately upgrade deployed systems that control their cameras.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head sensing-vs-architecture marginal-value accounting for transparent surfaces is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (polarization vision itself is KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Capture a 200-scene polarized glass dataset, train matched small models on RGB vs polarization pairs, compare with published RGB SOTA deltas.
main_risk: Doesn't help legacy imagery; framing must be prospective (system design), not retrospective.

one_liner: Prompt-through-glass confusion: point prompts inside glass regions make SAM segment the background object - measure the transparency-prompt pathology.
problem: Promptable models assume prompts land 'on' an object, but for transparent surfaces the prompt pixel contains two surfaces (glass + background). Which one SAM returns, and how consistently, is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM resolves the two-surface ambiguity by returning the background object in the overwhelming majority of cases (glass is never a hypothesis), and no prompt engineering (multi-point, box) reliably retrieves the glass surface - transparency is outside SAM's implicit object ontology, a categorical (not gradual) failure.
why_important: Defines a hard ontological boundary of promptable segmentation, relevant to any pipeline that might encounter windows/vitrines (retail, driving, indoor robotics).
why_possibly_novel: Two-surface prompt-resolution analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Prompt-grid evaluation on glass datasets: classify outputs as glass-surface/background/mixed; try prompt-engineering ladders for glass retrieval.
main_risk: Some 'glass' pixels are dominated by reflections (surface-like appearance) - stratify by transmission/reflection ratio.

one_liner: Depth-sensor dropout is free glass supervision: mine LiDAR/ToF invalid-return masks as automatic transparent-surface labels at fleet scale.
problem: Transparent surfaces are exactly where depth sensors return invalid/void measurements - a systematically informative failure that every robot fleet records and discards.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: RGB models trained purely on depth-dropout-derived pseudo-labels (with geometric filtering of other dropout causes) reach a large fraction (>70%) of fully-supervised glass segmentation accuracy with zero human labels, and scale with fleet data volume where supervised methods cannot.
why_important: Converts a sensor weakness into a self-annotating data engine for a notoriously label-starved problem.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: individual works use depth invalidity as a cue; the fleet-scale self-training scaling claim is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use existing RGB-D datasets (ScanNet-like), extract dropout masks, filter (specular metals, range limits), train RGB-only model, evaluate on GDD.
main_risk: Dropout also fires on dark/absorptive and distant surfaces; the filtering step determines everything.

one_liner: Mirror-boundary ownership is annotated inconsistently across datasets: the frame/content confusion audit.
problem: Does a mirror mask include its frame? The reflected content's boundary or the physical glass edge? Datasets answer differently, and models inherit incoherent supervision.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: public mirror/glass datasets disagree systematically on boundary conventions (measurable via matched-scene or protocol probing), and this convention noise accounts for a substantial fraction of apparent cross-dataset generalization failure - harmonizing conventions post hoc recovers several points of transfer performance for free.
why_important: Convention noise masquerades as model failure, corrupting scientific conclusions about architecture differences in the whole subfield.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-dataset convention forensics for specular/transparent classes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Annotate 100 shared-protocol probe images under each dataset's inferred convention, quantify convention distance, re-evaluate cross-dataset transfer after convention mapping.
main_risk: Inferring conventions from data is noisy; contact dataset authors where possible.

one_liner: Transparent vs translucent is a bimodal task hiding in one benchmark: clear glass and frosted glass are solved by different cues and should be split.
problem: Benchmarks pool clear (see-through) and frosted/textured (diffusing) surfaces. If the discriminative cues differ fundamentally (background continuity vs surface texture), pooled scores obscure two distinct problems.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-image performance across glass benchmarks is bimodal along a measurable transmission-clarity axis; model families rank DIFFERENTLY on the two modes (texture-based models win frosted, context-based win clear), so pooled leaderboards are not measuring a single capability.
why_important: Correct taxonomy is prerequisite for progress; a documented mode split would restructure how the subfield evaluates and designs.
why_possibly_novel: Clarity-axis bimodality analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate per-region clarity (background visibility metrics) on GDD/Trans10K, plot per-model accuracy distributions along the axis, test rank inversion.
main_risk: Clarity estimation without GT optics is approximate; hand-label a calibration subset.

one_liner: Day-night transmission/reflection flip: the same window changes optical class by time of day, and models trained on one phase fail on the other.
problem: Windows transmit by day (interior view) and reflect by night (mirror-like from lit side). This physically-forced within-scene domain shift is undocumented in segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: glass segmentation models exhibit a strong day-night performance asymmetry aligned with their training-set illumination statistics, and the SAME physical surfaces flip between 'easy' and 'hard' across the transition - fixed-scene time-lapse evaluation will show a characteristic sigmoid degradation tied to the transmission/reflection ratio, not to general low-light difficulty.
why_important: Building-scale vision (energy audits, security, robotics) operates around the clock; a physics-driven diurnal failure cycle is predictable and correctable once measured.
why_possibly_novel: Fixed-scene diurnal analysis for transparent surfaces is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect webcam/time-lapse footage of glass facades across day-night cycles, annotate once (geometry is fixed), evaluate models across the cycle against illumination covariates.
main_risk: Low-light degradation confounds; include matched non-glass control surfaces for baseline drift.

one_liner: Establish the human ceiling for clean-glass detection in single RGB images: some transparency is information-theoretically invisible.
problem: Claims of glass-detection progress never report the human ceiling. Perfectly clean, non-reflective glass may be undetectable in principle from single images - meaning benchmarks contain unsolvable pixels that cap and distort scores.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: human experts given unlimited time fail on a measurable subset of benchmark glass regions (near-zero mutual information cases), models fail on a superset of these, and removing information-theoretically-invisible regions from evaluation changes both absolute scores and method rankings.
why_important: Separates 'model limitation' from 'task impossibility' - required for honest progress claims and for deciding when extra sensors are mandatory rather than optional.
why_possibly_novel: Human-ceiling calibration for transparency benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run a careful human study (N=10, unlimited time, zoom allowed) on 300 glass regions; classify regions by human solvability; re-score public models on the solvable subset.
main_risk: Human performance depends on display conditions and effort; strict protocol needed.

one_liner: Interior-blindness test: mask out glass interiors entirely - if performance is unchanged, models never look at the glass.
problem: Related to frame reliance but stronger: perhaps NO pixel inside glass regions contributes to detection decisions - models may operate exclusively on surrounding geometry (door frames, wall openings).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: replacing all glass-interior pixels with scrambled or neutral content changes glass-region predictions by <5% IoU for current models - a falsifiable 'interior blindness' claim implying the task, as learned, is contextual opening detection, and that models will hallucinate glass in glassless openings (testable corollary on open windows).
why_important: The corollary - false glass on open frames - is a real robotics hazard (robot refuses to pass an open doorway) and reveals the true learned task.
why_possibly_novel: The open-frame hallucination corollary test is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Interior-scramble evaluation + a curated open-window/empty-frame probe set; measure hallucinated glass rate.
main_risk: Overlaps conceptually with W2-A-0101; kept because the corollary (hallucination on open frames) is a distinct falsifiable prediction.

one_liner: Joint vs sequential reflection-removal and segmentation: does cleaning reflections first help or destroy the very cues glass detectors need?
problem: Reflections are noise for scene segmentation but SIGNAL for glass detection. Pipelines that remove reflections before segmentation may improve object masks while blinding glass detection - an unmeasured interaction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: reflection-removal preprocessing improves general scene segmentation inside glass regions but strictly degrades glass-region detection itself, with the tradeoff strong enough that optimal pipelines must run both paths - a quantified antagonism between two subfields' objectives.
why_important: Both communities publish independently; demonstrating their objectives are antagonistic in composition changes how full systems should be built.
why_possibly_novel: The antagonism quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run 3 reflection-removal methods before 3 glass detectors and 3 scene segmenters; measure the two metrics' movement directions.
main_risk: Reflection-removal quality varies; conclusions should be method-robust.

one_liner: LiDAR-camera disagreement mining auto-labels glass at driving-fleet scale: the free training set nobody harvests.
problem: In driving stacks, LiDAR passes through glass while camera sees surfaces (or vice versa for mirrors) - systematic cross-sensor disagreement localizes transparent surfaces, yet is discarded as noise.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: cross-sensor disagreement patterns (camera-detects-surface + LiDAR-returns-far) yield glass pseudo-labels with precision >80% after geometric filtering in urban scenes, sufficient to train camera-only glass detection that generalizes to buildings/bus-stops/storefronts absent from any human-labeled dataset.
why_important: Storefront/bus-shelter glass matters for driving safety and is essentially unlabeled at scale today.
why_possibly_novel: Disagreement-mining for transparent-class auto-labeling in driving data is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run the mining rule on nuScenes/Waymo sequences, manually audit 500 mined regions for precision, train and evaluate a camera-only model.
main_risk: LiDAR behavior on glass varies with angle/coating (sometimes returns); precision audit is the gating step.

one_liner: Liquid-level segmentation in transparent containers: the meniscus is a 1-pixel curve whose cues are refraction discontinuities, not edges.
problem: Estimating fill levels through glass (labs, kitchens, industry) requires localizing the liquid-air interface, which presents as a refraction-index discontinuity - a signal class no segmentation paradigm targets.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: meniscus localization from single RGB fails with standard segmentation (boundary F-score near chance) but becomes reliable using background-distortion discontinuity features across the interface - and container curvature can be jointly inferred, making level estimation metrically accurate to <5% of container height.
why_important: Lab automation and food robotics need fill-level perception; also a clean scientific instance of 'segmenting an index-of-refraction boundary'.
why_possibly_novel: Meniscus segmentation as a benchmark task is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Capture container ladder (shapes x liquids x backgrounds) with measured fill levels; benchmark segmentation vs distortion-feature approaches.
main_risk: Opaque liquids trivialize the task, colorless liquids in textureless scenes may be impossible - the dataset must span the difficulty axis honestly.

one_liner: Mirror recursion depth as a scene-understanding stress test: what do models do with mirrors inside mirrors?
problem: Nested reflections (mirror showing a mirror) produce recursive scene copies. Model behavior on recursion - treating each level as real, or collapsing all - probes whether any scene-graph reasoning exists in dense predictors.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: current models segment first-level reflected content as real objects at the same rate as directly-viewed objects (no reflection discount at all), and behavior is IDENTICAL at deeper recursion levels - demonstrating zero representation of the reflection relation, falsifiable by any level-dependent behavior.
why_important: A crisp probe separating 'pixel classification' from 'scene understanding' - useful as a diagnostic axis for foundation model claims.
why_possibly_novel: Recursion-depth-graded evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Stage two-mirror scenes with controlled recursion, run panoptic/promptable models, tabulate per-level treatment of duplicated objects.
main_risk: Small niche; value is diagnostic, framed as a probe rather than a benchmark.

one_liner: Caustics as transparent-object shadows: the bright patterns under glassware are a detection cue with known physics that no model uses.
problem: Transparent objects cast structured light patterns (caustics) and faint darkened shadows. These secondary evidence sources are visible when the object is not, and are absent from all training objectives.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: caustic/shadow regions are detectable with high precision and their presence improves transparent-object localization recall substantially in tabletop scenes (especially for rim-lit invisible glassware), with the geometric back-projection from caustic to object being learnable from synthetic optics.
why_important: Robotic grasping of glassware fails on exactly the invisible cases; secondary-evidence detection is a fundamentally different attack on the problem.
why_possibly_novel: Caustic-mediated object localization for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Render synthetic tabletop scenes with physically-correct caustics, train caustic detector + back-projection, test on real captured glassware scenes with directional light.
main_risk: Requires directional lighting; diffuse-lit scenes lose the cue - operating conditions must be characterized.

one_liner: Glass boundary is physically a gradient, not a curve: annotations pretend a sharp edge exists where refraction blends millimeters of scene.
problem: At glass edges (especially curved surfaces), the image transitions through a refraction gradient several pixels wide. Sharp-polygon annotations impose a fictional boundary whose placement varies by annotator - structurally identical to smoke's problem but unrecognized for rigid transparent objects.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: boundary-localization variance among annotators on curved-glass edges is several times higher than on opaque-object edges (measurable), and boundary-quality metric differences between competing methods on transparency benchmarks fall INSIDE this annotation noise band - boundary-level rankings there are statistically meaningless.
why_important: Guards the community against over-interpreting boundary-metric progress on transparency benchmarks.
why_possibly_novel: Annotation-noise-floor analysis specific to refractive edges is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-annotator re-labeling of 200 curved-glass edges, compute noise floor, compare with published method deltas.
main_risk: Straightforward but requires funding a small annotation study.

one_liner: Cross-dataset transparency transfer is near zero, and the cause is photographic setting bias, not object diversity: lab-vs-wild forensics.
problem: Transparency datasets are collected in narrow settings (lab turntables, stock photos, specific cities). Cross-dataset generalization numbers are rarely reported and anecdotally terrible - but WHY they fail is unattributed.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: cross-dataset performance drops are predicted by capture-setting statistics (lighting type, background depth structure, camera height) rather than object-category overlap - transfer fails on photography, not on objects - implying collection-protocol diversification beats category diversification for the next dataset.
why_important: Directly instructs how the community should spend its next data-collection dollar for transparent objects.
why_possibly_novel: Setting-vs-category attribution of transfer failure is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Full cross-evaluation matrix over 5 transparency datasets; regress transfer drops on setting statistics vs category-overlap measures.
main_risk: Setting statistics are post-hoc descriptors; causal confirmation needs controlled recapture of matched objects across settings.

one_liner: A $200 thermal camera makes glass opaque: quantify when cheap LWIR fusion beats years of RGB algorithmic progress on transparent surfaces.
problem: Long-wave infrared does not transmit through glass (KNOWN physics) - glass is opaque and boundary-crisp in thermal. The economic tradeoff between adding a thermal channel and pursuing RGB-only algorithms is never computed.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: RGB+LWIR late fusion with a trivial model exceeds the best RGB-only glass segmentation by a margin larger than the total published RGB architectural progress since the task's inception, and the fusion model's failures are confined to thermally-equilibrated scenes (measurable operating boundary).
why_important: If a cheap sensor dominates the algorithmic frontier, safety-critical system builders (robots near glass) should know before funding more RGB research.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: thermal glass opacity is textbook optics; the quantified benchmark-level economic comparison is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect 150 aligned RGB-LWIR glass scenes, train small fusion model, compare against RGB SOTA reproduced on the RGB channel of the same scenes.
main_risk: Thermal-RGB alignment and resolution mismatch; scene temperature equilibrium cases where thermal contrast vanishes.

one_liner: Puddles are mirrors on the road: wet-surface reflections are systematically mislabeled and cause phantom-object segmentation in driving scenes.
problem: After rain, road puddles reflect vehicles, lights, and sky. Driving datasets label puddle pixels as 'road', and models inherit both phantom objects (reflected cars segmented as cars) and missed hazards (puddle itself unrecognized).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on wet-scene driving data, a measurable rate of false vehicle/pedestrian segments spatially coincides with puddle reflections (verifiable by geometric mirroring about the road plane), and this error class is absent from benchmark metrics because puddle regions are labeled road and errors there are diluted - a hidden safety-relevant failure mode with a geometric verification method.
why_important: Phantom pedestrians in reflections can trigger emergency braking; the geometric verification makes the audit rigorous rather than anecdotal.
why_possibly_novel: Mirror-geometry-verified phantom-object auditing in driving segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mine wet scenes from BDD/ACDC, detect vertically-mirrored segment pairs about the road plane, quantify phantom rate per model.
main_risk: True objects and their reflections co-occur; the mirroring test must be strict to avoid false audit positives.

one_liner: Shadow-density inversion recovers translucency alpha for free: an object's shadow encodes its transmission coefficient.
problem: Ground-truth alpha for translucent objects requires studio matting. But the shadow a translucent object casts has attenuation proportional to its transmission - physics offers free alpha labels outdoors.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-region transmission coefficients recovered from shadow luminance ratios (object shadow vs adjacent opaque-reference shadow) agree with studio-measured alpha within usable tolerance, enabling automatic construction of translucency-supervised datasets from ordinary sunlit footage.
why_important: Would unlock large-scale translucency supervision without studios - feeding every idea that needs alpha ground truth (smoke, frosted glass, fabrics).
why_possibly_novel: Shadow-mediated alpha recovery as a dataset-construction tool is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Capture objects with known transmission (calibrated filters) in sunlight, invert shadow ratios, validate against ground truth; then mine web imagery.
main_risk: Multiple light sources and ambient bounce corrupt the inversion; restrict to strong-sun regimes and quantify error bars.

one_liner: Screens are emissive fake windows: displays fool glass/scene segmentation, and their temporal artifacts (refresh, moire) are the untapped tell.
problem: TVs and monitors show scenes that models segment as real 3D content (a person on a billboard segmented as pedestrian). Their physical tells - refresh flicker, moire against sensor grid, spectral spikiness - are never exploited.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: display-region false-positive rates for person/vehicle classes are substantial in urban scenes, and a rolling-shutter-aware temporal probe (banding detection) identifies emissive displays with high precision, eliminating most phantom segments at negligible compute.
why_important: Billboards with faces/cars are ubiquitous; driving and surveillance stacks need display rejection, and the physics tell is robust across display content.
why_possibly_novel: Display-rejection via sensor-display temporal interaction for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate urban scenes with active displays, measure phantom-class rates across models; implement banding detector, measure rejection precision/recall.
main_risk: Modern displays at high refresh with global-shutter cameras may lack banding; enumerate the sensor-display compatibility matrix.

one_liner: Dirt makes glass visible: performance vs surface-condition curves reveal that benchmarks oversample dirty, easy glass.
problem: Dust, smudges, and rain droplets give glass surfaces detectable texture. If benchmarks oversample real-world dirty glass, reported performance overstates ability on clean architectural glass - the dangerous case.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: model accuracy on glass regions is a strong increasing function of surface-contamination level (quantifiable via micro-texture statistics), benchmark distributions are skewed toward contaminated glass relative to modern building stock, and re-weighting evaluation to clean-glass-heavy distributions drops SOTA scores dramatically.
why_important: Deployment environments (offices, malls) feature professionally-cleaned glass - exactly the underrepresented hard case; the analysis recalibrates safety expectations.
why_possibly_novel: Contamination-conditioned evaluation for transparency is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Score contamination level on benchmark glass regions (annotator + texture statistics), plot accuracy vs contamination, reweight and re-rank.
main_risk: Contamination scoring is subjective at the margins; anchor with controlled dirty-to-clean captures of one facade.

one_liner: Window tint and low-emissivity coatings create a spectral fingerprint: modern architectural glass is detectable by its color cast, old glass is not.
problem: Contemporary buildings use coated/tinted glazing with subtle spectral signatures (green/blue edge casts, reflectance curves), while historic clear glass lacks them. Detection difficulty may be stratified by construction era - an unexamined structure in the data.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: glass-detection accuracy correlates with coating-induced spectral signatures measurable in RGB statistics; controlling for context, coated glazing is substantially easier than heritage clear glass - implying reported urban benchmark performance silently rides on modern construction practice and will degrade in historic districts.
why_important: Geographic/architectural generalization of glass detection has direct safety implications for delivery robots and drones operating across city ages.
why_possibly_novel: Construction-era stratification of transparency performance is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Tag benchmark glass by building era/coating evidence, stratify performance; capture matched modern vs heritage facades for causal confirmation.
main_risk: Era correlates with frame style and cleanliness; multi-covariate analysis required.

one_liner: Do models and humans find the same camouflage hard? Correlate model difficulty with human search time per image.
problem: Camouflaged object detection (COD) difficulty is assumed to align with human difficulty, but models use different cues; misalignment would mean COD benchmarks measure something other than camouflage.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-image model error and human search time correlate only moderately (rank r about 0.3-0.5), with systematic divergence classes: humans fail on semantic mimicry (leaf-shaped insects), models fail on low-level texture continuity - two dissociable camouflage mechanisms confounded in one benchmark.
why_important: If difficulty axes dissociate, defense/wildlife applications need mechanism-specific evaluation, and 'superhuman COD' claims need re-reading.
why_possibly_novel: Human-search-time-anchored difficulty decomposition for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run a timed human search study (N=20, 300 COD images), correlate with per-image model errors, factor-analyze the divergences.
main_risk: Search time is noisy and display-dependent; needs psychophysics rigor.

one_liner: COD benchmarks have a center-and-single-object bias: randomized multi-instance evaluation collapses reported SOTA.
problem: COD datasets typically frame one centered camouflaged subject (photographer bias). Models may learn 'find the centered anomaly' rather than camouflage-breaking.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SOTA COD models degrade disproportionately (vs a saliency-model control) when evaluated on off-center crops, multi-instance composites, and empty scenes (false-positive stress) - a large fraction of measured COD skill is compositional prior, not camouflage analysis.
why_important: Real camouflage scenarios (wildlife surveys, search-and-rescue) have arbitrary composition and mostly-empty frames; benchmark bias hides deployment failure.
why_possibly_novel: Composition-bias stress testing specific to COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-render COD test sets with controlled recomposition (offset crops, mosaics, negatives), report degradation ratios per model.
main_risk: Recomposition artifacts; use camera-trap footage as the natural-composition validation.

one_liner: Quantify the information motion adds to camouflage breaking: matched-frame video-vs-still analysis on camouflaged animals.
problem: Motion famously breaks camouflage, but the magnitude - how many bits motion adds over the best static analysis - has never been quantified for models or humans on matched data.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for strongly-camouflaged targets, 3-5 frames of motion raise model detection from near-chance to high accuracy (most of the task's information is temporal), implying static COD is a fundamentally information-starved formulation and the field's static focus is misallocated.
why_important: Redirects COD research investment toward temporal formulations where the information actually lives.
why_possibly_novel: Bits-added-by-motion quantification on matched still/video pairs is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: MoCA dataset: evaluate matched models on single frames vs short clips, sweep clip length, plot information gain curves.
main_risk: Camera motion contaminates object motion; use stabilized subsets.

one_liner: Camouflage and saliency are poles of one conspicuity axis: test whether a single linear direction in feature space spans both tasks.
problem: Salient object detection and COD are run as separate subfields with separate models, yet they plausibly measure opposite ends of one perceptual quantity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in foundation-model feature space, a single learned 'conspicuity' direction supports both SOD and COD via thresholding at opposite ends (linear probe transfers between tasks with minor loss), implying the two literatures are duplicating one problem - falsifiable if cross-task probes fail.
why_important: Would unify two benchmark ecosystems and reveal that dozens of specialized architectures encode one scalar function.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-task linear-direction unification test is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train linear probes on DINOv2 features for SOD, evaluate on COD (inverted) and vice versa; compare with specialized SOTA.
main_risk: Task definitions differ beyond conspicuity (object-hood, boundaries); partial transfer needs careful interpretation.

one_liner: Split camouflage into texture-matching vs shape-disruption mechanisms and show current benchmarks confound them.
problem: Biological camouflage uses distinct strategies (background matching, disruptive coloration, edge mimicry). Datasets pool them, so 'COD performance' averages over mechanistically different problems.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: annotating COD images by camouflage mechanism reveals strongly method-dependent performance profiles (edge-based methods fail on disruptive coloration, texture methods fail on background matching), and mechanism composition varies across datasets enough to explain most cross-dataset ranking instability.
why_important: A mechanistic taxonomy converts an appearance-shuffled benchmark into interpretable sub-problems with different optimal designs.
why_possibly_novel: Mechanism-stratified COD evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (mechanisms themselves are KNOWN in biology, e.g. Cott's principles).
minimal_experiment: Have biologists annotate mechanism labels on 1k COD images, stratify existing model results, quantify ranking flips.
main_risk: Mechanisms co-occur in single animals; multi-label annotation needed.

one_liner: Region-core evaluation for ambiguous boundaries: scoring only the indisputable interior changes COD/boundary-class rankings.
problem: For camouflaged and fuzzy-boundary objects, annotator disagreement concentrates at boundaries, yet metrics weight boundary pixels heavily - rankings may reflect boundary-style matching rather than detection ability.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: evaluating on eroded 'consensus cores' plus a separate detection-level score reorders published COD methods materially, and the reordering correlates with which annotation team produced each training set - boundary-heavy metrics have been rewarding style imitation.
why_important: Cheap re-evaluation protocol that could correct a whole leaderboard's conclusions without new data collection.
why_possibly_novel: Core-based re-ranking audit for ambiguity-heavy tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Erode GT masks at multiple radii, re-score public COD predictions, measure rank stability vs erosion radius.
main_risk: Erosion destroys legitimately-informative boundary skill for thin animals; report per-shape-class.

one_liner: COD models exploit chromatic micro-contrast that humans cannot see: grayscale and chroma-noise ablations reveal non-perceptual shortcuts.
problem: If models detect camouflaged animals via sub-perceptual color differences (JPEG chroma noise, sensor pattern), they solve a different problem than camouflage perception - and will fail when those artifacts change.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD SOTA drops far more than human performance under chroma removal and chroma-noise matching (models rely on machine-visible chromatic microstructure), and this reliance predicts cross-camera generalization failure - the shortcut is measurable and consequential.
why_important: Determines whether COD progress is perceptual science or artifact mining; guides dataset re-collection with camera diversity.
why_possibly_novel: Perceptual-vs-machine cue decomposition in COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate models and humans on original vs chroma-ablated COD images; correlate model reliance with cross-dataset drops.
main_risk: Human baseline collection needed; ablation must preserve perceptual equivalence (verify psychophysically).

one_liner: Artificial (military/textile) camouflage and biological camouflage do not transfer: two data regimes with different statistics.
problem: COD datasets are mostly biological; applications often target artificial camouflage (nets, patterns, clothing). Whether learned camouflage-breaking transfers between the regimes is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: cross-regime transfer (bio-trained to artificial, and reverse) loses most performance because the two regimes break different statistical assumptions (biological camouflage matches local texture statistics; printed patterns match texture class but violate phase statistics) - a measurable statistical signature separates them.
why_important: Security and conservation users assume COD models generalize; a documented regime boundary with statistical explanation prevents misdeployment.
why_possibly_novel: Bio-vs-artificial camouflage transfer quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble small artificial-camouflage test set, run bio-trained SOTA, analyze failures via texture-statistics comparisons.
main_risk: Artificial-camouflage data availability; may require synthetic rendering with real patterns.

one_liner: The zoom paradox: camouflage vanishes at high magnification, so scale selection IS the camouflage problem - test scale-oracle decomposition.
problem: Camouflage works at the scale where object texture matches background; zoom in enough and micro-texture differences appear. Whether model failure is scale-selection failure vs discrimination failure is unresolved.
