core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: with an oracle providing optimal analysis scale per region, simple texture discriminators match SOTA COD models (discrimination is easy at the right scale), so COD progress has mostly been implicit scale-search progress - reframing the problem as attention/search, not representation.
why_important: Identifies the actual hard sub-problem, redirecting architecture effort toward scale policy learning.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-oracle attribution for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Grid-search analysis scale per image region on COD data, compare oracle-scale simple features vs end-to-end SOTA.
main_risk: Oracle defined via GT leaks information; careful protocol (scale chosen on held-out criterion) required.

one_liner: Matting-vs-masking crossover for fuzzy classes: measure the boundary-alpha entropy above which binary annotation becomes counterproductive.
problem: Hair, fur, feathers, and foliage boundaries are partial-coverage zones. The field lacks a criterion for when to switch from binary masks to alpha mattes, so datasets choose arbitrarily.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: there exists a measurable boundary-alpha entropy threshold above which training with binary labels actively degrades both binary AND soft evaluation performance relative to matte supervision (label noise exceeds signal), and common classes (fur, hair, foliage) sit above it while most objects sit below.
why_important: Provides a principled annotation-policy rule for every future dataset touching fuzzy classes.
why_possibly_novel: A quantified supervision-type crossover criterion is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On matting datasets with true alpha, threshold alphas into binary labels at various entropy levels, train matched models, locate the crossover.
main_risk: Threshold may be architecture-dependent; test across 3 model families.

one_liner: Train on disagreement maps directly: predicting WHERE annotators disagree transfers across datasets better than predicting masks.
problem: Annotator disagreement is discarded as noise, but disagreement structure (what confuses humans) may be a more universal, transferable target than any single mask convention.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a model trained to predict inter-annotator disagreement maps on one dataset predicts disagreement on unseen datasets and unseen classes better than mask-trained models' uncertainty predicts either - ambiguity is a more domain-invariant signal than object identity.
why_important: A transferable ambiguity detector has universal uses: annotation routing, evaluation weighting, and safe-deployment gating - one model serving all segmentation efforts.
why_possibly_novel: Disagreement as the primary (not auxiliary) prediction target with cross-dataset transfer claims is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use multi-annotator datasets (LVIS/LIDC/COD multi-rater subsets), train disagreement predictor, test zero-shot on held-out multi-rater sets.
main_risk: Disagreement conflates stimulus ambiguity with protocol/skill differences; needs dataset-effect controls.

one_liner: Camouflage needs global context more than saliency does: context-radius sweeps as a signature that separates the two tasks computationally.
problem: Whether COD is locally solvable (texture anomaly) or requires scene-level reasoning (what background SHOULD look like here) determines correct architectures - but no one has measured the context-requirement curve.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD accuracy grows with input context radius much longer than SOD accuracy does (context saturation at ~2x object size for SOD vs >8x for COD), because detecting background-matching requires modeling background statistics far from the object - a measurable computational signature of the task's structure.
why_important: Context curves are architecture-independent task descriptors that tell designers what receptive fields are actually necessary.
why_possibly_novel: Comparative context-requirement curves across SOD/COD are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Crop-radius sweep evaluation of matched models on SOD and COD datasets, plot accuracy-vs-context curves.
main_risk: Crop-based context control confounds resolution; use masking-based context control too.

one_liner: Cross-domain camouflage: does COD pretraining transfer to isointense lesion detection in medical images?
problem: Isointense tumors (same intensity as surrounding tissue) are literally camouflaged anatomy. Whether camouflage-breaking skills learned on animals transfer to medical camouflage would reveal if COD models learn generalizable 'subtle-difference amplification'.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD-pretrained models fine-tune to isointense-lesion segmentation with significantly less medical data than generic-pretrained models (positive transfer of camouflage-breaking), and the transferred capability localizes to texture-discrepancy feature channels identifiable by ablation.
why_important: Would establish camouflage-breaking as a portable capability and give medical imaging a new pretraining source; negative result equally informative about COD's true content.
why_possibly_novel: COD-to-medical transfer study is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Fine-tune COD-pretrained vs ImageNet/DINO-pretrained models on low-contrast liver/brain lesion sets across data-budget ladder.
main_risk: Modality gap may swamp task-similarity benefits; include modality-adapted controls.

one_liner: COD models lack inhibition-of-return: they find one instance and stop, missing conspecific groups - measure multi-instance recall collapse.
problem: Camouflaged animals often occur in groups, but COD models (and datasets) are single-instance biased; sequential search behavior (find, inhibit, continue) has no model analogue.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on multi-instance camouflage scenes, per-instance recall for the 2nd..Nth instances drops steeply conditional on finding the 1st (models' spatial attention collapses onto the found instance), while human searchers show much flatter conditional recall - a measurable architectural deficit in iterative search.
why_important: Wildlife population surveys (the main COD application) require counting, not detecting one; conditional-recall metrics expose the real gap.
why_possibly_novel: Conditional multi-instance recall analysis for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Composite calibrated multi-instance scenes + real herd/flock camera-trap images, measure conditional recall curves for models and humans.
main_risk: Compositing realism; camera-trap GT requires expert annotation.

one_liner: Compression halos leak object boundaries in COD datasets: an artifact audit of whether benchmarks are accidentally easy.
problem: JPEG compression creates ringing/blocking artifacts that differ between smooth animal bodies and textured backgrounds, potentially outlining 'camouflaged' objects with machine-visible halos.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: COD datasets contain compression-artifact gradients along object boundaries detectable by simple filters, models exploit them (performance drops on re-compressed or raw-recaptured versions), and artifact strength correlates with reported per-image accuracy - part of COD performance is compression forensics.
why_important: Determines whether benchmark difficulty is real; parallels found in deepfake detection where compression artifacts dominated (KNOWN phenomenon in that field).
why_possibly_novel: Compression-forensic audit of COD specifically is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Measure boundary-aligned artifact energy across COD datasets; re-evaluate models on artifact-normalized versions.
main_risk: Re-compression changes many things at once; include artifact-matched control regions.

one_liner: Humans improve on camouflage with viewing time; models are anytime-flat: the missing iterative-inference dimension.
problem: Human camouflage-breaking is a temporal process (seconds of scrutiny), while feedforward models emit one answer. Whether iterative computation (recurrence, diffusion steps, TTA loops) recovers the human time-accuracy curve shape is unexplored.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: model families with iterative inference show accuracy-vs-compute curves qualitatively matching human time-accuracy curves on COD (log-linear gains), while feedforward models are flat - and the iterative gains concentrate on exactly the images where humans need long viewing, suggesting shared computational structure in the search process.
why_important: Connects camouflage perception to a concrete computational property (iterative refinement) with architecture-agnostic evidence.
why_possibly_novel: Time-accuracy curve matching between humans and iterative models on COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect human time-accuracy data (masked-exposure protocol); run diffusion/recurrent segmenters at varying step counts; compare curve families per image.
main_risk: Curve similarity is weak evidence for mechanism sharing; frame claims carefully.

one_liner: Background-statistics complexity predicts COD difficulty better than any object property: difficulty lives in the scene, not the animal.
problem: COD difficulty is intuitively attributed to the animal's camouflage quality, but the background's statistical richness (how many plausible hiding textures it offers) may dominate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-image model error is predicted more strongly by background texture-diversity statistics (entropy of local texture descriptors) than by object-side features (size, contrast, edge density), and manipulating backgrounds alone (same animal composited into richer scenes) moves difficulty as predicted - difficulty is a scene property.
why_important: Difficulty prediction from unlabeled scenes enables dataset design, active collection, and deployment risk maps (which habitats defeat detection).
why_possibly_novel: Scene-side difficulty attribution with compositing causality is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Regress errors on scene vs object features across COD datasets; run compositing intervention study.
main_risk: Compositing artifacts alter difficulty independently; needs artifact-controlled composites.

one_liner: Part-level ambiguity in camouflage: where the animal ends and the mimicked substrate begins is sometimes objectively undecidable - propose decision-theoretic annotation.
problem: A stick insect's legs against twigs create regions where even experts cannot delimit the boundary (occlusion + mimicry). Forcing binary annotation there manufactures noise that training and evaluation both inherit.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert annotators given an explicit 'undecidable' label option use it on a stable, reproducible subset of pixels (high inter-expert agreement on WHERE decisions are impossible), and excluding those regions from training improves model performance on the decidable majority - undecidability is itself reliably annotatable.
why_important: Introduces a third label state with measurable reliability, applicable to every ambiguity-heavy domain (medical margins, smoke edges).
why_possibly_novel: Reproducibility measurement of explicit undecidability annotation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Three-state re-annotation of 300 hard COD images by 5 experts, measure agreement on the undecidable state, retrain with exclusion masks.
main_risk: Annotators may use the escape hatch inconsistently without strict protocol; instructions design is critical.

one_liner: Eulerian micro-motion amplification as COD preprocessing: breathing and heartbeat make hidden animals visible to ordinary segmenters.
problem: Living camouflaged animals exhibit involuntary micro-motions invisible per-frame. Motion amplification could convert the temporal signal into spatial signal that any static model can use - untested as a COD pipeline.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: applying temporal motion amplification to static-camera clips converts a substantial fraction of model-undetectable camouflaged animals into detectable ones at fixed false-positive rate, with gains concentrated on live-and-still subjects (validating the biological mechanism).
why_important: A cheap, model-agnostic capability jump for wildlife monitoring and search applications, grounded in a physical signal orthogonal to appearance.
why_possibly_novel: Motion-magnification preprocessing for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (magnification itself is KNOWN: Eulerian Video Magnification, Wu et al. 2012).
minimal_experiment: Fixed-camera wildlife clips with hidden animals: run detection with and without amplification preprocessing at matched FPR.
main_risk: Wind-driven vegetation motion amplifies too; needs frequency-band selection tuned to biological motion.

one_liner: Findability bias: COD datasets contain only camouflage that FAILED (someone photographed it) - true camouflage performance is unbounded above benchmarks.
problem: Every COD image exists because a human found the animal. Camouflage that succeeds is systematically absent from data, meaning benchmarks sample the easy tail of the true distribution - an unmeasurable-seeming selection bias that can actually be bounded.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: using camera-trap archives where animal presence is known independently (telemetry-collared animals, baited sites with activity logs), the recall of both humans and models on 'present-but-unphotographable' cases is drastically lower than benchmark numbers - and the gap (findability bias magnitude) can be estimated quantitatively for the first time.
why_important: All COD performance claims inherit this bias; measuring it converts an epistemological worry into a correction factor for real-world deployment planning.
why_possibly_novel: Independent-presence-verified COD evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Partner with ecology telemetry datasets: sample camera-trap frames where collar GPS confirms in-view presence, measure detection rates vs standard benchmarks.
main_risk: GPS-to-camera-frame alignment uncertainty; requires ecology collaboration and careful geometry.

one_liner: Boundary-gradient-direction statistics separate camouflaged from conspicuous objects: a low-level signature of camouflage strategy.
problem: Camouflaged boundaries should have systematically weaker and differently-oriented image gradients than normal object boundaries, but this low-level statistical characterization of camouflage has not been built - it could ground difficulty measures and detection priors in measurable image structure.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the joint distribution of (gradient magnitude, gradient-to-boundary-normal angle) along GT boundaries cleanly separates camouflaged from conspicuous objects, and the separation axis predicts per-object model failure better than global contrast measures - camouflage has a quantitative boundary signature.
why_important: Provides an image-computable camouflage-strength scale (useful for dataset design, difficulty stratification, and even camouflage design/assessment in biology).
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-statistics-based camouflage quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute the joint statistics on COD vs COCO boundaries, train a difficulty predictor, validate against per-object model errors.
main_risk: Statistic may reduce to known contrast measures; the angular component is the novelty bet.

one_liner: Shadow inconsistency betrays camouflaged objects: texture can mimic, but cast shadows obey geometry that mimicry cannot fake.
problem: An animal matching background texture still casts a body-shaped shadow inconsistent with flat substrate. Shadow-based camouflage-breaking is documented in biology (countershading counters it) but unused in computational COD.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: explicit shadow-geometry analysis (detecting shadow regions inconsistent with local surface relief implied by the rest of the scene) detects a meaningful subset of camouflaged objects that texture-based models miss entirely, and the two detection channels' errors are near-independent (large ensemble gain).
why_important: An orthogonal physical channel with near-independent errors is the most valuable kind of ensemble component for high-stakes search.
why_possibly_novel: Shadow-consistency reasoning for COD is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Annotate shadow evidence on COD subsets with strong directional light, build shadow-anomaly detector, measure complementary recall.
main_risk: Only works under directional lighting; diffuse-light scenes contribute nothing (operating-envelope caveat).

one_liner: Human-AI teaming for camouflage search: model proposals + human verification exceeds either alone, but only if model uncertainty is exposed.
problem: COD applications are human-in-the-loop (rangers, searchers), yet benchmarks evaluate models solo. Team performance - and what model outputs (masks, heatmaps, uncertainty) maximize it - is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: showing calibrated model heatmaps (not binary masks) roughly doubles human search efficiency on hard camouflage while binary masks INDUCE misses via anchoring (humans stop searching after verifying shown proposals) - output format causally changes team recall, with binary masks the worst choice despite being the field's standard output.
why_important: The deliverable format question affects every deployed search system; anchoring-induced misses are a safety-relevant human-factors failure invisible to model-only evaluation.
why_possibly_novel: Output-format causal study for camouflage search teaming is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Controlled search study (N=30) with format conditions (none/mask/heatmap/uncertainty), measure team recall, time, and anchoring miss rates.
main_risk: Human-subject logistics; effects may depend on searcher expertise (recruit both novices and experts).

one_liner: Model-specific worst-case camouflage synthesis: use texture generation to find each model's blind spots and test whether blindness transfers.
problem: COD evaluates on nature's camouflage, but each model has its own worst-case textures. Whether adversarially-synthesized camouflage transfers across models would reveal if camouflage vulnerability is architectural or universal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-model optimized camouflage textures (differentiable rendering of object surface texture against fixed backgrounds) reduce that model's detection to near zero while remaining human-detectable, and transfer across model families at rates well below adversarial-perturbation transfer - camouflage blind spots are model-specific, unlike pixel-attack vulnerability.
why_important: Maps the difference between perceptual camouflage (universal) and model camouflage (idiosyncratic), with defense implications for anyone relying on automated detection.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-model transferability analysis of synthesized 3D-consistent camouflage is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (adversarial texture work is KNOWN, e.g. adversarial patches/clothing).
minimal_experiment: Optimize textures against 3 detector families in simulation, cross-evaluate the transfer matrix, verify human-visibility with a small study.
main_risk: Simulation-optimized textures may not survive real rendering conditions; physical validation is a larger follow-up.

one_liner: Ambiguous boundaries drift with image resolution: the same object gets objectively different 'correct' boundaries at different scales - boundary GT is scale-relative.
problem: A fuzzy boundary annotated at 4K differs from the same boundary annotated at 512px, not by error but by information availability. Datasets mix annotation scales silently, and evaluation assumes scale-absolute GT.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: annotator boundary placement on ambiguous edges shifts systematically (not just noisily) with viewing resolution - a measurable scale-dependent bias field - and models trained on mixed-resolution annotations learn an average boundary that is optimal at NO resolution, degrading boundary metrics at every scale.
why_important: Establishes that boundary ground truth is scale-relative, forcing resolution metadata into annotation protocols and scale-conditional evaluation - a foundational correction for boundary research.
why_possibly_novel: Scale-relativity of boundary annotation as a measured phenomenon is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Have annotators label identical fuzzy boundaries at 4 zoom levels (order-randomized), quantify systematic placement shifts vs noise.
main_risk: Zoom interfaces confound with interaction affordances (brush size); strict interface control needed.

one_liner: Three-way boundary error decomposition: how much reported boundary error is model, annotation, or metric artifact?
problem: Boundary metrics lump together model mislocalization, annotation imprecision, and rasterization/metric artifacts; the field optimizes the sum without knowing its composition.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on standard benchmarks, at least half of measured boundary error within 3px of GT is attributable to annotation imprecision and rasterization (estimable via multi-annotation and re-rasterization controls), meaning models are closer to the achievable boundary ceiling than metrics suggest and sub-3px 'progress' claims are mostly noise-fitting.
why_important: Recalibrates what boundary improvements are real, and defines the achievable frontier every method should be compared against.
why_possibly_novel: A formal decomposition protocol with published per-benchmark error budgets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-annotate 200 object boundaries at high zoom, estimate annotation noise spectra, propagate through metrics, compare against published method deltas.
main_risk: Extrapolating from 200 objects to benchmark-wide claims needs careful sampling design.

one_liner: Size-stratified reporting flips leaderboards: mIoU improvements of recent methods concentrate entirely in large objects.
problem: mIoU weights pixels, so large objects dominate; two methods with equal mIoU can differ enormously on small objects, and progress claims may hide small-object stagnation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-scoring the last 5 years of leading semantic/panoptic methods with size-stratified metrics shows near-zero progress in the smallest object decile (progress has been large-object progress), and ranking inversions occur for a substantial fraction of published comparisons.
why_important: If small-object performance has been flat while headlines improved, the field has been optimizing a metric artifact - a meta-finding that redirects evaluation practice.
why_possibly_novel: Longitudinal size-stratified meta-analysis of published models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Download 10 public checkpoints spanning 5 years, evaluate size-stratified on ADE20K/Cityscapes, plot per-decile progress curves.
main_risk: Checkpoint availability and preprocessing comparability; must reproduce official numbers first.

one_liner: The upsampling ceiling: bilinear decoder interpolation imposes a hard boundary-sharpness floor that no training can cross.
problem: Virtually all decoders upsample coarse features with smooth interpolation; this architecturally bounds achievable boundary sharpness, but the bound has never been computed and compared with observed errors.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for each common decoder design, there is a computable minimum boundary transition width (from the interpolation kernel and feature stride), observed model boundaries sit AT this floor (not above it), and boundary-error differences between published methods largely reduce to their upsampling-path differences - training and losses are second-order for sharpness.
why_important: Would reduce a confusing literature of boundary methods to an analyzable signal-processing property, telling designers exactly where sharpness comes from.
why_possibly_novel: Analytic sharpness-floor computation validated against model zoo behavior is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Derive floors for 5 decoder designs, measure boundary transition widths of corresponding checkpoints on step-edge probes, test floor-attainment.
main_risk: Learned upsampling components complicate the analysis; treat them as measurable empirical kernels.

one_liner: Thin structures break at regular intervals set by feature stride: connectivity failure is periodic, not random.
problem: Segmented wires, branches, and vessels show gaps. If gaps are periodic (aligned with stride/receptive-field geometry) rather than random, the failure is architectural aliasing with a specific signature and fix path.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the autocorrelation of gap positions along thin structures shows peaks at multiples of the effective feature stride across architectures, and gap probability depends on the structure's sub-stride phase - connectivity failure is deterministic aliasing, falsifiable by phase-shifted re-inference reducing gaps.
why_important: Periodic failure implies cheap test-time fixes (phase ensembling) and indicts stride design rather than data or capacity for a classical failure mode.
why_possibly_novel: Gap-periodicity forensics on thin-structure segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Segment synthetic and real thin structures, compute gap-position autocorrelation vs stride, test phase-jitter ensembling.
main_risk: Multiple strides in pyramidal models blur the periodicity; analyze per-scale contributions.

one_liner: Which boundary errors do humans actually notice? Build the perceptual boundary metric from discrimination experiments.
problem: Boundary metrics (BF-score, boundary IoU) weight all deviations equally, but human observers notice some errors (corner cutting, protrusion loss) far more than others (smooth in/out breathing) - the perceptual weighting is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: human detection thresholds for boundary deviations vary by an order of magnitude across error types (systematic offsets vs high-frequency wiggle vs feature deletion), and a perceptually-weighted metric built from measured thresholds predicts human quality judgments far better than existing boundary metrics - which misrank a meaningful share of comparisons.
why_important: Boundary quality ultimately serves human consumers (editors, clinicians); a psychophysically-grounded metric would reset how boundary progress is scored.
why_possibly_novel: Threshold-measurement-based metric construction for segmentation boundaries is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: 2AFC discrimination study over parameterized boundary distortions, fit threshold model, validate on preference prediction of real model outputs.
main_risk: Perceptual weights may be task-dependent (editing vs measuring); collect per use case.

one_liner: Polygon-vs-pixel ground truth is a hidden treatment: rasterization conventions systematically bias boundary supervision across datasets.
problem: Masks originate as polygons (COCO), brush strokes, or pixel labels, each with different rasterization and corner behavior; models trained across datasets inherit conflicting micro-boundary conventions.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a classifier can identify a mask's annotation tool from boundary micro-statistics alone with high accuracy (tool fingerprints exist), and cross-dataset boundary-metric gaps shrink measurably after fingerprint-normalizing GT - part of 'domain gap' in boundary quality is tooling, not imagery.
why_important: Identifies an ignored confounder in every cross-dataset boundary comparison and offers a normalization remedy.
why_possibly_novel: Annotation-tool fingerprint forensics on mask boundaries is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train tool classifier on masks from datasets with known tooling, apply cross-dataset, re-evaluate transfer gaps after harmonizing rasterization.
main_risk: Tool and content are confounded across datasets; validate fingerprints on same-content multi-tool annotations.

one_liner: For small objects, context carries most of the information: measure the interior-vs-context information ratio as a function of object size.
problem: Small objects have few interior pixels; recognition may rest almost entirely on context. The interior/context information balance as a function of size has not been quantified, though it dictates correct architecture and augmentation choices.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: masking object interiors reduces small-object segmentation accuracy by far less than masking equivalent context rings, with the interior contribution rising steeply above ~32px - a measurable crossover implying sub-crossover objects are 'context-defined' and interior-focused methods are wasted on them.
why_important: Explains why small-object performance resists resolution increases in some regimes, and quantifies exactly what supervision small objects need.
why_possibly_novel: Size-conditional information-source decomposition is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Interior/context masking sweeps across object-size bins on COCO/LVIS, plot information-ratio curves per class family.
main_risk: Masking artifacts; use multiple fill strategies and report agreement.

one_liner: GPU-budget-matched showdown: high-resolution crops vs bigger models for small-object segmentation.
problem: Two competing recipes claim small-object gains - spend compute on resolution (crops, tiling) or on capacity (larger backbones). They are never compared at matched total compute, so the field lacks an exchange rate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched training+inference FLOPs, resolution investment dominates capacity investment for objects below ~2% image area (with a measurable crossover size), and the advantage compounds under domain shift because resolution gains are shift-invariant while capacity gains partially memorize.
why_important: An exchange-rate law between resolution and capacity would guide every deployment with small objects (aerial, medical, defect inspection).
why_possibly_novel: Budget-matched resolution-vs-capacity frontier for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Grid of (resolution, model size) at fixed FLOP budgets on aerial + medical datasets, map iso-compute performance contours vs object size.
main_risk: Conclusions may be architecture-family-specific; replicate across CNN and ViT families.

one_liner: Optimal polygon click budget allocation: where should an annotator spend the next vertex for maximal mask fidelity?
problem: Polygon annotation spends vertices uniformly or by habit, but boundary information density varies enormously along contours (corners vs straight runs); the optimal allocation policy and its savings are unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: curvature-adaptive vertex allocation achieves target boundary fidelity with 30-50% fewer clicks than uniform or annotator-natural allocation (measurable on re-annotation studies), and existing dataset polygons are far from the efficient frontier - quantifying wasted annotation spend at ecosystem scale.
why_important: Annotation budgets are the binding constraint on dataset scale; a proven allocation policy converts directly into more labeled data per dollar.
why_possibly_novel: Information-theoretic vertex-allocation analysis of real datasets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute fidelity-vs-vertex-count curves for optimal (dynamic programming on GT contours) vs actual COCO polygons; run small human study with guided placement.
main_risk: Human motor/attention costs may not follow vertex-count economics; the human study is the decisive leg.

one_liner: Per-class signed boundary bias: models systematically over- or under-segment each class by a constant offset that morphological recalibration removes.
problem: Boundary error is reported as unsigned distance, hiding a possible constant signed bias per class (e.g. 'person' always 2px eroded, 'sky' always dilated) that would be trivially correctable if measured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a large fraction of per-class boundary error is a constant signed offset (bias, not variance) stable across images and datasets for a given model - and per-class morphological recalibration (single dilation/erosion parameter fitted on validation) recovers a large share of boundary-metric error at zero architecture cost.
why_important: Free accuracy lying on the table for every deployed model, plus a diagnostic separating systematic from stochastic boundary behavior.
why_possibly_novel: Signed-bias decomposition with recalibration accounting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Measure per-class signed boundary offsets for 5 public models, fit recalibration on val, report test boundary-metric recovery.
main_risk: Bias may vary with object scale/context, making constant-offset correction too crude - measure the residual structure.

one_liner: Corners are the hardest pixels: boundary error grows superlinearly with local curvature, exposing decoders as low-pass shape filters.
problem: Errors concentrate at high-curvature boundary features (fingertips, leaf tips, corners), consistent with spectral bias, but the error-vs-curvature law and its architecture dependence have not been established.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: boundary displacement error grows superlinearly with local GT curvature, with an architecture-specific cutoff frequency measurable from the error spectrum - CNNs and ViTs show different cutoff signatures, and the cutoff predicts performance on curvature-heavy domains (text, machinery, foliage) better than aggregate metrics.
why_important: A transferable spectral characterization of decoders enables domain-model matching from first principles (measure domain curvature spectrum, pick decoder with adequate cutoff).
why_possibly_novel: Curvature-resolved error laws with spectral cutoffs are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Bin boundary errors by local curvature across model zoo and datasets, fit error-vs-curvature laws, extract cutoffs, validate domain-matching predictions.
main_risk: Curvature estimation on noisy GT is delicate; use analytically-known synthetic shapes as anchors.

one_liner: Uncertainty glint: tiny objects announce themselves as anomalous uncertainty texture even when the class prediction misses them entirely.
problem: Small objects below the detection threshold often leave no trace in hard predictions, but they may perturb the model's uncertainty/feature maps in a detectable way - a second-channel signal for recall recovery.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at locations of missed small objects, per-pixel predictive-entropy neighborhoods have statistically distinct texture (localized entropy spikes) relative to matched background, supporting a recall-recovery detector that finds a meaningful fraction of misses at low false-positive cost - the model 'flinches' where it cannot 'see'.
why_important: Missed small objects are the costliest errors in screening applications; harvesting sub-threshold evidence directly attacks the recall frontier.
why_possibly_novel: Uncertainty-texture mining for sub-threshold objects is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVIS/aerial datasets, extract entropy-map patches at missed-object locations vs matched negatives, train shallow detector, report recall-at-FPR added.
main_risk: Entropy spikes also occur at texture boundaries; the discriminator must beat that base rate.

one_liner: Stuff-stuff boundaries are measure-zero fictions: grass-to-sidewalk transitions are physically bands, and the label model should say so.
problem: Between stuff classes (grass/dirt, sand/water) there is often a mixed transition band, not a curve. Datasets draw arbitrary curves through the band, and models are penalized for reasonable placements within it.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: annotator agreement within stuff-stuff transition bands is near chance (band placement is arbitrary), band widths are measurable and class-pair-specific, and introducing band-aware evaluation (no penalty within measured band) changes stuff-class rankings while leaving thing-class rankings intact - showing current stuff boundary scores are substantially noise.
why_important: Stuff classes dominate scene area; noise-driven rankings there corrupt aggregate metrics that guide the field.
why_possibly_novel: Transition-band measurement and band-aware evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-annotate stuff transitions on ADE/Cityscapes subsets, measure band widths, re-score public models band-aware.
main_risk: Some stuff transitions ARE sharp (curb edges); the method must classify band vs edge cases first.

one_liner: Below the annotation noise floor: SOTA claims on tiny-object benchmarks assert precision the labels cannot support.
problem: For an 8px object, a 1px annotation error swings IoU by tens of points. Benchmarks report tiny-object metrics to decimals without computing the label-noise floor, so some published gains are unfalsifiable.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: propagating measured annotation position noise through IoU for small size bins yields uncertainty intervals wider than most published method-to-method gaps in those bins - a decisive fraction of tiny-object SOTA claims are statistically vacuous, and the community's smallest evaluable object size is derivable per dataset.
why_important: Defines the epistemic limit of small-object benchmarking and prevents wasted effort chasing noise.
why_possibly_novel: Noise-floor-derived minimum-evaluable-size analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate annotation jitter from double-labeled subsets, Monte-Carlo propagate through size-binned metrics, overlay published deltas.
main_risk: Jitter estimates from small double-labeled samples have their own uncertainty; report meta-intervals.

one_liner: Sub-stride phase determines tiny-object visibility: shifting the image by 8 pixels changes which small objects a model finds.
problem: Feature-map stride quantizes where evidence lands; a tiny object's alignment with the stride grid (its phase) may decide detection - implying single-pass evaluation undercounts model capability and phase-TTA recovers it.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-object detection outcomes for sub-stride objects flip with input translation at rates far above large-object rates (phase sensitivity), aggregate phase-averaged recall exceeds single-phase recall substantially, and phase sensitivity per architecture is predictable from its stride pyramid - a deterministic, correctable component of small-object failure.
why_important: Distinguishes 'cannot represent' from 'unlucky alignment', with an immediately usable inference fix and a design principle (anti-aliased strides) validated by the phase signature.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic phase-sensitivity accounting for small-object segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (shift-variance of CNNs in general is KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Translate test images over a stride-period grid, measure per-object outcome flip rates by size, evaluate phase-ensembled recall.
main_risk: Border effects from translation; use central-crop evaluation regions.

one_liner: Shadow edges poison boundary supervision: models trained with gradient-aligned boundary rewards learn to follow illumination, not objects.
problem: Many pipelines sharpen boundaries using image gradients (CRF-style refinement, edge-guided training). Shadow edges are strong gradients that do not bound objects; the systematic confusion rate this induces is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models with gradient-coupled boundary refinement place object boundaries onto shadow edges at measurably higher rates than gradient-free models (a shadow-following bias), and the bias grows with refinement strength - quantifying a hidden cost of a ubiquitous technique and predicting its failure in harsh-light domains (aerial noon imagery, surgical lighting).
why_important: CRF/edge-guidance is folklore-good; measuring its shadow tax would qualify decades of accepted practice with domain-specific guidance.
why_possibly_novel: Shadow-specific failure accounting of gradient-based refinement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate shadow-crossing object boundaries, compare boundary placement of refined vs unrefined variants of the same models, sweep refinement strength.
main_risk: Isolating refinement as the only difference requires careful model surgery; use toggleable refinement implementations.

one_liner: Hairline cracks defeat both training and evaluation: 1-pixel objects need sub-pixel offset-field formulations, not masks.
problem: Infrastructure cracks, cell membranes, and hairline defects are ~1px structures where binary masks cannot even represent the target faithfully, yet the field forces mask formulations onto them.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: representing thin structures as sub-pixel center-line + width fields (continuous offsets) instead of binary masks improves BOTH detection recall and downstream measurement accuracy (crack width estimation) at matched supervision cost, because the continuous formulation matches the object's actual dimensionality - falsifiable by direct formulation comparison.
why_important: Thin-structure measurement is an economically huge application (infrastructure inspection) currently served by a mismatched formulation.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: center-line representations exist in vessel literature; the sub-pixel measurement-accuracy comparison against mask formulations at matched supervision is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On crack datasets with caliper-measured widths, train mask vs offset-field formulations, compare detection and physical-measurement error.
main_risk: Requires physically-measured GT (width calipers); small but real collection effort.

one_liner: Depth-of-field is a per-pixel boundary-sharpness oracle that models ignore: defocused boundaries deserve wide predictions, focused ones sharp.
problem: Within one photo, optical defocus varies boundary sharpness continuously, but models emit uniform-sharpness boundaries everywhere - a mismatch between optics and output that nobody exploits or measures.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: model boundary error correlates strongly with local defocus (measurable via blur estimation), models do NOT modulate their boundary confidence with defocus (uniform sharpness output), and defocus-conditioned evaluation reveals current boundary metrics penalize physically-inevitable uncertainty as if it were model error.
why_important: Separates optical information limits from model limits per pixel, enabling fairer evaluation and defocus-aware outputs for editing applications.
why_possibly_novel: Defocus-conditioned boundary analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate local blur on benchmark images, bin boundary errors by blur level, test whether model confidence tracks blur.
main_risk: Blur estimation errors propagate; use focal-stack captures with known defocus as calibration.

one_liner: Contour-domain error autocorrelation reveals each decoder's effective receptive field along boundaries - a fingerprint measurable without internals.
problem: How far boundary errors correlate ALONG the contour (error wavelength) encodes the decoder's spatial coupling, but boundary evaluation collapses everything to scalars, discarding this diagnostic structure.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the autocorrelation length of signed boundary error along contours is a stable architecture fingerprint (invariant across datasets, distinct across model families), predicts which post-processing helps (short-wavelength errors respond to smoothing, long-wavelength to re-recognition), and can identify anonymous model families from outputs alone.
why_important: Gives practitioners a black-box diagnostic that prescribes the right fix, and gives forensics a model-attribution tool.
why_possibly_novel: Contour-frequency-domain error analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute along-contour error spectra for 8 public models over 3 datasets, test cross-dataset stability and family separability.
main_risk: Contour parameterization ambiguities at junctions; restrict to simple closed contours initially.

one_liner: Upstream JPEG kills small objects before the model ever sees them: pipeline compression bounds recall independent of model quality.
problem: Data pipelines (dashcams, drones, cloud upload) compress images before inference; tiny low-contrast objects may be erased at the compression stage, making model improvements irrelevant - yet compression is absent from benchmark methodology.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for objects under ~12px, realistic pipeline compression (bitrates of deployed dashcams/drones) removes recoverable evidence for a large fraction of instances (verified by human inspection of decompressed crops), establishing a compression-determined recall ceiling that no model surpasses - and benchmark images, being lightly compressed, systematically overstate deployable recall.
why_important: Redirects small-object investment toward capture/codec policy where the recall is actually lost, with quantitative ceilings per bitrate.
why_possibly_novel: Compression-ceiling accounting for small-object segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-compress benchmarks at deployment bitrates, measure model + human recall ceilings vs original, tabulate evidence destruction per size bin.
main_risk: Codec diversity (H.264/H.265/AV1) requires a matrix, not a single number.

one_liner: Attribute the small-object gap: with oracle localization, is segmentation of small objects actually solved?
problem: Small-object segmentation failure conflates finding (localization) and delineating (mask quality). The conditional performance - mask quality GIVEN correct localization - isolates which stage fails.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: conditioned on oracle boxes, small-object mask quality is close to large-object mask quality (normalized for pixel count), so the small-object problem is >80% a search/detection problem, not a segmentation problem - implying segmentation-architecture work on small objects is largely misdirected.
why_important: Cleanly splits a conflated problem and reallocates effort to the failing stage (search strategies, high-recall proposals).
why_possibly_novel: Stage-conditional gap attribution for small objects is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate promptable and two-stage models with GT-box prompts across size bins, compare conditional mask quality profiles.
main_risk: Normalizing mask quality across sizes is subtle (IoU size-sensitivity); use boundary-normalized metrics.

one_liner: Decompose boundary uncertainty into normal and tangential components: only normal errors matter, and metrics that mix them misrank methods.
problem: Boundary deviations perpendicular to the contour (position error) change the region; deviations along it (parameterization wiggle) often do not matter - yet distance-based boundary metrics penalize both indiscriminately.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: decomposing boundary error into normal/tangential components shows the tangential component contributes substantial metric variance while being nearly uncorrelated with human quality judgments and downstream task success - normal-only metrics agree better with both, and re-scoring benchmarks with them changes method orderings.
why_important: A geometrically-principled metric correction that removes a systematic noise source from all boundary evaluation.
why_possibly_novel: Normal/tangential decomposition for segmentation evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement decomposed metrics, re-score model zoo, correlate both components with human preferences from a small study.
main_risk: Correspondence between predicted and GT contours is ambiguous at large errors; define robust matching first.

one_liner: Instance merging obeys a crowding law: adjacent-instance merge probability is a universal function of gap-to-size ratio, like human visual crowding.
problem: Dense instances (cells, crowds, grapes) get merged by segmenters. If merge probability follows a universal law in dimensionless gap/size units - analogous to crowding in human peripheral vision (KNOWN: Bouma's law) - dense-scene capability could be predicted and compared principledly.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: merge probability across models and domains collapses onto a single curve in (gap/object-size, contrast) coordinates with model-specific scale factors - a 'machine Bouma law' - enabling dataset-independent dense-scene capability ratings and principled prediction of failure density in novel domains.
why_important: Universal laws compress messy benchmarks into transferable engineering constants; a crowding constant per model would be a durable, comparable capability spec.
why_possibly_novel: Dimensionless-collapse analysis of instance merging is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Measure merge rates on synthetic instance grids (controlled gap/size/contrast) plus cell/crowd datasets, test curve collapse across 5 models.
main_risk: Real-scene occlusion patterns may break the two-parameter description; add occlusion fraction as third axis if needed.

one_liner: Models have a blob prior: error statistics reveal systematic shape simplification toward compact blobs, measurable as a shape-frequency transfer function.
problem: Predictions tend toward smoother, rounder shapes than GT, but 'shape simplification' has never been characterized as a transfer function (which shape frequencies are attenuated how much) that would make the bias precisely correctable and comparable.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: comparing shape-descriptor spectra (elliptic Fourier coefficients) of predictions vs GT yields a stable per-model attenuation curve (the blob-prior transfer function), consistent across datasets, whose inverse partially restores fine shape structure post hoc - shape bias is a measurable filter, not a vague tendency.
why_important: Converts a folklore bias into an engineering object (measurable, invertible, comparable across models) with direct value for shape-critical applications (typography, machining, biology morphometrics).
why_possibly_novel: Transfer-function characterization of segmentation shape bias is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute EFD spectra ratios prediction/GT per model, verify cross-dataset stability, test spectral re-inflation on held-out data.
main_risk: Inversion amplifies noise along with signal; regularized inversion needed and honest failure reporting.

one_liner: Photograph printed calibration shapes to get camera-true boundary ground truth with exact sub-pixel geometry - the first zero-annotation boundary benchmark.
problem: All boundary evaluation inherits annotation noise. Printing precisely-known vector shapes, photographing them under controlled conditions, and registering the known geometry yields ground truth with certainty no annotator can provide - yet no such benchmark exists for segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a physically-photographed benchmark of exactly-known shapes (varying size, curvature, contrast, blur, texture) will reveal sub-pixel systematic biases of segmentation models (chromatic offsets, contrast-dependent placement, curvature attenuation) that are invisible on annotated data because they are smaller than annotation noise - opening a metrology-grade regime of boundary science.
why_important: Establishes an absolute measurement foundation the entire boundary literature lacks; every sharpness/bias claim becomes precisely testable.
why_possibly_novel: Metrology-style physical-ground-truth benchmarks for segmentation are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (camera calibration targets are KNOWN but serve geometry, not segmentation evaluation).
minimal_experiment: Print vector shape set, photograph across cameras/lighting/scales, register via fiducials, evaluate model zoo at sub-pixel precision.
main_risk: Printed shapes are unnatural stimuli; complement with textured/embedded variants to test ecological validity.

one_liner: Pixel entropy does not predict object-level failure: the granularity mismatch at the heart of segmentation uncertainty.
problem: Uncertainty is produced per-pixel but consumed per-object (is THIS lesion trustworthy?). Whether pixel-level uncertainty aggregates into valid object-level confidence has not been rigorously tested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: standard aggregations of pixel uncertainty (mean/max entropy over mask) predict object-level errors (misses, hallucinations, gross misshaping) only weakly (AUROC<0.7), because object failures are correlated-error events invisible to independent-pixel statistics - and object-level failure needs its own predictor trained on object-level outcomes.
why_important: Every clinical/industrial consumer needs object-level confidence; if the standard recipe is invalid, the field's uncertainty outputs are decorative.
why_possibly_novel: Granularity-mismatch quantification for segmentation uncertainty is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On 3 datasets, compute pixel-aggregate vs learned object-level confidence, compare AUROC for object-failure prediction.
main_risk: Learned object-level predictors may overfit failure modes of specific models; test cross-model transfer.

one_liner: Calibration degrades before accuracy under distribution shift: miscalibration as an early-warning canary for silent segmentation failure.
problem: Deployed models fail silently under gradual shift (weather, sensor aging). If calibration metrics degrade earlier along shift gradients than accuracy does, they provide label-free advance warning - the lead-lag relationship is unmeasured for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: along parameterized shift ladders (fog density, noise level, geography), expected calibration error inflects at milder shift levels than mIoU does (a measurable lead), and the lead size is consistent enough to define actionable monitoring thresholds - calibration is the canary, not just a companion metric.
why_important: Label-free failure forecasting is the missing piece of deployment monitoring; a validated lead-lag law would be immediately adopted.
why_possibly_novel: Lead-lag analysis of calibration vs accuracy under graded shift is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate models along synthetic and natural shift ladders (ACDC severity levels), plot ECE and mIoU inflection points, quantify lead consistency.
main_risk: ECE estimation needs labels too; the deployment version must use proxy calibration signals (agreement-based), adding a validation step.

one_liner: Instance count, not pixel count, governs long-tail segmentation: disentangle the two supervision currencies.
problem: Rare-class performance is attributed to 'few pixels', but classes vary independently in instances-per-class and pixels-per-instance; which currency actually buys performance is confounded in natural datasets.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched total pixels, many-small-instances classes substantially outperform few-large-instances classes (instance diversity teaches shape/context variation that pixel volume cannot), with a measurable exchange rate - so long-tail interventions should target instance acquisition, not pixel acquisition.
why_important: Directly changes data-collection strategy for rare classes (many quick examples beat few thorough ones), a high-leverage economics result.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled pixel-vs-instance supervision disentanglement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Subsample LVIS classes into matched-pixel/varied-instance and matched-instance/varied-pixel grids, train and compare per-class outcomes.
main_risk: Class semantics confound (small-instance classes differ in kind); use within-class subsampling designs.

one_liner: Measure the labeling ROI of uncertainty-routed annotation: does model uncertainty actually direct human effort to where it pays?
problem: Uncertainty-guided active labeling is widely assumed beneficial, but for segmentation the regions models are uncertain about (boundaries, ambiguous textures) may be exactly where human labels are ALSO noisy - buying little.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: routing annotation to high-model-uncertainty regions yields lower marginal model improvement per annotation-hour than routing to high-DISAGREEMENT-between-models regions, because self-uncertainty concentrates on irreducibly ambiguous pixels while cross-model disagreement marks learnable errors - an economics experiment with a counter-intuitive predicted winner.
why_important: Annotation routing policies move real budgets; identifying the right routing signal has direct multiplicative value across the industry.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head routing-signal comparison measured in Dice-per-hour is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Fixed-budget annotation simulation plus small real-annotator study comparing routing signals on a medical and a driving dataset.
main_risk: Results may depend on annotator skill and label noise model; report across annotator pools.

one_liner: Ensemble disagreement decomposes into boundary jitter vs semantic conflict, and only the second predicts real failure.
problem: Deep-ensemble disagreement for segmentation mixes two phenomena: small spatial jitter of agreed boundaries, and genuine semantic conflicts (different labels/regions). Treating them as one scalar wastes the signal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: after registering member boundaries (factoring out sub-3px jitter), the residual semantic-conflict component predicts object-level errors and OOD inputs far better than raw disagreement, while the jitter component tracks stimulus edge blur - two useful signals recoverable from one ensemble by simple decomposition.
why_important: Upgrades the most common uncertainty tool for dense prediction at zero training cost, and explains why raw ensemble variance underperforms expectations.
why_possibly_novel: Jitter/conflict decomposition of segmentation ensembles is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Decompose disagreement for a 5-member ensemble on clean and shifted data, compare failure-prediction AUROC of components vs raw variance.
main_risk: Registration of member boundaries is nontrivial at large conflicts - exactly where it matters; needs robust matching.

one_liner: The abstention cliff: models never predict classes below a training-frequency threshold, and the threshold is predictable from loss geometry.
problem: Rare classes are not just less accurate - below some frequency, models predict them literally never (silent class death). The location and universality of this cliff is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-class prediction frequency vs training frequency shows a sharp cliff (not smooth decline) at a threshold determined by the class's feature-space overlap with head classes, consistent across architectures - class death is a phase transition predictable from data statistics, and no amount of training-length increase revives dead classes.
why_important: Practitioners assume more training or mild reweighting recovers rare classes; a documented death threshold with a predictor would change how teams triage the long tail.
why_possibly_novel: Class-death phase-transition characterization for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Frequency-ladder subsampling of LVIS/ADE classes across seeds, map prediction-frequency cliffs, regress thresholds on feature-overlap measures.
main_risk: Cliff position may drift with loss/sampler choices used in practice; map across common configurations.

one_liner: Conformal inner-outer mask pairs: distribution-free coverage guarantees for segmentation, tested for usability where it matters.
problem: Conformal prediction offers guaranteed-coverage regions, which for masks naturally become nested inner (surely-object) and outer (possibly-object) contours - but whether achievable interval widths are narrow enough to be USEFUL in real tasks is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: conformalized inner/outer mask pairs achieve nominal coverage with width overheads small enough for radiotherapy-margin and robot-grasp use in most cases (median annulus width under 15% of object diameter), but widths blow up predictably on ambiguity-heavy classes - producing the first usability map of conformal segmentation.
why_important: Guarantees without usability are academic; a domain-by-domain width atlas tells practitioners where conformal methods are deployable today.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: conformal segmentation papers exist; the usability-atlas framing with task-anchored width thresholds is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement split-conformal masks on medical + driving datasets, tabulate coverage and width distributions against task-derived width budgets.
main_risk: Exchangeability violations under shift void guarantees; report shift sensitivity honestly.

one_liner: Anomaly-segmentation benchmarks are boundary detectors in disguise: SOTA methods flag object-background transitions, not anomalies.
problem: Road-anomaly benchmarks reward high anomaly scores on unusual objects; but if methods' scores concentrate on ALL boundaries (of normal objects too), leaderboard success may reflect boundary-affinity, not anomaly understanding.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for leading anomaly-segmentation methods, a large fraction of their positive signal lies within thin bands around object boundaries (normal or anomalous alike), and a boundary-band-excluded re-evaluation collapses the leaderboard while a simple interior-focused baseline climbs - current metrics conflate edge-awareness with anomaly detection.
why_important: Anomaly segmentation feeds safety cases in driving; knowing whether methods detect anomalies or just edges is not optional.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-band ablation audits of anomaly benchmarks are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-score public anomaly methods with boundary-band exclusion on SegmentMeIfYouCan-style data, quantify rank changes.
main_risk: Some anomaly signal legitimately lives at boundaries; interpret with both included/excluded views.

one_liner: Validate the aleatoric/epistemic decomposition against ground truth ambiguity: at boundaries, current methods conflate what they claim to separate.
problem: Methods claim to separate data uncertainty (aleatoric) from model uncertainty (epistemic), but both explode at boundaries, and no one validates the decomposition against measured stimulus ambiguity (annotator variance) and measured model ignorance (OOD-ness).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at object boundaries, reported aleatoric and epistemic maps correlate with each other far more than either correlates with its ground-truth referent (annotator variance for aleatoric, holdout-domain error for epistemic) - the decomposition largely fails exactly where uncertainty is largest, and honest evaluation requires referent-anchored validation.
why_important: The decomposition justifies real decisions (collect more data vs accept ambiguity); if it is invalid at boundaries, those decisions are misinformed.
why_possibly_novel: Referent-anchored validation of the decomposition for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On multi-annotator datasets with OOD splits, correlate each uncertainty type with its referent at boundary vs interior pixels.
main_risk: Referents are imperfect proxies; triangulate with multiple referent definitions.

one_liner: Miscalibration direction flips between head and tail classes: one temperature cannot fix a structured, sign-changing bias.
problem: Segmentation calibration is usually addressed with global temperature scaling, implicitly assuming uniform miscalibration; class-conditional structure (overconfident on rare, underconfident on common, or the reverse) is undocumented.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-class calibration curves show a systematic sign flip along the frequency axis (head classes underconfident, tail classes overconfident, driven by loss dynamics and label noise asymmetries), so global temperature scaling worsens one end - and the flip point is predictable from class frequency and co-occurrence entropy.
why_important: A sign-changing bias makes the standard remedy actively harmful for part of the label space - important for any consumer of segmentation confidences.
why_possibly_novel: Frequency-resolved calibration-sign analysis for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute per-class reliability diagrams on ADE/LVIS models, locate sign structure, test global-vs-per-class temperature consequences.
main_risk: Per-class calibration estimates are noisy for the rarest classes; use hierarchical estimation.

one_liner: Are tumor-volume confidence intervals valid? Propagate segmentation uncertainty into derived clinical quantities and test empirical coverage.
problem: Downstream users consume derived scalars (volumes, diameters, areas) with error bars produced from pixel uncertainties under independence assumptions that boundary-correlated errors violate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: volume CIs computed under pixel-independence are anti-conservative by 2-5x (empirical coverage far below nominal) because boundary errors are long-range correlated, and correlation-aware propagation (sampling coherent boundary perturbations) restores near-nominal coverage without model changes - a purely statistical fix to a clinically dangerous underestimate.
why_important: Treatment monitoring uses volume changes; overconfident CIs can turn measurement noise into false progression/response calls.
why_possibly_novel: Coverage-validated propagation for segmentation-derived scalars is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-rater or synthetic-GT lesion data: compare nominal vs empirical coverage across propagation schemes and uncertainty methods.
main_risk: Requires trustworthy reference volumes; synthetic-lesion anchoring mitigates.

one_liner: Region-level selective prediction dominates image-level: reject the 5% of regions causing 50% of risk instead of whole images.
problem: Selective prediction for segmentation typically abstains per-image, discarding mostly-correct outputs; per-region abstention could retain value while excising risk, but its operating curves are unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: risk-coverage curves for region-level abstention strictly dominate image-level abstention by large margins across datasets (same risk at 3-5x higher coverage), and the optimal rejection granularity (region size) is predictable from the spatial autocorrelation of errors - a complete recipe for deployable selective segmentation.
why_important: Converts selective prediction from an academic exercise into a practical tool: most of the image is usually fine.
why_possibly_novel: Granularity-optimized selective segmentation with dominance quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build risk-coverage curves at multiple abstention granularities on medical + driving models, verify dominance and granularity predictor.
main_risk: Region abstention needs downstream handling protocols (what fills rejected holes) - application-specific.

one_liner: Do uncertainty overlays help or hypnotize? Measure over-reliance dynamics when clinicians see model confidence maps.
problem: Uncertainty visualization is assumed to improve human oversight, but confidence maps could induce automation bias (trusting confident-but-wrong regions MORE) - the behavioral effect is unmeasured for segmentation review.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: showing uncertainty overlays reduces human error-catch rates in high-confidence-but-wrong regions (attention is captured by flagged areas, unflagged errors get a pass) while improving catch rates in flagged areas - net effect on total misses can be NEGATIVE when model calibration is poor, making overlay deployment conditional on calibration quality.
why_important: A pre-deployment behavioral law (when overlays help vs harm) is needed before uncertainty visualization becomes standard in clinical tools.
why_possibly_novel: Automation-bias quantification for segmentation uncertainty display is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (automation bias in general is KNOWN in human factors).
minimal_experiment: Controlled review study: radiology trainees correct model masks with/without overlays where some errors are confident; measure catch rates by condition.
main_risk: Human-subject study logistics; effects may vary with expertise level (include as factor).

one_liner: Context prior vs class prior in the tail: rare classes fail because their contexts are rare, not because their appearance is unlearned.
problem: Rare-class failure is attributed to insufficient appearance examples, but rare classes also occupy rare contexts; the two deficits (appearance model vs context prior) have different remedies and are never separated.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: pasting rare-class instances into common contexts recovers a large fraction of their segmentation accuracy (context prior dominates appearance deficit), while common classes pasted into rare contexts degrade sharply - most 'long-tail appearance learning' framing misattributes a context-prior problem, redirecting fixes toward context-decorrelated training.
why_important: Copy-paste augmentation works (KNOWN empirically); this explains WHY and predicts when it will not (appearance-limited classes), converting a trick into a diagnostic-driven method.
why_possibly_novel: Context/appearance deficit decomposition via bidirectional pasting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Bidirectional paste experiments on LVIS tail/head classes, decompose error recovery by manipulation direction.
main_risk: Pasting artifacts help models detect pasted objects; use high-quality harmonization and artifact controls.

one_liner: TTA-disagreement as epistemic proxy fails exactly under systematic shift: characterize the validity boundary of consistency-based uncertainty.
problem: Test-time-augmentation disagreement is a popular free uncertainty signal, but under systematic shift all augmented views are fooled identically, silencing the alarm precisely when needed - the validity envelope is unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: TTA-disagreement tracks error well under stochastic corruptions (noise, blur) but decouples under systematic shifts (new sensor, new geography) with near-zero failure-prediction power there - and the decoupling is detectable ONLINE via disagreement-distribution shape, giving a self-diagnosing uncertainty signal that knows when it is blind.
why_important: Prevents dangerous false confidence in the cheapest uncertainty method, and the self-diagnosis extension rescues its deployability.
why_possibly_novel: Validity-envelope mapping with online self-diagnosis for TTA uncertainty is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Correlate TTA-disagreement with error across stochastic vs systematic shift suites; test distribution-shape detector for decoupling onset.
main_risk: The taxonomy stochastic-vs-systematic is fuzzy at edges; define operationally by augmentation-space coverage.

one_liner: Top-2 logit margin at each pixel is a free boundary-ambiguity map: validate it against annotator disagreement without any uncertainty machinery.
problem: Models already compute per-pixel class margins; whether this zero-cost signal matches human boundary ambiguity as well as expensive Bayesian machinery does has never been benchmarked head-to-head.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the top-2 margin map correlates with annotator disagreement maps nearly as strongly as deep ensembles do (within 10% of ensemble correlation) at 1/Nth the cost, but ONLY for in-distribution boundary ambiguity - establishing a practical uncertainty hierarchy: margins for boundaries, ensembles for OOD, nothing extra needed in between.
why_important: A validated cost-capability hierarchy stops teams from paying ensemble costs for boundary questions margins already answer.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head referent-anchored comparison of margin vs ensemble for boundary ambiguity is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On multi-annotator data, correlate margin maps and ensemble maps with disagreement; stratify by in/out-of-distribution condition.
main_risk: Margins are miscalibrated per-class (see frequency sign-flip idea); may need per-class normalization to shine.

one_liner: Semantically-weighted confusion: wrong-but-adjacent (car-truck) vs wrong-and-absurd (car-sky) errors have identical metric cost but wildly different consequences - measure the absurdity distribution.
problem: Confusion severity is flat in all standard metrics. The distribution of error 'semantic distance' - and whether newer models err more reasonably - is unmeasured, though consumers care mostly about absurd errors.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models with similar mIoU differ up to severalfold in absurd-error rates (semantic distance above safety thresholds), the absurdity rate is NOT monotonically improved by scale or recency (some new models err more absurdly), and absurdity-weighted rankings disagree with mIoU rankings enough to matter for safety-driven selection.
why_important: Safety cases hinge on worst-case severity, not average overlap; an absurdity metric with published model profiles fills a real selection gap.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic absurdity-distribution profiling of segmentation models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (hierarchical metrics exist but adoption-focused profiling of the model zoo does not, to my knowledge).
minimal_experiment: Define semantic distance via ontology + human severity ratings, profile 10 public models, compare rankings vs mIoU.
main_risk: Semantic distance definition is contestable; validate against human severity judgments.

one_liner: Near-duplicate training images create overconfidence pockets: data attribution for segmentation miscalibration.
problem: Web-scraped training sets contain near-duplicate clusters; models see some visual patterns many times, plausibly producing spatially-localized overconfidence unrelated to true reliability - a data-side cause of miscalibration nobody audits.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: test-image regions visually similar to high-duplication training clusters show systematically inflated confidence at equal accuracy (an overconfidence pocket signature), and deduplicated retraining flattens these pockets - a measurable causal path from data redundancy to calibration structure.
why_important: Connects dataset hygiene to trustworthiness (not just accuracy), giving calibration auditors a new data-side lever.
why_possibly_novel: Duplication-conditioned calibration analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Cluster training data by similarity, map test-time confidence vs nearest-cluster duplication level, retrain deduplicated for the causal leg.
main_risk: Similarity-to-training measurement is itself model-dependent; use external embedding for neutrality.

one_liner: What hides in ignore regions? Benchmarks' void labels conceal systematic model failures that count in deployment.
problem: Evaluation protocols exclude 'void/ignore' pixels (ambiguous, boundary, unlabeled regions). Models are unconstrained there, and deployment consumes those predictions anyway - what models actually emit in ignored zones is undocumented.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: within ignore regions, model predictions are strongly model-specific and often absurd (class flicker, impossible layouts), inter-model agreement collapses (revealing that supervision, not learning, was constraining them), and downstream metrics that consume full maps (planning, rendering) degrade measurably due to ignore-zone behavior invisible to benchmarks.
why_important: The gap between evaluated pixels and consumed pixels is a silent deployment liability; quantifying it forces protocol honesty.
why_possibly_novel: Ignore-region behavioral audit is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Extract ignore-region predictions from public models on Cityscapes/ADE, measure inter-model agreement and downstream-task sensitivity to those zones.
main_risk: No GT there by definition; evaluation must use consistency, plausibility, and downstream proxies.

one_liner: Sub-10-example classes are retrieval, not generalization: feature-space nearest-neighbor tests reveal the memorization regime of the extreme tail.
problem: Classes with a handful of training instances still show nonzero test performance; whether this reflects generalization or disguised memorization (matching near-identical training instances) determines whether extreme-tail scores mean anything.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for classes under ~10 training instances, test-set successes overwhelmingly occur on test instances with near-duplicate training matches (feature distance below a threshold), and success probability drops toward zero as match distance grows - extreme-tail performance is retrieval performance, and benchmark tails measure dataset redundancy rather than model capability.
why_important: Recalibrates every long-tail leaderboard's bottom decile and separates two capabilities (retrieval vs generalization) that current metrics blend.
why_possibly_novel: Match-distance-conditioned success analysis for tail segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For LVIS rare classes, compute per-test-instance nearest-training distances, plot success vs distance, compare against head-class curves.
main_risk: Feature space choice affects distance; replicate across embeddings.

one_liner: Uncertainty as the first sensor to fail: under gradual weather degradation, which uncertainty signal rises first, and does its order match accuracy decline?
problem: Multi-signal uncertainty stacks (entropy, margin, ensembles, TTA) are compared on static benchmarks, but deployment needs to know their ONSET ORDER under gradually worsening conditions - who warns first, who warns falsely.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: signals have a reproducible onset ordering along weather-degradation trajectories (e.g. ensemble disagreement first, entropy last), the ordering is stable across scenes but differs across shift types, and combining onset order with signal levels identifies the shift TYPE label-free - uncertainty dynamics carry diagnostic information that static levels discard.
why_important: Deployment monitoring needs early, interpretable alarms; onset-order fingerprints add a diagnosis capability to mere detection.
why_possibly_novel: Temporal onset-order analysis of uncertainty signals is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Drive models along graded weather ladders (synthetic + ACDC), record all signals, test ordering stability and shift-type classification.
main_risk: Graded natural weather data is limited; synthetic gradients must be validated against natural anchor points.
