one_liner: Confidence dilutes with vocabulary size in open-vocabulary segmentation: a predictable law makes scores incomparable across vocabularies.
problem: Open-vocabulary models score each pixel against arbitrary user-supplied class lists; adding distractor classes necessarily redistributes probability mass, so confidence (and thresholded decisions) depend on vocabulary size - a structural effect nobody models or corrects.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-pixel confidence for the true class decays with vocabulary size following a predictable law (driven by embedding-space crowding around the true class), decision flips under vocabulary growth concentrate on tail/ambiguous classes, and a crowding-aware confidence normalization restores vocabulary-invariant behavior - fixing silent incomparability across deployments.
why_important: Open-vocabulary models are deployed with wildly different class lists; vocabulary-dependent behavior means the same model+image gives different answers by list choice - users deserve a characterization and correction.
why_possibly_novel: Vocabulary-scaling laws for dense open-vocabulary confidence are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep vocabulary sizes with controlled distractor sampling on OV segmentation models, fit decay laws, test normalization for invariance.
main_risk: Distractor choice affects the law's parameters; characterize semantic-proximity dependence explicitly.

one_liner: Seed-churn maps: pixels that flip between training runs form a free, model-intrinsic ambiguity atlas that matches human disagreement.
problem: Retraining with different seeds flips predictions on specific pixels (churn). This intrinsic instability is treated as noise, but its spatial structure may encode exactly the stimulus ambiguity that expensive uncertainty methods try to estimate.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: pixelwise churn across 5-10 seeds correlates with human annotator disagreement as strongly as deep-ensemble variance does (they are near-duplicate signals), churn maps are stable dataset properties (transferable across architectures), and published per-method 'improvements' concentrate suspiciously on high-churn pixels - simultaneously offering a cheap ambiguity atlas and a benchmark-noise audit tool.
why_important: One artifact (churn atlas) serves three uses: free uncertainty referent, benchmark noise floor, and reproducibility diagnostics for claimed gains.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: churn is studied in classification; dense churn atlases with the benchmark-audit application are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train 10 seeds of 2 architectures on Cityscapes, build churn atlases, correlate with multi-annotator data, overlay published method deltas.
main_risk: Compute cost of multi-seed training (moderate); mitigated by using smaller proxy models if transfer holds.

one_liner: Rare-context hallucination: models paint plausible-but-absent stuff classes (water under bridges, sky through gaps) driven by context priors overpowering evidence.
problem: Segmentation errors are usually studied as misclassification of present things; systematic hallucination of ABSENT classes in strongly-suggestive contexts (context-completion errors) is unquantified for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in contexts statistically associated with a class (bridge implies water below), models predict the associated class at measurable rates even when it is verifiably absent, the hallucination rate scales with context-class association strength mined from training co-occurrence, and evidence-ablation shows these pixels rely on context, not appearance - dense prediction has a measurable prior-override failure mode analogous to LLM hallucination.
why_important: Establishes hallucination as a quantifiable dense-prediction phenomenon with a data-statistics predictor - relevant for safety and for understanding context integration generally.
why_possibly_novel: Context-completion hallucination quantification for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Curate context-strong/class-absent images (dry canals, drained pools, bridges over roads), measure per-model hallucination vs mined association strength.
main_risk: Verifying true absence needs careful curation; some cases are genuinely ambiguous from single views.

one_liner: The tail is where annotation noise lives: rare-class 'errors' are disproportionately label errors, making measured tail performance a lower bound with a computable correction.
problem: Rare classes are annotated by workers with less exposure and lower agreement; model 'failures' there may substantially be annotator failures, systematically understating true tail capability.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert re-audit of model-GT disagreements will show the label-fault rate rising steeply from head to tail classes (annotator unfamiliarity effect), and correcting evaluated labels compresses the head-tail performance gap substantially - part of the long-tail problem is a long-tail-of-annotation-quality problem, with different implied remedies.
why_important: If the tail gap is partly measurement artifact, expensive tail-focused training methods are being judged against corrupted references - the field should fix references before methods.
why_possibly_novel: Frequency-resolved label-error auditing for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (classification label-error work is KNOWN: Northcutt et al.).
minimal_experiment: Sample model-GT disagreements across frequency deciles on LVIS, expert-adjudicate 2k cases, fit fault-rate vs frequency, re-estimate corrected gaps.
main_risk: Expert adjudication is itself imperfect for genuinely ambiguous tail categories; use multi-expert panels.

one_liner: Real crowdworker clicks vs simulated clicks: quantify the sim2real prompting gap that inflates every interactive segmentation benchmark.
problem: Interactive segmentation is evaluated with simulators (click at center of largest error). Real users click by salience, habit, and motor economy; the distribution gap and its score inflation are unmeasured for general annotators.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: replayed real-user click sessions yield measurably worse NoC/IoU curves than simulator evaluation for the same models (inflation >20% in clicks-to-target), and models RANK differently under real clicks - some architectures are robust to human click styles, others are simulator-tuned.
why_important: If rankings flip under real usage, years of interactive-segmentation comparisons need re-reading, and future evaluation must include click-style robustness.
why_possibly_novel: A public real-click corpus with replay evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Collect 2k real click sessions via crowdsourcing on COCO objects, replay against 5 models, compare with simulator curves.
main_risk: Interface design shapes click behavior; use multiple interface variants to bound the effect.

one_liner: Information-per-second of annotation primitives: clicks vs scribbles vs boxes vs verbal corrections, measured properly for once.
problem: Annotation-efficiency papers compare supervision types by count (10 clicks vs 1 box), not by human time and cognitive cost - the actual currency. The efficiency ordering may invert under time-based accounting.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under wall-clock accounting with real annotators, scribbles dominate clicks for organic shapes and boxes dominate for convex objects (a shape-conditional efficiency map), while the field's per-interaction accounting has promoted clicks beyond their true standing - and optimal interfaces should switch primitives per object geometry.
why_important: Every labeling operation allocates budget by these tradeoffs; a shape-conditional efficiency map is directly actionable industry-wide.
why_possibly_novel: Time-based shape-conditional efficiency measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Timed annotation study (N=20) across primitive types and object-shape strata, fit efficiency map, validate model-training outcomes per budget.
main_risk: Annotator skill heterogeneity; use within-subject designs.

one_liner: Unpromptable objects exist: characterize the reachable mask space of frozen interactive models and what lies outside it.
problem: Interactive models are assumed universal - enough clicks reach any mask. But the decoder's output manifold may exclude some masks entirely (certain topologies, textures), making some objects unreachable at ANY click budget.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for frozen interactive segmenters there exist GT masks whose best reachable IoU (under exhaustive prompt search) plateaus below 0.7 (structural unreachability), unreachable objects share identifiable properties (wiry topology, translucency, extreme aspect), and unreachability persists across prompt types - defining the model's true expressivity boundary, distinct from its average behavior.
why_important: Annotation pipelines assume humans+model can always produce GT; unreachable objects silently corrupt datasets built with model assistance.
why_possibly_novel: Reachability analysis of interactive segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Exhaustive/beam prompt search on 1k diverse objects, identify plateau cases, cluster their properties, verify with human super-users.
main_risk: Search may miss exotic prompt combinations; bound claims by search budget honestly.

one_liner: Label order shapes the final model: easy-first vs hard-first annotation curricula produce different models at identical final budgets.
problem: Datasets are annotated in some order (often easy-first), and models are periodically retrained during collection (model-assisted labeling). Whether the ORDER leaves a permanent imprint on the final dataset+model is unexamined.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in model-in-the-loop annotation, easy-first ordering converges to datasets with systematically different error profiles than hard-first (assistance quality compounds: early model errors seed persistent label styles), and the final-model performance difference at identical budgets exceeds typical method deltas - collection order is a hidden hyperparameter of dataset quality.
why_important: Every assisted-labeling operation implicitly chooses an order; knowing the compounding effect would change collection protocols cheaply.
why_possibly_novel: Order-effect quantification in assisted dataset construction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Simulated assisted-labeling runs with order policies on a fully-labeled dataset (labels revealed per policy), compare final model quality and error styles.
main_risk: Simulation fidelity to real human-model interaction; a small real study for anchoring.

one_liner: Verification bias: annotators accept wrong-but-plausible machine masks at high rates, and the accepted errors are systematically correlated with model style.
problem: Verify-and-fix workflows (machine proposes, human approves) are the industry standard, but acceptance decisions under time pressure may pass through model errors that free-drawing annotators would never make - contaminating datasets with model-correlated noise.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: acceptance error rates for plausible-but-wrong proposals exceed free-drawing error rates severalfold for boundary details and small parts, the accepted errors correlate across the dataset (same model style), and models trained on verified data inherit and AMPLIFY these correlated errors - a measurable contamination loop absent from noise-model assumptions (which assume independent noise).
why_important: Correlated label noise breaks the independence assumptions behind noise-robust training; quantifying the loop is prerequisite to fixing dataset factories.
why_possibly_novel: Correlated-contamination quantification of verify-workflows is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Controlled study: same images labeled by verify-vs-draw protocols, measure error correlation structure, train models on each, compare inherited biases.
main_risk: Time-pressure realism in lab studies; partner with a real annotation vendor for ecological validity.

one_liner: Detect the SAM fingerprint: datasets annotated with SAM assistance carry identifiable boundary-style signatures that future models inbreed on.
problem: Post-2023 datasets are increasingly SAM-assisted. If SAM's boundary style (edge-snapping, blob bias, characteristic curvature spectrum) marks these labels, models trained on them converge toward SAM's biases - ecosystem inbreeding that nobody tracks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a classifier distinguishes SAM-assisted from human-drawn masks at high accuracy using boundary micro-statistics (fingerprint exists), the fingerprint's prevalence in recent public datasets is substantial and rising, and models trained on fingerprinted data reproduce SAM's specific failure modes (holes filled, wires broken) even on classes where SAM was never involved - measurable style inheritance.
why_important: Dataset provenance transparency and bias tracking for the foundation-model era; inbreeding could silently homogenize the field's failure modes into single points of failure.
why_possibly_novel: SAM-fingerprint forensics and inheritance measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build fingerprint classifier on known SAM/human mask pairs, survey 10 recent datasets, test failure-mode inheritance in models trained on high-fingerprint data.
main_risk: Post-editing by humans blurs fingerprints; classifier must handle mixed provenance.

one_liner: Where should a scribble go? Skeleton vs boundary-following vs freeform strokes have measurably different information gain per pixel drawn.
problem: Scribble supervision treats all strokes equally, but stroke PLACEMENT geometry (medial axis, near-boundary, random) plausibly changes information delivered per unit effort - the placement policy question is unstudied.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for equal stroke length, skeleton-placed scribbles train better region models while near-boundary parallel strokes train better boundary models (a decomposable placement effect), and a mixed policy tuned per class geometry outperforms natural human scribbling by a meaningful margin - placement policy is worth more than scribble quantity within realistic budgets.
why_important: Scribble platforms can guide stroke placement with simple UI nudges; validated policies convert to free accuracy across weak-supervision projects.
why_possibly_novel: Stroke-placement information analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Synthesize placement-controlled scribbles from GT masks, train per policy at matched stroke budgets, decompose gains by region/boundary metrics.
main_risk: Synthetic scribbles idealize human motor behavior; verify with guided-human study.

one_liner: Region-level active learning with real time-cost models: intra-image selection beats whole-image selection once annotation time is measured honestly.
problem: Active learning for segmentation mostly selects whole images, but annotation cost varies enormously within images; region-level selection with realistic time models (travel time, context acquisition, zooming) has never been evaluated under honest cost accounting.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under measured per-region annotation time models (including the overhead of context re-acquisition when jumping between regions), region-level selection still dominates image-level by >30% Dice-per-hour at practical budgets, but naive per-pixel-uncertainty region selection UNDERPERFORMS image selection because it ignores overhead - cost-model realism determines the ranking of AL strategies.
why_important: AL research optimizes proxy costs; showing rankings flip under real time models forces the field toward deployable protocols.
why_possibly_novel: Overhead-aware regional AL evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Measure annotation time components in a small study, build cost model, re-simulate AL strategy comparison on 3 datasets.
main_risk: Time models vary by tooling; publish the cost model as configurable artifact.

one_liner: Shape predictability determines point-supervision efficiency: one point suffices exactly when class shape entropy is low - fit the law.
problem: Single-point supervision recovers surprising performance for some classes and fails for others. The determining property is presumably how predictable the class's shape is given one point - a measurable quantity nobody has connected.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the fraction of full-mask performance recoverable from single-point supervision per class is predicted (r>0.8) by class shape entropy (variance of shape descriptors across instances), yielding a practical law: measure shape entropy from a handful of masks, predict point-supervision viability before committing to an annotation scheme.
why_important: Converts supervision-scheme selection from trial-and-error into a measurement-driven decision - direct savings for every new dataset.
why_possibly_novel: Shape-entropy-based supervision-efficiency law is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Across 40 classes from COCO/LVIS, train point-supervised models, regress recovered-performance fraction on shape-entropy estimates from 20 masks per class.
main_risk: Context predictability confounds shape predictability; include context-entropy covariate.

one_liner: Expertise routing: measure WHERE expert annotation beats crowd annotation at the pixel level, and route only those pixels to experts.
problem: Datasets choose expert or crowd annotation wholesale, but expertise plausibly matters only in specific regions (ambiguous boundaries, rare structures); the pixel-level expertise premium map is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert-vs-crowd label agreement analysis will show the expertise premium concentrates in <20% of pixels (identifiable a priori by ambiguity predictors), and a routing policy sending only those regions to experts achieves expert-level dataset quality at a fraction of expert cost - measurable end-to-end via models trained on routed datasets.
why_important: Expert time is the scarcest resource in specialized domains (medical, scientific imagery); pixel-level routing is the efficient frontier of annotation economics.
why_possibly_novel: Pixel-resolved expertise-premium mapping with routed-dataset validation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Double-annotate (expert+crowd) 500 medical/complex images, map premium regions, test predictor, train models on routed vs pure datasets at matched cost.
main_risk: Premium maps may be domain-specific; replicate across two domains.

one_liner: Optimal correction-frame selection in video annotation: model uncertainty peaks beat uniform keyframes, but the real optimum is drift-onset frames.
problem: Video annotation corrects the tracker at chosen frames; the frame-selection policy (uniform, uncertainty-based, drift-onset-based) determines total cost, but policies have not been compared under matched click budgets.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: correcting at detected drift-onset frames (from self-diagnosis signals) yields better final video masks than uniform or uncertainty-peak selection at equal correction budget, with the advantage growing with video length - because corrections BEFORE error compounding are worth multiples of corrections after.
why_important: Video annotation is the current cost bottleneck for VOS datasets; a validated frame-selection policy compounds savings across the ecosystem.
why_possibly_novel: Drift-onset-timed correction policy evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Simulate correction policies with SAM2 on DAVIS/LVOS at matched budgets, compare final-quality curves; small human study for timing realism.
main_risk: Drift-onset detection quality gates the policy; co-develop with the self-diagnosis idea.

one_liner: The good-enough plateau: humans stop correcting at ~90% quality, leaving systematic residual errors aligned with model biases in every assisted dataset.
problem: Assisted annotation ends when the human judges the mask 'good enough', not when it is correct. The residual errors are thus model-biased (humans fix salient errors, keep model-style subtle ones) - a structured contamination whose form is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: assisted-annotation residuals concentrate in low-salience error types (boundary offsets in blurry regions, small holes) while free-drawn labels distribute errors differently, the residual structure matches the assisting model's bias profile, and datasets can be forensically dated/attributed to their assisting model by residual structure alone.
why_important: Defines the quality ceiling of the assisted-annotation paradigm and provides provenance forensics; also predicts what SECOND-generation models can and cannot learn from such data.
why_possibly_novel: Residual-structure analysis of the good-enough threshold is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Have annotators 'finish' assisted masks, then expert-audit at high zoom; compare residual profiles across assisting models and against free-drawing.
main_risk: Good-enough thresholds vary with pay/incentives; sample multiple annotation economies.

one_liner: Gaze as free dense supervision: eye-tracking during ordinary image inspection carries recoverable segmentation signal.
problem: Wherever humans inspect images professionally (radiology, quality control), gaze data is potentially collectible at zero marginal effort; its information content for segmentation supervision is essentially unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: gaze density and scanpath features around objects contain enough localization signal that gaze-weak-supervised models reach a meaningful fraction (>50%) of point-supervised performance without ANY deliberate annotation, and gaze fixation ORDER additionally encodes object saliency structure usable for curriculum construction.
why_important: Free supervision from existing professional workflows would be transformative for domains where deliberate annotation competes with real work (medicine).
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: gaze studies exist in radiology perception research; segmentation-supervision extraction with performance accounting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use public radiology gaze datasets (e.g. REFLACX-like), derive gaze-based pseudo-labels, train and compare against point-supervised baselines.
main_risk: Gaze concentrates on diagnostic hotspots, not object extents; may supervise detection better than delineation (report both).

one_liner: Language vs clicks for disambiguation: when scenes get crowded, referring expressions become cheaper than pointing - find the crossover.
problem: Disambiguating a target among similar instances can be done by clicking (spatial) or describing ('the third cup from the left') - the interaction-cost crossover between modalities as scene complexity grows is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: measured in time-to-correct-mask, clicking dominates in sparse scenes but language dominates beyond a measurable instance-density threshold (pointing precision degrades with crowding faster than description length grows), and hybrid systems that ROUTE by predicted density beat either modality alone by >20% throughput.
why_important: Multimodal annotation interfaces are buildable today; the routing law tells builders when each modality pays, grounded in measurement rather than fashion.
why_possibly_novel: Modality-crossover measurement for segmentation disambiguation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Timed human study across instance-density ladder with click-only, language-only, and routed interfaces on crowded scenes (shelves, crowds).
main_risk: Language grounding model quality gates the language arm; use the best available grounding models and report sensitivity.

one_liner: Annotation protocol is a stronger treatment than architecture: same images labeled boundary-first vs region-first produce measurably different trained models.
problem: Protocols (labeling order, tool, instructions) are considered logistics, not science. If protocol-induced differences in trained models exceed typical architecture deltas, the field's controlled comparisons are missing a dominant variable.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: training identical architectures on the same images labeled under two professional protocols (boundary-tracing-first vs region-filling-first) produces models whose performance difference on neutral test sets exceeds the median published architecture improvement - protocol choice silently dominates a meaningful fraction of reported progress.
why_important: A provocative, testable claim about what actually drives measured differences in the literature; would force protocol reporting standards.
why_possibly_novel: Protocol-as-treatment controlled experiments are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Commission dual-protocol labeling of 2k images by the same vendor, train matched models, compare deltas against a survey of published architecture gains.
main_risk: Annotation cost of the dual corpus; mitigate with a focused domain (e.g. one driving subset).

one_liner: Negative-space labels for rare classes: marking 'definitely-not-X' regions is cheap and disproportionately valuable for tail-class learning.
problem: All annotation effort goes into positive labels; explicit negatives (this region certainly contains no X) are never collected, though for rare classes the model's main confusion is what ISN'T the class.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for tail classes, a budget split that spends 30% on definitely-not-X region marking (fast, low-cognitive-load) beats 100%-positive budgets by a measurable margin on precision-critical metrics, because rare-class errors are dominated by hard-negative confusion that positives cannot teach - the value of negative space is class-frequency-dependent and predictable.
why_important: A cheap new annotation primitive with a theory of when it pays - immediately testable by any labeling operation struggling with tail precision.
why_possibly_novel: Explicit negative-region annotation economics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On LVIS tail classes, simulate budget splits using existing annotations to synthesize negatives, then run a small real-annotation confirmation.
main_risk: Negatives may be too easy (uninformative regions get marked); guided negative selection needed.

one_liner: Annotator zoom telemetry is a free boundary-uncertainty ground truth: where humans zoom in, ambiguity lives.
problem: Annotation interfaces record zoom/pan behavior that nobody analyzes; zoom-in events plausibly mark exactly the boundary regions annotators find uncertain - a free, behavioral ambiguity signal at dataset scale.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: zoom-event density along boundaries correlates strongly with inter-annotator disagreement (validating telemetry as ambiguity GT), and models calibrated against zoom-density maps achieve boundary-uncertainty quality comparable to expensive multi-annotator supervision - telemetry replaces redundant labeling for uncertainty training.
why_important: Multi-annotator redundancy is the current (expensive) route to ambiguity ground truth; telemetry is already being recorded and discarded industry-wide.
why_possibly_novel: Telemetry-derived ambiguity supervision is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Instrument an annotation tool, collect telemetry on multi-annotated images, validate zoom-disagreement correlation, train uncertainty heads on telemetry.
main_risk: Zoom behavior also reflects object size and tool ergonomics; regression controls required.

one_liner: Let the model ask: binary yes/no questions about parts ('is the strap included?') beat clicks for ambiguity resolution per second of human time.
problem: Interactive segmentation only accepts spatial gestures, but much residual ambiguity is SEMANTIC (include the handle? the shadow? the attached cable?) - resolvable by one binary answer instead of several corrective clicks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: an interaction budget spent on model-generated binary part-inclusion questions resolves granularity/attachment ambiguity faster (in human-seconds to target IoU) than the same budget in clicks, specifically on objects whose ambiguity is compositional rather than boundary-metric - a measurable interaction-modality advantage on a definable object subset.
why_important: Identifies the right interaction primitive per ambiguity TYPE, moving interactive segmentation beyond pure spatial correction toward mixed-initiative dialogue.
why_possibly_novel: Question-generation for segmentation disambiguation with time-based evaluation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Wizard-of-Oz study: humans answer scripted part-questions vs click corrections at matched time budgets on ambiguous objects (bags with straps, tools with cables).
main_risk: Automatic question generation is a hard subproblem; the study establishes value before building it.

one_liner: Correction propagation: one human fix retrieved-and-applied across thousands of images sharing the same systematic model error.
problem: Model errors are systematic (same failure on similar inputs), but human corrections are consumed once. Retrieving past corrections for similar contexts could amortize each fix across the corpus - the amortization factor is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: corrections cluster in feature space (systematic error families), retrieval-based correction transfer (apply the nearest past correction's local transformation) fixes a substantial fraction of same-family errors without new human input, and the human-effort amortization factor exceeds 10x on homogeneous corpora (aerial tiles, pathology slides) - correction reuse is a neglected order-of-magnitude lever.
why_important: Changes annotation economics fundamentally on large homogeneous corpora, which is exactly where annotation costs bite hardest.
why_possibly_novel: Retrieval-based correction propagation for dense labels is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On aerial/pathology corpora, collect corrections, cluster error contexts, measure transfer precision of retrieved fixes vs fresh model predictions.
main_risk: Bad transfers corrupt labels silently; needs conservative confidence gating and audit sampling.

one_liner: Noisy-many vs precise-few for pretraining: fit the exchange rate between mask quantity and mask quality at fixed annotation budget.
problem: A fixed budget buys either many rough masks or few precise ones. The quality-quantity exchange rate for segmentation pretraining/training - and whether it depends on downstream task boundary-sensitivity - has never been mapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on the quality-quantity frontier at matched budget, region-level downstream tasks favor quantity strongly (rough masks nearly free of penalty) while boundary-level tasks favor quality with a sharp threshold effect (below some precision, masks are worse than useless for boundary learning) - two regimes with a measurable phase boundary that should govern annotation-spec decisions.
why_important: The single most common annotation-planning question, currently answered by intuition; a published frontier with the phase boundary would be a standard reference.
why_possibly_novel: Budget-matched quality-quantity frontier mapping is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Degrade GT masks at controlled precision levels, train at matched simulated budgets across quality-quantity mixes, map the frontier for region vs boundary metrics.
main_risk: Synthetic degradation may not mimic real cheap-annotation error structure; anchor with real dual-quality annotations.

one_liner: Multi-view agreement replaces annotation: photos of the same scene from different angles provide free correspondence-based mask supervision.
problem: Multi-view captures (real-estate scans, photogrammetry, casual multi-shots) constrain segmentation geometrically - a mask valid in one view must reproject consistently to others - but this free supervision channel is unexploited for training 2D segmenters.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: cross-view mask-consistency training on unlabeled multi-view corpora (enforcing reprojection agreement via estimated geometry) improves single-view segmentation of view-dependent failure cases (glare, oblique angles, partial occlusion) by a measurable margin over single-view SSL at matched data volume - geometry is a supervisor that photometric SSL cannot replicate.
why_important: Taps enormous existing multi-view corpora (mapping, real estate, e-commerce turntables) as free dense supervision, targeting exactly the failures single views cannot teach.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: multi-view consistency is used in 3D reconstruction; its harvest as 2D segmentation supervision at scale is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use ScanNet/RealEstate-style corpora, add reprojection-consistency objectives to an SSL baseline, evaluate single-view improvements on shifted test sets.
main_risk: Geometry estimation errors inject noise; restrict supervision to high-confidence correspondences.

one_liner: Click order is a cognitive probe: the sequence in which annotators click parts reveals a shared human object-decomposition that models lack.
problem: Multi-click annotation sequences encode which parts humans consider primary, ambiguous, or boundary-critical - a behavioral window into human object structure that is recorded everywhere and studied nowhere.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: click sequences across annotators show strong order regularities (canonical part order per category: face before limbs, body before accessories), the regularities predict which parts models most often mis-segment (late-clicked parts are model-hardest), and sequence-derived part priorities improve error prediction beyond appearance features - human interaction order encodes a difficulty structure models share.
why_important: A zero-cost behavioral dataset for studying object decomposition, with practical use in error prediction and annotation UI design.
why_possibly_novel: Click-order regularity analysis as cognitive/difficulty probe is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mine click logs from open annotation projects (or collect via crowdsourcing), quantify order regularities, correlate with per-part model error rates.
main_risk: Order reflects UI layout and motor efficiency too; experimental designs must separate these.

one_liner: Give annotators an explicit 'uncertain' brush: does three-state labeling (yes/no/unsure) improve downstream models over forced binary?
problem: Forced-binary interfaces convert annotator uncertainty into silent noise. An explicit unsure-label preserves the information, but whether models trained with it beat models trained on forced-binary labels (at equal annotation time) is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: three-state annotation costs <10% extra time, the unsure-regions reproduce across annotators (they mark signal, not laziness), and excluding-or-downweighting unsure pixels during training improves test performance on the confident-consensus region more than the removed supervision costs - explicit uncertainty capture is annotation-time-positive.
why_important: A minimal interface change with dataset-wide benefits, directly adoptable by every labeling tool if validated.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled three-state protocol evaluation with downstream accounting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Dual-protocol labeling study (binary vs three-state) on ambiguous-heavy imagery, train matched models, compare on high-confidence test regions.
main_risk: Unsure-label semantics drift between annotators without careful instruction design.

one_liner: Tool fingerprints across public datasets: identify which annotation software made each mask and quantify tool-induced bias in the ecosystem.
problem: Public datasets were annotated with different tools (polygon editors, brushes, assisted systems) whose geometric artifacts (vertex spacing, curvature quantization, snap behaviors) enter the labels - the ecosystem-wide composition and its downstream effects are unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mask micro-geometry classifies annotation tooling with high accuracy across major datasets, tool composition differs strongly by dataset era and domain, and models trained cross-dataset devote measurable capacity to tool-style translation (probeable as tool-predictive features in the trained weights) - the ecosystem carries a tooling-bias layer nobody accounts for.
why_important: Meta-transparency for the entire benchmark ecosystem, and a concrete confounder to control in cross-dataset studies.
why_possibly_novel: Ecosystem-scale tool forensics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble tool-labeled mask corpora (known-provenance datasets), train fingerprint classifier, survey 15 public datasets, probe trained segmenters for tool-feature encoding.
main_risk: Provenance ground truth for older datasets is scarce; bootstrap from documented cases.

one_liner: The 100-labeled-pixels challenge: map the extreme-low-budget frontier of segmentation to find where each supervision paradigm collapses.
problem: Label-efficiency papers compare at comfortable budgets (1-10% of pixels); the extreme regime (say 100 labeled pixels per class total) has no map, though it reveals which paradigms extract the most information per label bit and where each breaks.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at extreme budgets, paradigm rankings invert relative to comfortable budgets (foundation-feature probing dominates fine-tuning; consistency methods collapse entirely below a measurable threshold; point-supervision beats mask-supervision per pixel), producing a budget-vs-paradigm phase map with actionable regime boundaries - the field's efficiency conclusions are budget-regime-specific and do not extrapolate down.
why_important: Scientific applications (rare phenomena, expert-only labels) live in the extreme regime the literature never visits; the phase map is their missing guidance.
why_possibly_novel: Extreme-budget phase mapping is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Budget ladder from 100 to 100k labeled pixels across 5 paradigms on 3 datasets, plot the phase map with collapse thresholds.
main_risk: High variance at tiny budgets demands many seeds; compute cost is real but bounded.

one_liner: Decompose any domain gap into photometric, geometric, and semantic components with controlled re-rendering - then publish the composition per benchmark.
problem: 'Domain gap' is treated as a scalar, but its composition (color/sensor vs viewpoint/layout vs class-distribution differences) determines which adaptation method can possibly work - and no benchmark reports its composition.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: using controlled transformations (photometric transplants, geometry-preserving style transfer, label-distribution reweighting), each popular shift benchmark decomposes into stable component fractions; adaptation methods' gains align with the component they address (photometric methods win only on photometric-heavy gaps), explaining most of the notorious inconsistency of UDA results across benchmarks.
why_important: Gives the field a diagnostic vocabulary: measure your gap's composition first, then choose methods - replacing the current lottery.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic gap-composition accounting across benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build the three controlled transforms, measure component fractions on 6 shift pairs, correlate method-gain profiles with compositions.
main_risk: Components interact (not perfectly separable); report interaction terms honestly.

one_liner: Sim2real gap lives in materials, not geometry: hybrid renders (real textures on synthetic geometry, and vice versa) isolate what synthetic data gets wrong.
problem: Synthetic training data underperforms real data for segmentation, but WHERE the deficit lives (shape/layout realism vs material/lighting appearance) is folklore, not measurement - though it determines where rendering effort should go.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: crossing the factors (synthetic geometry + real-photograph textures vs real geometry + synthetic materials) shows the material/appearance factor explains the large majority of the sim2real segmentation gap, geometry realism contributing little - implying cheap geometry with photo-real materials is the optimal synthetic-data recipe, opposite to where most rendering compute goes.
why_important: Synthetic data budgets are large and misallocated if the geometry-heavy intuition is wrong; factor attribution redirects the spend.
why_possibly_novel: Factor-crossed hybrid rendering attribution for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct the 2x2 render conditions in a driving simulator with texture transplants, train per cell, evaluate on real benchmarks.
main_risk: Texture transplantation introduces its own artifacts; needs artifact-matched controls.

one_liner: Night failure is mostly ISP failure: models degrade on processed JPEGs, not on darkness itself - RAW-domain evaluation separates the two.
problem: Nighttime segmentation failure is attributed to insufficient light, but consumer ISP pipelines (denoising, tone mapping, white balance) transform night captures aggressively and variably; models may fail on ISP artifacts rather than photon scarcity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: evaluating on RAW-processed-with-fixed-simple-pipeline night images recovers a substantial fraction of the day-night performance drop relative to camera-ISP JPEGs (the ISP is a major failure contributor), and the recovered fraction varies by ISP vendor - night robustness research is partly chasing vendor-specific artifacts.
why_important: If the ISP is a first-order factor, night perception should be co-designed with capture pipelines, and existing night benchmarks measure entangled camera stacks rather than vision capability.
why_possibly_novel: ISP-vs-photon attribution for night dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use datasets with RAW night captures (or collect paired RAW/JPEG), evaluate models across processing pipelines, decompose the drop.
main_risk: RAW night data with segmentation GT is scarce; may need targeted collection with transfer-annotated labels.

one_liner: Camera ISP fingerprint as an unbenchmarked shift axis: same scenes through different phone pipelines measurably move dense predictions.
problem: Every camera brand applies proprietary processing (sharpening, denoising, color science). Models trained on one ISP mix may silently degrade on another - an axis orthogonal to weather/geography that no benchmark isolates.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: capturing identical scenes with multiple devices (tripod-locked) and evaluating fixed models shows per-model prediction shifts comparable in magnitude to mild weather shift, with boundary-level metrics most affected (sharpening halos) - ISP variation is a first-class shift axis deserving its own benchmark. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search on existing cross-device studies.
why_important: Deployments span device fleets; an ignored first-order shift axis means fleet-wide QA is currently blind to a real variance source.
why_possibly_novel: Tripod-locked cross-ISP dense-prediction benchmarking appears missing.
minimal_experiment: Capture 200 locked scenes with 5 devices, run model zoo, quantify prediction divergence and metric movement per device pair.
main_risk: Perfect pixel alignment across devices is impossible (optics differ); evaluate with alignment-tolerant metrics.

one_liner: BN-statistics adaptation helps photometric shift but actively harms semantic shift: map when the cheapest TTA trick becomes poison.
problem: Test-time normalization-statistics adaptation is the default cheap fix under shift, applied indiscriminately; its failure conditions (when target statistics differences reflect content, not style) are anecdotal.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: across a controlled shift taxonomy, statistics adaptation improves photometric/sensor shifts consistently but DEGRADES performance under label-distribution and content shifts (it 'corrects' real signal), with the harm predictable from the correlation between channel statistics and class evidence - yielding a practical pre-test that decides whether to adapt.
why_important: A deploy-time go/no-go test for the most-used adaptation trick prevents silent self-inflicted damage.
why_possibly_novel: Shift-type-conditional harm characterization with a predictive pre-test is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply statistics adaptation across shift-type ladders (photometric, weather, geographic, class-mix), measure signed effects, validate the harm predictor.
main_risk: Modern normalization-free architectures reduce the scope; include them for completeness.

one_liner: Geographic shift decomposes into stuff-appearance and thing-longtail: cross-region failure has two mechanisms needing opposite remedies.
problem: Models trained in one region degrade in another, but the degradation conflates two mechanisms - unfamiliar background appearance (road surfaces, vegetation) and unfamiliar object variants (vehicle types, dress) - which respond to different fixes (style adaptation vs data collection).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-class cross-region degradation splits bimodally - stuff classes fail by appearance statistics (fixable by style-level adaptation, no new labels) while thing classes fail by variant novelty (fixable only by target-region examples) - and the split predicts which classes any adaptation method can rescue, explaining heterogeneous published UDA results class-by-class.
why_important: Region expansion is the standard deployment problem (driving, agriculture, mapping); a mechanism-level failure map converts adaptation from alchemy to engineering.
why_possibly_novel: Mechanism-split analysis of geographic shift per class is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Cross-evaluate on multi-region datasets (Mapillary regions, IDD vs Cityscapes), classify per-class failures by style-transfer-recoverability, validate the two-mechanism model.
main_risk: Some classes fail by both mechanisms; use continuous mixture attribution, not hard split.

one_liner: Transferability is spatially structured: sky transfers, road texture does not - build per-region transfer maps and adapt only what fails.
problem: Adaptation methods treat images uniformly, but shift affects scene regions unequally (sky is universal; ground textures are local). Spatially-selective adaptation could preserve what already transfers - if transfer geography were measured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-pixel cross-domain performance retention has strong reproducible spatial/semantic structure (a transfer map stable across model families), uniform adaptation methods measurably damage well-transferring regions while fixing bad ones (netting less than possible), and transfer-map-gated adaptation beats uniform adaptation at matched compute.
why_important: Reveals adaptation's hidden collateral damage and provides a general recipe (measure, gate, adapt) applicable to every UDA method.
why_possibly_novel: Transfer-geography mapping with gated adaptation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compute per-class/per-region retention across 4 shift pairs and 3 models, verify map stability, implement gated variant of one standard UDA method.
main_risk: Gating needs target labels to validate - use held-out target labels for science, proxy signals for the method.

one_liner: Weather shifts do not compose additively: rain+night is worse than rain-effect plus night-effect - measure the interaction matrix.
problem: Robustness studies test single factors (rain OR night OR fog), but deployment presents combinations; if degradations interact super-additively, single-factor benchmarks systematically understate real risk - the interaction structure is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: factorial evaluation over weather-condition combinations reveals significant super-additive interactions for specific pairs (night amplifies rain's effect via reflections; fog amplifies backlight), the interaction matrix is stable across models (physics-driven, not model-driven), and worst-case combinations are predictable from single-factor physics rather than requiring exhaustive testing.
why_important: Safety validation currently extrapolates from single factors; a measured interaction matrix corrects the risk model where it is most wrong.
why_possibly_novel: Factorial interaction analysis of weather robustness is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use condition-rich datasets (ACDC, BDD) plus controlled synthesis for missing cells, fit interaction terms per class, test cross-model stability.
main_risk: Natural data has sparse combination coverage; synthesis fills cells but needs realism validation.

one_liner: Geometry as the shift-invariant channel: does routing through depth (RGB to depth to segmentation) transfer better than direct RGB segmentation?
problem: Appearance shifts (weather, sensors, geography) barely change scene geometry. If segmentation via an intermediate geometric representation retains more accuracy under shift, the invariance structure of the task itself becomes exploitable - a question about representations, not methods.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a pipeline segmenting from predicted depth+normals (with a thin appearance channel) loses less under photometric/weather shift than matched direct-RGB models (geometry mediates invariance), but pays a measurable in-distribution penalty on texture-defined classes - a quantified invariance-vs-acuity tradeoff with a computable optimal mixing ratio per deployment shift profile.
why_important: Establishes which invariances are worth buying at what acuity price - a design law for robustness rather than another method.
why_possibly_novel: Geometry-mediated transfer quantification for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train matched direct and geometry-mediated segmenters, evaluate across shift ladders, fit the tradeoff frontier and mixing-ratio optimum.
main_risk: Depth estimators carry their own shift sensitivity; measure and account for it explicitly.

one_liner: Benchmark the shift-measures: which unsupervised domain-distance metric actually predicts segmentation performance drop?
problem: Teams estimate deployment risk with feature-space distances (FID-like, MMD, proxy accuracies), but these metrics have never been systematically validated as PREDICTORS of dense-prediction degradation - the meta-question the field skipped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: common distribution distances correlate weakly with segmentation drop across a broad shift matrix (r<0.5), because they weight global appearance over the boundary- and minority-class evidence segmentation depends on; a dense-prediction-specific measure (built from label-free prediction statistics like churn, margin distributions, connected-component statistics) predicts drops substantially better - and the validated predictor becomes a deployment tool.
why_important: Every go/no-go deployment decision under shift implicitly trusts some distance measure; validating them is basic metrological hygiene the field lacks.
why_possibly_novel: Predictive-validity benchmarking of shift measures for dense tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble 30+ source-target segmentation pairs with known drops, correlate candidate measures, build and validate the dense-specific predictor.
main_risk: Conclusions depend on shift-pair diversity; deliberately include adversarially-mild and severe pairs.

one_liner: Adaptation hysteresis: a model adapted A-to-B differs from one trained at B directly, and the path-dependence predicts continual-adaptation drift.
problem: Continual test-time adaptation walks models through condition sequences (day to dusk to night). Whether the endpoint depends on the path (hysteresis) - and whether looping conditions returns the model to its start - determines if continual adaptation is stable or secularly drifting.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: adapted models exhibit measurable hysteresis (A-to-B-to-A does not recover the original A performance; the gap grows with loop count - secular drift), drift accumulates in specific layers (normalization and early convolutions), and periodic anchor-replay eliminates it at negligible cost - continual adaptation without anchoring is quantifiably unsafe over long deployments.
why_important: Continual TTA is heading into products; its long-horizon stability has never been characterized, and drift would be a slow silent failure.
why_possibly_novel: Hysteresis/drift analysis of adaptation dynamics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Cycle models through condition loops (synthetic + ACDC sequences), measure return-gap growth, localize drifting parameters, test anchor-replay.
main_risk: Results depend on the specific TTA algorithm; cover the 3 main families.

one_liner: Annotation-convention shift masquerades as domain shift: cross-country dataset gaps are partly label-sociology gaps.
problem: Cross-dataset evaluation (Cityscapes to IDD to BDD) conflates appearance shift with annotation-convention differences (what counts as 'road' vs 'parking'; curb handling; rider/vehicle splits) - the convention fraction of the measured gap is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-annotating a sample of target-domain images under the SOURCE dataset's written protocol recovers a substantial fraction (>25%) of the measured cross-dataset performance gap for affected classes - meaning published cross-domain numbers systematically overstate appearance-driven failure and adaptation methods get credit for learning label conventions.
why_important: Separates two entangled research problems (visual robustness vs ontology mapping) that need entirely different solutions.
why_possibly_novel: Protocol-controlled re-annotation accounting for domain-gap decomposition is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-annotate 300 target images under source protocol, re-evaluate the gap per class, tabulate the convention fraction.
main_risk: Written protocols under-specify actual annotator behavior; use annotators trained on source-dataset examples.

one_liner: Resolution regime shift: models trained at 1024px meet 4K deployment - effective receptive fields misalign with object scales in a predictable, correctable way.
problem: Training and deployment resolutions diverge (datasets are downsampled; cameras improve). The resulting scale mismatch between learned receptive fields and presented object sizes is a shift axis handled today by ad hoc resizing folklore.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: performance under resolution shift follows a predictable curve in the ratio of object-pixels-per-receptive-field between train and test, is asymmetric (upscale deployment hurts more than downscale), and optimal test-time resizing is computable from dataset object-size statistics alone - replacing folklore with a scaling rule that recovers most of the mismatch loss.
why_important: Resolution mismatch is ubiquitous and silently mishandled; a validated rule converts a recurring engineering headache into a formula.
why_possibly_novel: Dimensionless resolution-shift law for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train at multiple resolutions, test across a resolution ladder, fit the law in ratio coordinates, validate the resizing rule on held-out datasets.
main_risk: Architecture-dependent effects (ViT patchification vs CNN strides) may split the law; fit per family.

one_liner: Compression asymmetry: benchmarks are compressed, deployment streams are rawer - models overfit artifacts they will not see, an inverted shift nobody tests.
problem: Shift studies assume deployment is degraded relative to clean benchmarks, but for compression the arrow can invert: web-scraped training data is heavily compressed while deployment feeds (industrial cameras, medical scanners) are near-lossless - models may DEPEND on compression artifacts.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models trained on web-compressed data measurably degrade on lossless imagery (artifact dependence: denoising-like artifacts act as learned features), the effect concentrates in texture-defined classes, and light recompression of deployment inputs (deliberately degrading them toward training statistics) IMPROVES accuracy - a counter-intuitive, immediately testable prescription.
why_important: The recompression prescription is deployable in an afternoon if validated; the phenomenon also reframes 'data quality' - matching beats maximizing.
why_possibly_novel: Inverted compression-shift analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate web-trained models on lossless captures vs recompressed versions of the same, measure the signed effect per class.
main_risk: Effect size may be small for modern diverse training sets; report honestly across training-data eras.

one_liner: Where does foundation-feature robustness come from - data diversity or training objective? Checkpoint-ladder analysis separates the credit.
problem: DINOv2/SAM features transfer robustly, credited vaguely to 'scale'. Whether robustness accrues from data diversity, objective choice, or training duration - decomposable via public checkpoint series - matters for what to invest in next.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: analyzing robustness (shift-retention of downstream segmentation) across public checkpoint ladders and matched-data reruns shows data diversity dominates objective choice by a wide margin (matched-data models converge in robustness across objectives; matched-objective models diverge with data), and robustness saturates earlier in training than in-distribution accuracy - actionable credit assignment for the ecosystem's biggest investment question.
why_important: Billions of compute dollars ride on the diversity-vs-objective question; even partial credit assignment from existing artifacts is high-value.
why_possibly_novel: Robustness credit-assignment via checkpoint forensics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe segmentation robustness across available checkpoint series (DINO variants, MAE, CLIP at multiple data scales), fit robustness-accrual curves per factor where artifacts allow.
main_risk: Public artifacts confound factors; where reruns are needed, use small-scale matched experiments and extrapolate cautiously.

one_liner: Predict per-pixel performance drop from the source model alone: performance forecasting as a first-class dense-prediction task.
problem: Before deployment, teams need per-region risk maps for the target domain without target labels - a forecasting task distinct from adaptation, with no benchmark or standard method for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-pixel drop is forecastable (correlation >0.6 with realized drop) from source-model-computable signals (feature-space distance to training manifold, margin statistics, augmentation sensitivity), forecast errors are themselves structured (over-optimistic on novel classes, over-pessimistic on style variation) - and a benchmark of forecasting quality would expose large differences between signals the field currently treats as interchangeable.
why_important: Risk forecasting is the deployment decision-maker's actual question; formalizing it as a benchmarked task channels research toward what practitioners need.
why_possibly_novel: Dense performance-forecasting benchmark construction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build forecast-vs-realized evaluation on 10 shift pairs, compare 6 forecasting signals, publish the benchmark protocol.
main_risk: Forecast quality varies by shift type; the benchmark must stratify to avoid misleading averages.

one_liner: Natural adversarial weather mining: search real archives for the worst-case conditions per model, instead of averaging over benchmark weather.
problem: Robustness is reported as averages over available conditions, but safety depends on worst cases; mining large unlabeled archives (webcams, dashcams) for each model's WORST natural conditions - and checking if they are shared across models - is unexplored.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: guided search over unlabeled archives (optimizing a label-free failure proxy) discovers natural condition clusters where model performance is far below benchmark-average robustness numbers (hidden failure modes: specific sun angles, wet-road glare geometries, mixed precipitation), and a substantial fraction of these clusters transfer across model families - natural worst cases are systematic, findable, and shared.
why_important: Averages hide the failures that cause accidents; a mining methodology gives safety teams a repeatable worst-case discovery tool.
why_possibly_novel: Label-free worst-case mining in natural archives for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement failure-proxy-guided search over webcam archives, verify mined clusters with spot annotation, test cross-model transfer of hardness.
main_risk: Failure proxies may mine proxy-artifacts rather than true failures; spot annotation is the essential control.

one_liner: Time-of-day is a hidden label prior: models learn that parked cars appear at night and fail on time-swapped scenes - anti-causal shortcut measurement.
problem: Class distributions correlate with capture time (delivery trucks by day, parked rows by night); models may encode time-conditioned priors rather than appearance evidence, failing when the correlation breaks (night football game, daytime empty streets).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models infer global time-of-day from image statistics and modulate class priors accordingly (probeable: time is linearly decodable from features and causally influences predictions via controlled relighting), and prior-override errors occur at measurable rates on time-atypical scenes - a quantifiable anti-causal shortcut with a stress-test suite as the deliverable.
why_important: Time-atypical scenes (emergencies, events) are exactly when perception must work; a validated stress suite would catch this failure class pre-deployment.
why_possibly_novel: Time-conditioned prior measurement for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe time decodability in features, evaluate on curated time-atypical scenes, use relighting interventions to separate appearance from prior effects.
main_risk: Relighting realism; complement with natural time-atypical collections.

one_liner: Per-class transfer matrix of synthetic data: adding simulation helps some real classes and quantifiably harms others - the negative-transfer ledger.
problem: Synthetic data is added wholesale on the assumption of average benefit, but per-class effects (sim vehicles helping, sim pedestrians hurting via uncanny appearance) are rarely itemized - teams cannot make class-level decisions.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mixed real+synthetic training produces a stable per-class signed-effect ledger (consistent across seeds and architectures), harms concentrate in classes where synthetic appearance diverges most from real (measurable via per-class feature distances), and class-selective synthetic mixing (include only positive-ledger classes) beats wholesale mixing by a meaningful margin - synthetic data needs itemized accounting, not blanket adoption.
why_important: Turns synthetic-data decisions from faith into ledger-driven engineering, with immediate gains from selective mixing.
why_possibly_novel: Signed per-class transfer accounting with selective-mixing validation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train real-only vs mixed vs class-selective mixes on driving data (GTA/SYNTHIA + Cityscapes), tabulate signed ledgers, validate the divergence predictor.
main_risk: Ledger stability across simulators must be tested, not assumed; use two simulators.

one_liner: UDA methods overfit their development benchmark pair: rank correlation across novel shift pairs is the reproducibility number nobody reports.
problem: Unsupervised domain adaptation methods are developed and tuned overwhelmingly on GTA-to-Cityscapes; whether their rankings hold on fresh shift pairs (different domains, modalities, directions) is the field's unasked generalization question about itself.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: re-running leading UDA methods with frozen hyperparameters on 6 novel shift pairs yields low rank correlation with their canonical-benchmark ranking (methods overfit the development pair's shift composition), while simple baselines (strong augmentation, self-training) rank far more stably - the field's method-ranking signal is substantially benchmark-specific noise.
why_important: A meta-scientific audit determining whether UDA progress is real; stability-ranked methods are what practitioners should actually adopt.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-pair rank-stability auditing of UDA is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Reproduce 8 UDA methods, evaluate frozen on novel pairs (medical, aerial, reversed directions), compute rank correlations and stability scores.
main_risk: Frozen hyperparameters may be unfair to methods needing tuning - but that itself is a deployability finding; report both regimes.

one_liner: Metric anchors survive shift: physical size priors (via camera geometry) remain valid when appearance shifts - measure how much of robustness they could carry.
problem: Appearance shifts destroy learned texture cues, but physical regularities (pedestrians ~1.7m, lane widths standardized) survive any weather; how much segmentation robustness metric-scale priors could contribute is unquantified because models entangle scale with appearance.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: probing shows current models' implicit size priors degrade under shift (they are appearance-entangled, not geometric), while models given explicit metric conditioning (camera intrinsics + horizon) retain class discrimination under severe appearance shift measurably better - the shift-invariant information in metric geometry is real, quantifiable, and currently unexploited.
why_important: Identifies an invariance channel that is free at deployment (intrinsics are known) and orthogonal to all appearance-based robustness work.
why_possibly_novel: Metric-prior shift-invariance quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe size-prior stability under shift ladders; train matched models with/without metric conditioning; compare shift retention per class.
main_risk: Intrinsics conditioning helps mainly ground-plane-anchored classes; scope claims accordingly.

one_liner: The domain-randomization sweet spot is predictable: too much randomization hurts, and the optimum tracks target-domain variance - fit the curve.
problem: Domain randomization strength is tuned blindly; the community knows extremes fail (too little = overfit, too much = unlearnable invariance) but has no predictive theory of the optimum's location.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: transfer performance vs randomization strength is reliably non-monotonic with a single optimum whose location scales with measured target-domain variance along each factor (color, texture, lighting independently), so the optimal randomization recipe is computable from a small unlabeled target sample - replacing grid search with measurement.
why_important: Randomization tuning consumes large simulation budgets; a predictive rule compresses it to one estimation step, and the variance-matching principle would generalize across factors.
why_possibly_novel: Variance-matched optimal-randomization law is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep per-factor randomization strengths training on synthetic driving data, locate optima across target datasets with different measured variances, test the scaling law.
main_risk: Factor interactions may shift optima jointly; fit both marginal and joint models.

one_liner: Amplitude-swap explains most photometric-shift benefit - but where does PHASE matter? Locate the residual that frequency-domain adaptation cannot touch.
problem: Fourier amplitude transfer between domains is a known cheap adaptation trick (KNOWN: FDA, Yang & Soatto CVPR 2020 - existence confident, details need verification); what remains AFTER amplitude alignment - the phase-borne shift component - has not been characterized, though it defines the method's ceiling.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: after optimal amplitude alignment, residual cross-domain error concentrates in phase-borne structures (layout differences, object-shape variants, edge geometry), is class-structured (things retain more residual than stuff), and no amplitude-space method can reduce it - establishing a measurable decomposition of photometric vs structural shift with amplitude methods' ceiling made explicit.
why_important: Tells the field precisely what the popular cheap trick cannot fix, preventing wasted iterations and directing effort at the structural residual.
why_possibly_novel: Phase-residual characterization of shift is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply exhaustive amplitude alignment on 5 shift pairs, decompose residual error by class and spatial-frequency band, compare against phase-perturbation sensitivity curves.
main_risk: Amplitude/phase decomposition is a linear-systems view of a nonlinear problem; treat as first-order analysis and validate conclusions behave stably.

one_liner: Part of every 'domain gap' is an annotation-quality gap: target-domain labels are often worse, inflating measured shift.
problem: Cross-domain evaluation assumes both domains' labels are equally good, but target datasets (developing-region driving data, rare-modality medical sets) often have younger annotation pipelines - measured 'domain gaps' partially reflect reference-quality differences.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: expert re-annotation of target-domain test samples to source-grade quality reduces measured domain gaps by a nontrivial fraction (>15% of the gap for at least some benchmark pairs), and the label-quality component is diagnosable WITHOUT re-annotation via model-consensus statistics - separating true shift from reference noise in every cross-domain claim.
why_important: Domain-gap numbers steer research priorities and product decisions; systematically inflated gaps misdirect both.
why_possibly_novel: Reference-quality decomposition of measured domain gaps is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-annotate 200 target test images at source-grade for 2 benchmark pairs, recompute gaps, validate the consensus-based diagnostic against realized corrections.
main_risk: Which pairs have quality asymmetry is unknown a priori; survey with the diagnostic first, then re-annotate the flagged pairs.

one_liner: Camera height is a geometric shift solvable in closed form: dashcam-to-bodycam transfer needs homography priors, not learned adaptation.
problem: Viewpoint-height shift (vehicle roof vs handheld vs robot-dog height) is treated with generic adaptation machinery, though it is substantially a known geometric transformation of ground-plane layout - suggesting geometry should replace learning for this axis.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for height shifts, ground-plane homography-based training augmentation (exact geometric reprojection given height priors) recovers more of the cross-height performance gap than generic UDA methods at a fraction of the complexity, and the residual after geometric correction isolates the truly appearance-borne component (occlusion pattern changes) - geometry-first decomposition beats learning-first for geometrically-caused shifts.
why_important: A class of shifts where the right answer is 100-year-old projective geometry would recalibrate the learn-everything reflex, with immediate value for robot/drone deployment from vehicle-collected data.
why_possibly_novel: Geometric-vs-learned adaptation head-to-head for height shift is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct height-paired data (multi-mount captures or synthetic), compare homography augmentation vs 3 UDA methods on cross-height segmentation.
main_risk: Homography assumes planar ground; cluttered 3D scenes violate it - measure where the assumption breaks.

one_liner: When is the whole object recoverable from image-level labels alone? Formalize and measure the part-to-whole information gap of CAM-style supervision.
problem: Class-activation-based weak supervision finds discriminative parts, not whole objects (KNOWN limitation). But the field lacks a principled account of WHEN whole-object extent is even inferable from image labels - which classes are structurally recoverable and which need shape priors.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: whole-object recoverability from image-level supervision is predicted by a measurable class property - the mutual information between object presence and non-discriminative object regions' appearance (context-part coupling) - producing a per-class recoverability score that forecasts weak-supervision performance before training and identifies classes where NO CAM-descendant can succeed.
why_important: Ends the per-method trial-and-error of weakly-supervised segmentation with a data-side impossibility diagnostic - saving effort and setting honest expectations.
why_possibly_novel: An information-theoretic recoverability criterion validated against method outcomes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Estimate context-part coupling for 30 classes (via masked-region prediction proxies), correlate with published + reproduced weak-supervision per-class results.
main_risk: Estimating the information quantity is itself model-dependent; triangulate with multiple estimators.

one_liner: Error inheritance coefficient: measure how teacher mistakes replicate into students under pseudo-labeling, per error type.
problem: Self-training assumes student models average away teacher noise, but teacher errors are systematic, and their inheritance rate (which error types replicate vs wash out) has never been itemized for segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: boundary-style errors and context-prior errors inherit at high rates (>70% persistence into students) while stochastic errors wash out, the inheritance coefficient per error type is stable across datasets, and it predicts the ceiling of iterated self-training in advance - pseudo-label pipelines have a computable error-genetics.
why_important: Semi-supervised pipelines dominate practical segmentation; knowing which teacher flaws are heritable tells teams what to fix BEFORE distillation, not after.
why_possibly_novel: Error-type-resolved inheritance measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train teacher, categorize its errors (boundary/semantic/context), train students on pseudo-labels, measure per-type persistence across two generations.
main_risk: Error categorization is partly subjective; use automatic taxonomies with human validation.

one_liner: Why does consistency regularization work - decision-boundary geometry or augmentation coverage? A controlled disentanglement.
problem: Consistency training (agree across augmentations) is the semi-supervised workhorse, credited to two mechanisms with different implications - smoothing decision boundaries in low-density regions vs implicitly expanding data coverage - never separated experimentally for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: holding augmentation-space coverage fixed while varying the consistency term (and vice versa) shows coverage explains most of the gain (consistency acts primarily as data amplification, not geometric smoothing), predicting that consistency helps only where augmentations bridge real distribution gaps - a testable mechanistic account that would demystify a ubiquitous method.
why_important: Mechanism determines when the method fails (augmentation-unreachable variation); the field applies it blind to this boundary.
why_possibly_novel: Coverage-vs-geometry disentanglement for dense consistency training is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Factorial design: supervised-with-augmentation vs consistency-with-matched-augmentation across augmentation families, measure gain attribution on 3 datasets.
main_risk: Perfectly matching coverage across arms is subtle; use augmentation-distribution diagnostics to verify the control.

one_liner: Does object-centric data cause segmentation emergence in SSL? Train DINO-style models on scene-only crops and watch attention objects disappear (or not).
problem: Self-supervised ViTs develop object-segmenting attention (KNOWN: DINO attention maps, Caron et al. 2021). Whether emergence requires object-centric training photos (ImageNet's bias) or arises from the objective on any natural data is an open causal question about where 'free objects' come from.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: training identical SSL recipes on deliberately de-object-centrified data (scene crops with no dominant object, matched scale/diversity) substantially degrades emergent objectness (attention-mask quality drops by half or more), demonstrating that 'objects for free' are inherited from photographic framing bias, not discovered by the objective - with direct implications for SSL on scene-heavy domains (driving, aerial, medical).
why_important: If emergence is data-borne, domains without object-centric framing cannot expect it - explaining known SSL disappointments there and redirecting pretraining design.
why_possibly_novel: Controlled data-causality test for objectness emergence is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train matched small ViTs (DINO recipe) on object-centric vs scene-crop corpora at equal scale, compare emergent attention segmentation quality.
main_risk: Emergence may need scale beyond affordable reruns; use the largest feasible scale and report scaling caveats.

one_liner: Unsupervised segmentation evaluation is circular: Hungarian matching to GT classes rewards granularity luck - novel-class evaluation breaks the illusion.
problem: Unsupervised segmentation reports mIoU after optimally matching discovered clusters to GT classes, which silently forgives arbitrary granularity choices and rewards matching the benchmark's ontology by chance - the evaluation partially measures its own matching step.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: current unsupervised methods' rankings are unstable under matching-protocol changes (over/under-clustering penalties, novel-class holdouts), and a matching-free evaluation (consistency, boundary agreement, cross-image co-segmentation coherence) reorders the field while better predicting downstream usefulness of discovered segments - a substantial fraction of reported 'unsupervised understanding' is matching artifact.
why_important: Unsupervised segmentation guides pretraining research; if its measurement is circular, the field is steering by a broken compass.
why_possibly_novel: Matching-protocol sensitivity audit for unsupervised segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
