minimal_experiment: Re-evaluate 6 unsupervised methods under matching-protocol variants and matching-free criteria, quantify rank instability and downstream predictivity.
main_risk: Matching-free criteria need their own validation; anchor with human usefulness judgments on discovered segments.

one_liner: What fraction of supervised segmentation is recoverable from motion alone? Train with only optical-flow-derived boundaries and count the percentage.
problem: Motion boundaries supervise object boundaries for free in video, but the ceiling of motion-only supervision - what percentage of fully-supervised static segmentation it recovers, and for which classes - has never been established as a reference number.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: motion-derived supervision recovers a class-dependent fraction of supervised performance with a bimodal structure - articulated/mobile classes recover >70% while static-only classes (furniture, buildings) recover near zero - and mobile-class features transfer to static instances of the same classes (motion teaches appearance), quantifying exactly what the 'motion as teacher' hypothesis delivers.
why_important: A reference decomposition for the oldest idea in developmental vision applied to modern models - tells the field which supervision motion can actually replace.
why_possibly_novel: Class-resolved recovery accounting of motion-only supervision is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Derive motion pseudo-labels from unlabeled video (flow discontinuities + temporal grouping), train static segmenters, tabulate per-class recovery on standard benchmarks.
main_risk: Flow quality gates the pseudo-labels; use multiple flow methods to bound sensitivity.

one_liner: Depth discontinuities vs semantic boundaries: map where they disagree, because disagreement zones are exactly what depth-based self-supervision cannot teach.
problem: Depth edges are used as free boundary supervision, assuming co-location with semantic boundaries; the systematic disagreement structure (material boundaries on flat surfaces, depth edges inside objects) defines the method's blind spots but has never been atlased.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: depth-semantic boundary disagreement follows a stable taxonomy (co-planar material transitions, self-occlusion edges within objects, contact boundaries) with measurable per-class rates, and depth-supervised models' errors concentrate precisely in the disagreement atlas - making the atlas a predictive map of where depth supervision fails and where photometric cues must take over.
why_important: Depth self-supervision is scaling with cheap depth sensors and monocular estimators; its predictable blind spots should be known before the ecosystem leans on it.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic disagreement atlasing between boundary types is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On RGB-D datasets with semantic GT, compute the boundary disagreement taxonomy, train depth-boundary-supervised models, verify error concentration in atlas zones.
main_risk: Sensor depth noise inflates disagreement estimates; use high-quality depth subsets for the atlas.

one_liner: Supervision mixing is super-additive: image tags plus a few points beat the sum of their separate contributions - map the synergy matrix.
problem: Weak supervision types (tags, points, scribbles, boxes) are studied in isolation; whether combinations interact synergistically (each resolving the other's ambiguity) or redundantly determines optimal annotation portfolios, and the interaction matrix is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: specific pairs are strongly super-additive (tags resolve point-supervision's class ambiguity; points resolve tags' localization ambiguity) with measurable interaction terms exceeding 20% of individual contributions, while other pairs are redundant (boxes+scribbles) - a supervision-portfolio theory with a measurable payoff matrix that annotation planners can use directly.
why_important: Budget-constrained projects mix supervision types by intuition; a measured synergy matrix upgrades this to portfolio optimization.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic interaction-term measurement across weak-supervision pairs is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Factorial supervision-mix training grid at matched budgets on COCO-derived weak labels, fit interaction terms per pair.
main_risk: Interactions may depend on class geometry; report per class family.

one_liner: Pseudo-label entropy drift is the collapse early-warning: self-training failure is forecastable several epochs before performance falls.
problem: Iterated self-training sometimes collapses (confirmation bias spiral), detected only after damage via labeled validation. A label-free early-warning signal from pseudo-label statistics would make self-training safely automatable.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: collapse events are preceded by a characteristic signature in pseudo-label statistics - falling entropy with rising spatial autocorrelation of confident regions (the model agreeing with itself in growing homogeneous patches) - detectable at least several epochs before labeled-metric decline, with low false-alarm rates on healthy runs; collapse has label-free precursors, making it preventable rather than diagnosable.
why_important: Turns a supervision-hungry safety check into a free one, unblocking self-training on domains with no validation labels at all (the setting where it matters most).
why_possibly_novel: Precursor-signature analysis for self-training collapse is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run many self-training trajectories with varied configs (some induced to collapse), log statistics, train collapse-precursor detector, evaluate lead time and false alarms.
main_risk: Collapse may be multi-modal (different signatures per cause); collect a taxonomy of collapse types.

one_liner: Rich-get-richer amplification in semi-supervised segmentation: fit the exponent by which pseudo-labeling amplifies class imbalance per iteration.
problem: Pseudo-labels over-represent head classes (confident) and starve tail classes, compounding across iterations - the amplification dynamics are known qualitatively but never fitted quantitatively, so nobody can predict end-state imbalance from initial conditions.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-iteration class-frequency evolution under standard self-training follows a measurable multiplicative dynamic (amplification exponent per class predicted by initial confidence gaps), the fitted dynamic accurately forecasts class death after N iterations from iteration-1 statistics, and forecast-guided per-class threshold correction prevents predicted deaths at minimal head-class cost.
why_important: Prediction beats postmortem: teams could know which classes their pipeline will kill before spending the compute.
why_possibly_novel: Fitted amplification dynamics with forecast validation are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (the qualitative bias is KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Instrument self-training on LVIS-style imbalanced data across iterations, fit per-class dynamics, validate forecasts on held-out runs.
main_risk: Dynamics may be architecture/threshold-policy specific; fit across the common policy families.

one_liner: Temporal correspondence is the missing hard-positive: video-mined positives beat augmentation positives for dense contrastive pretraining at matched compute.
problem: Dense contrastive SSL uses augmentation views as positives - geometrically trivial matches that may teach mostly low-level invariance. Video offers positives across real deformation, lighting, and viewpoint changes; the head-to-head value at matched compute is unresolved.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: replacing augmentation positives with tracked temporal correspondences (same surface point across seconds of video) improves downstream segmentation transfer specifically on deformation- and viewpoint-heavy classes by a measurable margin at matched pretraining compute, while degrading nothing - the positive-pair distribution, not the objective, is dense SSL's binding constraint.
why_important: Identifies WHERE dense SSL's remaining headroom lives (pair quality, not loss design), redirecting a crowded methods literature toward data construction. KNOWN: temporal SSL works exist; the controlled matched-compute pair-source comparison is the missing piece. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
why_possibly_novel: Pair-source-isolated comparison at matched compute.
minimal_experiment: Pretrain matched models with augmentation vs correspondence positives from the same video corpus, transfer to 4 segmentation benchmarks, stratify gains by class deformability.
main_risk: Tracking errors poison positives; gate by correspondence confidence and report sensitivity.

one_liner: The language granularity ceiling: measure the boundary precision that text supervision can possibly deliver, and how far CLIP-style dense models sit from it.
problem: Text-supervised dense models learn from captions that describe objects but never boundaries ('a dog on grass' says nothing about fur-edge pixels). The information-theoretic boundary ceiling of language supervision - and whether current models saturate it - is uncharacterized.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: boundary localization precision extractable from caption-supervised models has a hard ceiling well above photometric-edge precision (language never disambiguates within edge-bands), current open-vocabulary segmenters already sit near this ceiling (their boundary errors are irreducible by more text data), and all boundary precision beyond it must come from non-linguistic signals - quantifying an inherent division of labor between supervision modalities.
why_important: Prevents the ecosystem from expecting text scale-up to fix boundaries, and formalizes which supervision each output property requires.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-information ceiling analysis for language supervision is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compare boundary-metric scaling of text-supervised models across text-data scale ladders (available checkpoints), test for saturation against photometric-refinement upper bounds.
main_risk: Ceiling estimation from finite checkpoints is extrapolation; state confidence intervals honestly.

one_liner: EXIF is a weak supervisor: focal length, GPS, and timestamps carry measurable segmentation-relevant priors that models never see.
problem: Every photo carries metadata correlating with scene scale (focal length + distance), content priors (GPS: beach vs city), and lighting (time) - free conditioning information that dense pipelines strip away at ingestion. Whether it buys measurable accuracy is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: conditioning segmentation on cheap metadata embeddings improves per-class accuracy measurably (>1 point mIoU) concentrated in scale-ambiguous and region-typical classes, at zero annotation and negligible compute cost - and the gain SURVIVES metadata noise (wrong GPS) because conditioning is learned soft, quantifying a free-lunch the field discards by habit.
why_important: If a free input channel yields standing gains, every production pipeline is leaving accuracy on the table; also probes how much context priors contribute versus pixels.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic metadata-conditioning accounting for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train matched models with/without metadata conditioning on datasets retaining EXIF (Mapillary-like), itemize per-class gains and noise robustness.
main_risk: Metadata correlates with dataset collection artifacts; test cross-dataset to ensure priors are real, not leakage.

one_liner: SAM-generated panoptic pseudo-labels have a characteristic error anatomy: itemize it before the ecosystem trains a generation of models on it.
problem: Pipelines increasingly auto-label with SAM masks + classifier-assigned classes. The systematic error structure of this label source (granularity mismatches, boundary style, class-boundary misalignment) - and its downstream inheritance - is undocumented while adoption accelerates.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: SAM-pipeline pseudo-labels exhibit a stable error anatomy (over-segmentation of textured objects, under-segmentation of adjacent same-class instances, systematic part-whole granularity flips per class) quantifiably different from human-label noise, and models trained on them inherit the anatomy at high fidelity - making 'SAM-labeled' datasets scientifically distinct references whose results cannot be compared naively against human-labeled baselines.
why_important: Ecosystem-scale quality control: the field is about to run many comparisons confounded by label provenance without a characterization of the confound.
why_possibly_novel: Error-anatomy characterization of SAM-pipeline labels is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Generate SAM pseudo-labels on human-labeled benchmarks, itemize disagreement taxonomy, train on each, compare inherited error profiles.
main_risk: Anatomy depends on the assembly pipeline variant; characterize the 2-3 dominant public recipes.

one_liner: Cross-scene object co-occurrence mining: the same physical object photographed in different scenes is a free supervision pair nobody harvests.
problem: Web archives contain the same objects (landmarks, products, individual animals) across many scenes and conditions - instance-level correspondence at scale without labels. Its value as dense supervision (this exact thing, varied context) is unassessed.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: instance-matched cross-scene pairs (minable via retrieval) provide supervision that specifically improves segmentation invariance to context and lighting (the axes those pairs vary) beyond what within-scene or augmentation pairs teach, measurable as targeted transfer gains on context-shifted evaluations - a distinct, harvestable supervision signal between category-level and augmentation-level.
why_important: Identifies an untapped intermediate supervision granularity (instance-across-context) with a concrete mining path from existing archives.
why_possibly_novel: Instance-across-context supervision harvesting for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Mine product/landmark instance pairs via retrieval, add correspondence objectives to SSL pretraining, evaluate context-shift transfer against matched controls.
main_risk: Retrieval false matches inject noise; precision-gate the mining and measure the noise sensitivity curve.

one_liner: Self-training drifts toward the blob prior: iterated pseudo-labeling smooths mask shapes measurably generation by generation.
problem: Each self-training generation re-learns from its own smoothed outputs; shape detail (concavities, thin parts) may erode cumulatively - a mask-space analogue of repeated compression, unmeasured across generations.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: shape-complexity statistics of pseudo-labels (boundary tortuosity, concavity counts, thin-part frequency) decline monotonically across self-training generations at a measurable rate, the decline transfers to real-image predictions (the model becomes blob-biased everywhere), and shape-diverse anchor supervision (retaining a small human-labeled shape-rich subset each generation) arrests the drift - iterated self-training has a quantifiable shape half-life.
why_important: Multi-generation self-training underlies auto-labeling factories; shape erosion would be a compounding quality tax invisible to IoU until late.
why_possibly_novel: Generational shape-statistics tracking is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run 5 self-training generations, track shape statistics of labels and predictions, test anchor-subset arrest of the drift.
main_risk: Confounded with genuine error correction (some smoothing removes noise); separate via shape-known synthetic insets.

one_liner: Cross-class shape transfer: can point-supervised rare classes borrow shape models from shape-similar head classes, and can we predict which donor helps?
problem: Point supervision localizes but cannot teach shape. Head classes have rich learned shape models that might transfer to shape-similar tail classes (scissors borrowing from pliers) - but shape-donorship has no predictive theory.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: point-supervised tail-class mask quality improves substantially when the model has a shape-similar head class (measurable donor effect), donor benefit is predicted by shape-descriptor distance between classes (not semantic distance), and adversarial donor pairs (semantically close, shape-far: snake vs lizard) actively hurt - shape, not semantics, is the transferable currency for mask completion under weak supervision.
why_important: Provides a principled rule for which tail classes weak supervision suffices for (shape-donor available) versus which need full masks - direct annotation-planning value.
why_possibly_novel: Predictive shape-donorship analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Construct donor-controlled training sets (include/exclude shape-similar head classes), train point-supervised models, regress tail mask quality on donor shape distance.
main_risk: Disentangling shape from co-occurrence and context similarity requires careful class-set design.

one_liner: Do semi-supervised methods still matter under DINOv2-grade features? Systematic re-evaluation of SSL-for-segmentation on top of modern foundations.
problem: The semi-supervised segmentation literature largely predates strong foundation features; its methods were designed for label-starved randomly-initialized or ImageNet-pretrained regimes. Whether their gains survive when the backbone already encodes most structure is the field's uncomfortable open question.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on DINOv2-class frozen features, the gains of leading semi-supervised methods shrink to a small fraction of their reported values (foundation features already deliver what pseudo-labeling used to add), with the surviving gains concentrated in dataset-specific ontology learning - a large part of the sub-field's methodology is obsolete in the foundation regime, and honest re-baselining would reset its research agenda.
why_important: Prevents continued investment in methods whose problem has been dissolved (not solved) by pretraining progress; recalibrates what semi-supervision is FOR now.
why_possibly_novel: Foundation-regime re-baselining of the semi-supervised segmentation literature is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Re-run 6 leading semi-supervised methods with modern frozen/fine-tuned foundations across label budgets, compare gain profiles against original settings.
main_risk: Provocative framing invites pushback on implementation fairness; pre-register protocols and use authors' code where available.

one_liner: Boundary noise and region noise are different diseases: dense-label noise robustness has two regimes with opposite remedies.
problem: Label-noise-robust learning treats mask noise as one phenomenon, but boundary jitter (correct region, wrong edges) and region noise (wrong areas included/excluded) plausibly corrupt learning through different mechanisms needing different treatments - the two-regime structure is unverified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: controlled noise-type injection shows boundary noise degrades boundary metrics but leaves region learning nearly intact (models average jitter away) while region noise poisons both (models learn the wrong extent), robustness techniques sort cleanly by which regime they address, and real datasets' noise composition (measurable) predicts which technique family will help - a diagnostic-then-treat framework replacing one-size-fits-all noise robustness.
why_important: Noise-robust training choices currently ignore noise composition; matching treatment to diagnosis is basic but absent.
why_possibly_novel: Noise-type-regime decomposition for dense labels is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Inject calibrated boundary vs region noise on clean datasets, map degradation profiles, classify robustness methods by regime, validate on real noisy datasets.
main_risk: Real noise mixes both types; the composition estimator is the load-bearing deliverable.

one_liner: The granularity control problem: unsupervised instance discovery finds parts or groups unpredictably - measure what determines the discovered granularity.
problem: Clustering-based unsupervised instance discovery returns segments at uncontrolled granularity (wheels vs cars vs traffic). What data and algorithmic factors determine discovered granularity - and whether it can be dialed - is the unsolved usability question of the area.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: discovered granularity is predictable from measurable factors (feature layer depth, clustering scale parameter, and crucially the training data's own object-scale statistics), granularity is approximately a monotonic function of a single identifiable direction in hyperparameter space (a 'granularity dial' exists), and dial positions transfer across datasets after object-scale normalization - unsupervised discovery is controllable once its determinants are mapped.
why_important: Uncontrolled granularity blocks all practical use of unsupervised discovery; a validated dial converts it from curiosity to tool.
why_possibly_novel: Granularity-determinant mapping is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep the candidate factors on multi-granularity-annotated data (PartImageNet-style), measure discovered-granularity response surfaces, test dial transfer.
main_risk: Granularity may be irreducibly multi-modal per image; report distributional (not scalar) dial behavior.

one_liner: One labeled frame per video: quantify the propagation-quality law as a function of motion complexity to price video weak supervision.
problem: The cheapest video supervision is one labeled frame per clip, propagated by tracking. Its effective label quality varies wildly with clip content, and without a predictive law relating motion complexity to propagated-label quality, annotation planners cannot price this supervision.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: propagated-label quality decays with measurable clip statistics (flow magnitude variance, occlusion event rate, deformation energy) following a stable fitted law, the law transfers across trackers (it reflects content difficulty, not tracker identity), and law-guided clip selection (label the frames whose propagation will be reliable) yields dataset-quality improvements at fixed budget over uniform or random frame choice.
why_important: Converts video annotation planning from guesswork to forecast, with immediate value for every VOS/video-dataset builder.
why_possibly_novel: Fitted propagation-quality laws with planning application are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Propagate labels on fully-annotated video benchmarks, fit quality-vs-statistics laws across trackers, validate selection policy at matched budgets.
main_risk: Law stability across domains (sports vs surgery) needs testing; fit per domain and compare.

one_liner: Layered source files (PSD/SVG) are the largest untapped mask corpus: design assets contain millions of human-made segmentations nobody trains on.
problem: Designers produce layered compositions (product cutouts, photo composites, vector scenes) whose layers ARE segmentation masks with human-grade boundaries - a massive, growing, permissively-licensed-in-part corpus outside the field's data pipeline entirely.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: masks harvested from layered design files (deduplicated, quality-filtered) constitute a boundary-quality distribution SUPERIOR to crowdsourced polygons (designers cut edges pixel-perfectly for a living), pretraining on them transfers measurably to natural-image segmentation (especially boundary metrics), and their bias profile (product-centric, studio-lit) is quantifiable and complementary to web-photo datasets - a new data source with different economics than annotation.
why_important: Data sources, not methods, have driven recent leaps; a large orthogonal mask corpus with professional boundary quality could matter more than another architecture.
why_possibly_novel: Design-file mask harvesting at scale is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Harvest masks from openly-licensed layered assets, quantify boundary-quality distribution vs COCO, pretrain and measure transfer on boundary-heavy benchmarks.
main_risk: Licensing and composition bias; both are characterizable and the bias may complement (not duplicate) existing sources.

one_liner: What can sound NOT teach about segmentation? Build the taxonomy of audio-supervisable versus audio-invisible visual structure.
problem: Audio-visual segmentation learns to segment sounding objects (KNOWN field: AVS benchmarks exist). But the systematic limits - which object properties and classes audio supervision can never reach (silent, ambient-sound, many-to-one sources) - are uncharted, leaving the modality's true supervision value unquantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: audio supervision produces segmentation competence sharply stratified by a definable acoustic taxonomy (impulsive-sound rigid objects learn well; continuous-drone sources learn poorly; silent classes learn only via co-occurrence hitchhiking, measurable as indirect transfer), and the hitchhiking effect (silent objects learned through sounding companions) is a quantifiable, previously unmeasured supervision pathway.
why_important: Prevents over-claiming of audio-visual learning while identifying its genuine (and surprising: hitchhiking) contributions - honest boundaries for a fashionable modality.
why_possibly_novel: Supervision-limit taxonomy with hitchhiking quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train audio-visually on video corpora, evaluate per-class against the acoustic taxonomy, isolate hitchhiking via co-occurrence-controlled test sets.
main_risk: Taxonomy boundaries are fuzzy (most objects CAN sound); define by empirical sound-emission rates in the corpus.

one_liner: Physical support constraints prune impossible masks: 'objects rest on surfaces' as a validity filter measurably improves weak-supervision pipelines.
problem: Weakly-supervised masks routinely violate physics (floating fragments, gravity-defying extents), yet physical plausibility (support relations, contact consistency) is never used as a filter - a source of constraint that requires no labels at all.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a support-consistency checker (estimating ground plane and contact relations, flagging unsupported mask fragments) rejects pseudo-label errors with high precision (most flagged masks are indeed wrong), integrating it into self-training measurably improves final models, and the improvement concentrates on exactly the error types (floating fragments, shadow inclusion) that confidence-based filtering cannot catch - physics is an orthogonal, free filter for label factories.
why_important: Pseudo-label filtering currently relies solely on model confidence (circular); an independent physical validity channel breaks the circularity cheaply.
why_possibly_novel: Support-relation filtering for pseudo-label pipelines is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement plausibility checker on self-training pipelines for driving/indoor data, measure flag precision and end-model gains vs confidence-only filtering.
main_risk: Physics checks fail on genuinely airborne/occluded-support objects; measure the false-flag taxonomy.

one_liner: Annotation-free model ranking: can cross-model consensus plus perturbation stability rank segmentation models without any ground truth?
problem: Choosing among models for a new unlabeled domain currently requires labeling an evaluation set - often the deployment bottleneck. Whether label-free signals (inter-model agreement patterns, perturbation stability, physical plausibility) can reproduce GT-based rankings is a practical meta-question with scattered, task-inconsistent prior evidence.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a composite label-free ranking signal reproduces GT rankings with high fidelity (rank correlation >0.8) when candidate models are architecturally diverse, but FAILS predictably when candidates share training lineage (shared blind spots defeat consensus) - and the failure condition is detectable from the agreement structure itself, yielding a self-aware evaluation-free ranking protocol with known validity conditions.
why_important: Deployment teams face this exact decision weekly; a validated protocol WITH its validity detector would be adopted immediately.
why_possibly_novel: Validity-aware label-free ranking for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Across 10 datasets and 12 models of varied lineage, compare label-free composite rankings against GT rankings, characterize failure conditions by lineage overlap.
main_risk: Lineage overlap is becoming universal (everything descends from few foundations) - which itself would be a headline finding about ecosystem monoculture.

one_liner: Dense-prediction scaling laws diverge from classification: boundary quality scales with a smaller exponent than region accuracy - fit both.
problem: Scaling laws exist for classification/LLMs (KNOWN), but dense prediction may scale differently per output property: region-level semantics might follow data/model power laws while boundary precision saturates early (limited by resolution and label noise, not knowledge). No one has fitted property-resolved scaling curves.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: fitting scaling curves separately for region metrics and boundary metrics across model/data ladders reveals significantly different exponents (boundary exponent near zero beyond moderate scale - scale does not buy sharpness), implying the field's scaling investments improve WHAT models segment but not HOW WELL they trace it - a structural argument for redirecting boundary research away from scale.
why_important: Scaling strategy is the biggest resource decision in the field; property-resolved laws would show which problems scale can and cannot solve.
why_possibly_novel: Property-decomposed scaling analysis for segmentation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train/collect model ladders (existing checkpoint series + controlled small-scale runs), fit region-vs-boundary scaling exponents with confidence intervals.
main_risk: Boundary metrics hit label-noise floors that masquerade as saturation; use metrology-grade evaluation subsets (see physical-GT benchmark idea).

one_liner: The probing atlas: layer-by-layer, which foundation models linearly encode boundaries, parts, materials, and occlusion - a standardized dense-knowledge inventory.
problem: Claims like 'DINOv2 knows objects' rest on scattered probes with incompatible protocols. The field lacks a standardized, property-resolved inventory of what dense information each foundation model encodes linearly, at which layer, at what spatial precision.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a standardized probing battery (boundaries, part hierarchies, material vs shape, occlusion ordering, metric size) across major foundations will reveal strongly model-family-specific knowledge profiles (contrastive models encode materials better; MAE-style encode layout better; SAM encodes boundary-ownership uniquely) that PREDICT downstream fine-tuning outcomes per task better than aggregate benchmark scores - knowledge profiles, not leaderboard positions, should drive backbone selection.
why_important: Backbone choice is every project's first decision, currently made by leaderboard folklore; a validated knowledge inventory would replace it with measurement.
why_possibly_novel: Standardized cross-foundation dense-probing with downstream-predictivity validation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build the probe battery on 5 properties x 6 foundations x all layers, correlate profile-task match scores with realized fine-tuning outcomes on 8 tasks.
main_risk: Linear probes underestimate nonlinearly-encoded knowledge; include lightweight nonlinear probes as sensitivity analysis.

one_liner: Sub-patch information is not lost - it hides in neighboring tokens: measure recoverable sub-tokenization detail across ViT foundations.
problem: Patch tokenization (14-16px) supposedly destroys sub-patch spatial detail, capping dense tasks. But convolution-free ViTs may distribute sub-patch information across neighboring tokens' interactions - whether fine detail is destroyed or merely delocalized is a measurable representational question.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: sub-patch edge positions are decodable from local token NEIGHBORHOODS (not single tokens) at precision well below patch size (2-4px) in mid layers, decoding precision varies strongly across pretraining objectives, and the delocalized detail is exactly what boundary-refinement heads fail to exploit - foundation features contain more sharpness than any current decoder extracts.
why_important: If detail survives delocalized, boundary quality is a readout problem (fixable cheaply), not a representation problem (needing new pretraining) - a fork in the road for boundary research.
why_possibly_novel: Neighborhood-decoding analysis of sub-patch information is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train sub-pixel edge-position probes on token neighborhoods across layers/models using synthetic exact-edge stimuli, map recoverable precision.
main_risk: Synthetic edges may over-estimate recoverability on natural texture; validate on the physical-GT benchmark stimuli.

one_liner: Attention-sink artifacts corrupt dense features in predictable spatial patterns: map the damage and its downstream cost per task.
problem: KNOWN: ViTs develop high-norm artifact tokens (Darcet et al., 'Vision Transformers Need Registers'). What remains unmeasured is the spatial structure of artifact damage in dense downstream tasks - where in the image artifacts land, which classes suffer, and how much performance the artifacts actually cost end-to-end.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: artifact tokens localize preferentially in low-information regions (sky, walls) but their attention distortion damages predictions in a measurable halo AROUND those regions (displaced errors), the per-task cost is significant for segmentation but negligible for classification (explaining why the problem went unnoticed), and artifact-location prediction enables test-time feature cleaning worth a consistent fraction of the gap to register-equipped models.
why_important: Quantifies a known pathology's real dense-task cost and offers retrofit mitigation for the enormous installed base of artifact-bearing checkpoints.
why_possibly_novel: Spatial damage-mapping and retrofit-cleaning accounting is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (the artifact phenomenon itself is KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Localize artifacts across images, correlate with spatial error maps on segmentation, implement cleaning, measure recovered performance vs register-model upper bound.
main_risk: Artifact behavior differs across model families; scope claims per family.

one_liner: Generative vs discriminative pretraining for boundaries: diffusion features encode edges sharper than contrastive features - a controlled spectral comparison.
problem: Diffusion models must synthesize exact boundaries (generation demands sharpness), while contrastive objectives reward invariance (blur tolerance). Whether generative pretraining therefore yields sharper dense features - controlled for data and scale - is a fundamental objective-level question tangled in uncontrolled comparisons.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched data and compute, diffusion-pretrained features support higher boundary-precision readout (measurable via edge-position probing and boundary metrics) while contrastive features support better semantic discrimination - a principled objective-property tradeoff, implying optimal dense systems should read boundaries and semantics from DIFFERENT pretraining lineages.
why_important: Resolves a foundational which-objective-for-what question with design consequences for every dense pipeline.
why_possibly_novel: Matched-budget objective comparison focused on boundary spectra is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (uncontrolled diffusion-feature studies are KNOWN to exist).
minimal_experiment: Pretrain matched mid-scale models (diffusion, contrastive, MAE) on identical data, run boundary-precision and semantic probes, compare property profiles.
main_risk: Matched-budget pretraining is expensive at meaningful scale; use the largest affordable scale with scaling-trend checks.

one_liner: What makes a good visual in-context example? Retrieval laws for one-shot segmentation prompting with image-mask pairs.
problem: Visual in-context segmentation (prompt with example image-mask pairs, e.g. SegGPT-style - KNOWN to exist) is acutely sensitive to support-example choice, but support selection is folk art; the quantitative laws (what similarity dimensions matter, how gains scale with support-set size and diversity) are unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in-context segmentation quality is predicted by a learnable composite of support-query similarities where POSE and SCALE similarity dominate semantic similarity (opposite to text-LLM intuitions), gains saturate at very few supports (2-4) unless supports are diversity-selected, and a retrieval policy trained on these laws beats random/semantic retrieval by a large margin - in-context vision has its own retrieval science distinct from NLP's.
why_important: In-context dense models are the most annotation-efficient adaptation path; their usability hinges entirely on support retrieval, currently unprincipled.
why_possibly_novel: Support-retrieval law-fitting for dense in-context learning is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Sweep support choice along controlled similarity axes on in-context segmenters, fit gain predictors, validate learned retrieval on held-out tasks.
main_risk: Laws may be model-specific; test across 2-3 in-context architectures.

one_liner: When does nearest-neighbor label transfer beat fine-tuning? Map the regime boundary for non-parametric segmentation over foundation features.
problem: With strong frozen features, segmenting by retrieving similar labeled patches and transferring their labels (non-parametric) competes with parametric fine-tuning. The regime map - along labeled-set size, domain shift, and class granularity - of which paradigm wins where has not been drawn.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: nearest-neighbor transfer dominates fine-tuning below a measurable labeled-data threshold (a few hundred masks) and under moderate shift (retrieval adapts instance-wise; parameters overfit), while fine-tuning wins on fine-grained class boundaries requiring feature reshaping - and the crossover locations are predictable from feature-space class separability statistics, giving practitioners a measurement-driven paradigm selector.
why_important: The low-label regime is where most real projects start; knowing when to skip training entirely (retrieval only) saves widespread wasted effort.
why_possibly_novel: Paradigm regime-mapping with predictive crossover is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Grid over labeled-set size x shift x granularity comparing kNN-transfer vs fine-tuning on frozen DINOv2/SAM features, fit crossover predictors.
main_risk: kNN implementation quality (feature aggregation, spatial priors) strongly affects the frontier; use well-tuned versions of both paradigms.

one_liner: Resolution extrapolation failures are radially structured: positional-encoding interpolation breaks dense prediction from the image border inward.
problem: Models trained at low resolution are deployed at high resolution via positional-embedding interpolation; failures are treated as uniform degradation, but interpolation error geometry (extrapolation at borders, compression at center) predicts spatially structured damage nobody has mapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: under resolution extrapolation, dense-prediction error increases with a characteristic radial profile (worst at borders and corners, tracking positional-embedding interpolation error), the profile shape is predictable from the embedding scheme (learned absolute vs RoPE-style vs conv-derived), and border-cropped evaluation recovers most of the reported extrapolation gap - 'resolution generalization failure' is substantially a positional-geometry artifact with scheme-specific signatures.
why_important: Correct attribution changes the fix (positional scheme surgery, not retraining) and warns that border-heavy applications (panorama, document edges) suffer most.
why_possibly_novel: Radial error-profiling of resolution extrapolation is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate models across resolution ladders, map spatial error profiles per positional scheme, test border-crop recovery predictions.
main_risk: Content statistics also vary radially in photos (center bias); control with content-shuffled synthetic layouts.

one_liner: Do vision foundations share an object space? Measure cross-model representational alignment specifically on object-level axes, not global features.
problem: The platonic-representation debate (do independently trained models converge?) has been argued with global similarity metrics (KNOWN: representational-alignment literature exists); whether alignment holds specifically for OBJECT-level structure (boundaries, part decompositions, instance separations) - the part dense prediction cares about - is finer-grained and unresolved.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: object-level alignment between foundations (measured by transferability of object-axis linear maps between SAM/DINOv2/CLIP feature spaces) is substantially higher than global feature alignment, alignment grows with each model's downstream dense performance (convergence tracks competence), and residual misalignment localizes to specific properties (part granularity, boundary ownership) that differ by pretraining objective - the ecosystem is converging on WHAT objects are but not on their decomposition.
why_important: Convergence structure determines whether ensembling/stitching pays and what unique value each pretraining lineage retains - portfolio-level strategy for the field.
why_possibly_novel: Object-axis-resolved alignment measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Fit cross-model linear maps on object-centric probe tasks, quantify transfer per property, correlate alignment with performance across checkpoint ladders.
main_risk: Alignment metrics are subtle (CKA critiques are KNOWN); use multiple alignment measures and behavioral (not just geometric) tests.

one_liner: Vocabulary is a confounder in open-vocabulary segmentation: performance depends on distractor-list composition as much as on the model - benchmark the benchmark.
problem: Open-vocabulary segmentation scores depend on the evaluation vocabulary (which distractor classes compete), yet benchmarks fix arbitrary small vocabularies, making cross-paper numbers incomparable and inflating apparent competence relative to open-world deployment with thousands of candidate labels.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: OV segmentation scores decay predictably with vocabulary size and semantic density (distractor proximity), model RANKINGS flip between small-vocabulary and large-vocabulary regimes (some models are precision-optimized, others recall-optimized), and reporting vocabulary-scaling CURVES instead of point scores restores comparability - one protocol fix rescuing an incoherent evaluation ecosystem.
why_important: OV segmentation is the field's deployment-facing product; incomparable evaluation blocks real progress assessment.
why_possibly_novel: Vocabulary-scaling evaluation protocol with rank-flip demonstration is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate 6 OV models across controlled vocabulary ladders (size x density), demonstrate rank instability, propose and validate curve-based reporting.
main_risk: Overlaps conceptually with confidence-dilution idea (W2-A-0197) but targets evaluation protocol rather than confidence mechanics; keep both with distinct deliverables.

one_liner: How small can a decoder be? Localize where dense-task capacity actually lives by scaling decoders down over frozen foundations.
problem: Dense architectures allocate large decoders by convention, but if frozen foundation features already contain the needed information, decoder capacity might shrink drastically without loss - the capacity-localization question (encoder vs decoder) has never been answered with systematic decoder-scaling curves.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: over strong frozen encoders, segmentation performance vs decoder size shows a sharp knee at surprisingly small capacity (<1% of encoder parameters) for region metrics, but boundary metrics keep improving with decoder size (boundary computation genuinely lives in the decoder), and the knee position shifts predictably with encoder quality - a capacity-localization law separating what encoders know from what decoders compute.
why_important: Design efficiency (edge deployment) plus scientific attribution: knowing where each output property is computed directs both compression and improvement efforts.
why_possibly_novel: Property-resolved decoder-scaling laws are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Decoder-size ladders over 3 frozen foundations x 3 datasets, fit property-resolved capacity curves, locate knees vs encoder quality.
main_risk: Decoder architecture family may matter as much as size; replicate across 2 families.

one_liner: How precisely can MLLMs localize without a pixel decoder? Measure the text-coordinate segmentation ceiling of GPT-4V-class models.
problem: Multimodal LLMs describe and point at image content via text coordinates (boxes, polygon vertices as numbers). Their intrinsic localization precision - the ceiling of language-emitted geometry - determines whether pixel decoders are necessary or just convenient, and it has not been carefully measured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: MLLM text-coordinate boundary precision plateaus around coarse levels (5-10% of object scale) regardless of prompt engineering (a representation bottleneck, not an interface artifact - verifiable by probing whether visual tokens contain finer position information than the text head extracts), implying pixel-space readouts are structurally required for boundary tasks while detection-grade localization is already language-achievable.
why_important: Architectural guidance for the merging of MLLMs and dense vision: what must be grafted on versus what emerges from scale.
why_possibly_novel: Ceiling measurement with internal-information comparison (tokens vs text head) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Elicit coordinate outputs from 4 MLLMs across precision-demanding tasks, compare against linear probes on their visual tokens for the same geometry.
main_risk: Closed-model probing is limited; use open MLLMs for the internal-information leg.

one_liner: Does a granularity dial exist in prompt space? Search for a continuous direction controlling part-object-group level in promptable segmenters.
problem: SAM's granularity is controlled crudely (multimask choice); whether the underlying prompt-embedding space contains a continuous, monotonic granularity direction (allowing smooth part-to-whole dialing) is a concrete representational geometry question with direct interface value.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a single direction in SAM's prompt-token space monotonically controls output granularity across categories (found via paired part/whole supervision on a small set, transferring zero-shot to unseen categories), demonstrating granularity is linearly represented - and its transferability failure cases (categories with non-nested part structures) reveal where object decomposition is genuinely non-hierarchical.
why_important: A working dial would fix promptable segmentation's most common practical failure (wrong granularity), and the geometry finding informs how composition is encoded.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt-space granularity-direction search is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Fit granularity directions on part-annotated categories (PACO/PartImageNet), test zero-shot transfer, characterize monotonicity and failure taxonomy.
main_risk: Granularity may be encoded nonlinearly or per-category; a negative result still maps the encoding structure.

one_liner: Trace a bad mask to its training data: feasibility of influence-function attribution for promptable segmentation failures.
problem: When SAM fails on a mask, nobody can say WHICH training data (or absence thereof) is responsible - data attribution methods exist for classification (KNOWN: influence functions, TracIn lineage) but their feasibility, cost, and validity for billion-mask promptable models is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: scalable attribution approximations (gradient-sketch retrieval over training shards) identify training-set regions whose removal/addition causally changes specific failure behaviors (validated by targeted fine-tuning on attributed shards fixing the failure at above-random rates), making failure-driven data curation - fix the model by editing data, not weights - a practical loop for segmentation foundations.
why_important: Data curation is the main lever for foundation model quality; closing the failure-to-data loop would industrialize it.
why_possibly_novel: Attribution-driven repair loops for dense foundations are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On an open SAM-scale-down reproduction, attribute 100 failure cases, run targeted-data interventions, measure repair rates vs random-data controls.
main_risk: Attribution approximations may be too noisy at scale; the scaled-down setting bounds feasibility honestly.

one_liner: Shared blind spots across the model zoo: pixels where ALL foundations fail mark data-ecosystem holes, not architecture limits.
problem: Per-model error analysis cannot distinguish 'this architecture's weakness' from 'nobody's training data covers this'. Cross-model failure correlation - the shared-vs-unique error decomposition across independent lineages - has never been systematically computed for dense prediction.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a large fraction of segmentation errors (>40%) are shared across architecturally-independent models (data-ecosystem holes: web-photo biases, absent domains), shared-error regions are predictable from data-frequency estimates (how rare such pixels are online), and unique errors cluster by architectural family - producing an actionable split: fix shared errors with data expeditions, unique errors with architecture work.
why_important: The field's error-fixing effort is misallocated without this decomposition; shared holes need collection campaigns no single lab's method work can fill.
why_possibly_novel: Ecosystem-level error-correlation decomposition is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run 10 diverse models on 5 benchmarks, decompose per-pixel error correlation, correlate shared-error regions with web-frequency proxies.
main_risk: Lineage independence is eroding (shared data everywhere); quantify lineage overlap as a covariate.

one_liner: Image pretraining plus explicit tracking versus native video pretraining: budget-matched showdown for dense video tasks.
problem: Video foundation models cost far more to train than image models; whether native temporal pretraining buys anything over strong image features composed with lightweight tracking machinery - at matched total budget - is the central economics question of video representation learning, never cleanly tested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: for video segmentation tasks dominated by appearance continuity, image-pretraining + tracking matches or beats native video pretraining at equal budget (temporal structure is cheap to add post hoc), but a specific task subset (occlusion reasoning, motion-defined objects, temporal event boundaries) shows irreducible native-video advantages - defining precisely WHICH temporal capabilities require temporal pretraining and which do not.
why_important: Directly prices the video-pretraining premium and would redirect large compute investments if the composed alternative suffices for most tasks.
why_possibly_novel: Budget-matched composed-vs-native comparison with capability decomposition is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Match total budgets between (image SSL + tracking head) and video SSL pipelines, evaluate across a task battery stratified by temporal-dependence, itemize where native wins.
main_risk: Budget matching across paradigms has degrees of freedom; pre-register the accounting rules.

one_liner: Can a segmentation foundation be trained on zero real images? Push procedural-data pretraining (fractals, formulas, simulations) to its dense-prediction limit.
problem: Formula/fractal pretraining works surprisingly well for classification (KNOWN: FractalDB line of work exists); whether procedurally-generated data - with its perfect free labels and zero licensing/privacy burden - can carry DENSE pretraining to competitive levels, and what procedural ingredients matter, is largely unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: procedural pretraining reaches a substantial fraction (>70%) of real-data pretraining transfer for segmentation IF the generator includes specific ingredients - occlusion layering, boundary-complexity distributions matched to natural statistics, and material-like texture gradients - and ingredient ablations identify occlusion structure as the single most transfer-critical property, revealing what dense pretraining actually needs from data (compositional structure, not semantics).
why_important: A viable real-image-free pretraining path solves licensing/privacy constraints (medical!) and scientifically isolates which data properties dense learning consumes.
why_possibly_novel: Ingredient-ablated procedural pretraining for dense tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search beyond the KNOWN classification-focused work.
minimal_experiment: Build parameterized procedural generator, pretrain matched models across ingredient ablations, measure segmentation transfer against real-data controls.
main_risk: The gap may be irreducible for semantic tasks; even so, the ingredient-importance map is standalone valuable.

one_liner: Compression kills boundaries first: quantization and distillation degrade dense outputs in a property-ordered sequence worth mapping.
problem: Model compression is validated on aggregate metrics, but dense-output properties (region semantics, boundary precision, small-object recall, calibration) may degrade at very different rates - the degradation ORDER determines which applications can use compressed models, and it is unmeasured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: across compression methods (quantization, pruning, distillation), dense properties degrade in a consistent order - boundary precision first, small-object recall second, region semantics last (mirroring their dependence on high-frequency feature content) - and the ordering enables property-targeted compression (protecting boundary-critical channels identified by sensitivity analysis) that shifts the frontier for boundary-dependent applications.
why_important: Edge deployment of segmentation is exploding; property-ordered degradation maps tell each application what compression it can afford.
why_possibly_novel: Property-resolved compression analysis for dense prediction is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Compress 3 segmentation models along method ladders, track property-resolved metrics, test the protection scheme on boundary-critical channels.
main_risk: Ordering may vary by architecture; establish across families before claiming universality.

one_liner: Decode what learned dense prompts encode: continuous prompt vectors trained for segmentation tasks are interpretable dataset fingerprints.
problem: Visual prompt tuning learns small parameter sets that adapt frozen models to datasets; these vectors must encode the dataset's distinctive properties (class priors, boundary conventions, granularity), but nobody has tried to READ them - an interpretability opportunity with practical payoffs (dataset similarity, transfer prediction).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: learned dense-task prompts are decodable - prompt-space distances between datasets predict cross-dataset transfer performance (prompt geometry is a transfer map), prompt arithmetic works (combining prompts of dataset A's classes with dataset B's boundary convention), and specific prompt components isolate annotation-convention information - making prompts both a scientific instrument for dataset comparison and an engineering tool for convention translation.
why_important: A working dataset-fingerprint algebra would answer 'how similar are these datasets' and 'will transfer work' from cheap artifacts instead of expensive experiments.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt-space decoding and arithmetic for dense tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train prompts across 12 datasets on one frozen foundation, test distance-transfer correlation and convention-swap arithmetic on held-out pairs.
main_risk: Prompt solutions are non-unique (different seeds, same behavior); test geometry stability across seeds first.

one_liner: Is promptable segmentation emergent or smooth? Train a mini-SAM scaling series and settle whether the capability has a threshold.
problem: Emergence debates (capabilities appearing suddenly at scale) are unresolved for dense prediction: does promptability - responding correctly to spatial prompts - develop smoothly with scale or exhibit threshold behavior? The SAM training recipe at reduced scales provides a clean testbed nobody has exploited.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: prompt-following ability measured with fine-grained metrics develops SMOOTHLY across a mini-SAM scaling series (no emergence - apparent thresholds in prior anecdotes are metric artifacts, consistent with the KNOWN emergence-as-metric-artifact critique in LLMs), but specific sub-capabilities (negative-prompt understanding, multi-prompt integration) show genuinely delayed development - a capability-resolved developmental timeline for promptable vision.
why_important: Whether capabilities emerge or accrue determines training-investment risk (can you extrapolate from small pilots?) - a first-order question for anyone training dense foundations.
why_possibly_novel: Scaling-series developmental analysis of promptability is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train 6 SAM-recipe models from tiny to small scale on SA-1B subsets, evaluate capability-resolved prompt-following curves with continuous metrics.
main_risk: Mini-scale conclusions may not extrapolate to frontier scale; frame as developmental science with stated bounds.

one_liner: Feature quality is spatially anisotropic: foundation features degrade toward image borders, and panoramic/tiled applications inherit the damage.
problem: Foundation features are treated as spatially homogeneous, but training photos have strong center bias (subjects centered, borders contain periphery), plausibly training center-privileged features - a spatial quality gradient that tiled inference and panorama processing would repeatedly sample at its worst.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: probing tasks show systematic center-to-border feature quality gradients across foundations (matched-content probes decoding worse near borders), the gradient magnitude tracks each training corpus's measured center bias (data-borne, not architectural), and tiling strategies that avoid placing content at tile borders recover measurable accuracy in tiled high-resolution inference - a hidden spatial prior with direct engineering consequences.
why_important: Tiled inference is universal for high-res imagery (satellite, pathology); an unrecognized border penalty means widespread silent quality loss with a cheap layout fix.
why_possibly_novel: Spatial feature-quality gradient measurement is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Probe matched content at controlled positions across foundations, correlate gradients with corpus center-bias statistics, benchmark border-aware tiling.
main_risk: Positional embeddings entangle with content statistics; use content-controlled synthetic placements.

one_liner: Object tokens or distributed objectness? Causal feature-surgery to locate WHERE promptable models represent each object.
problem: Whether SAM-style models maintain discrete object-centric representations (tokens 'owning' objects) or distributed objectness (objects as patterns over patch features) is a resolvable representational question - via causal intervention (ablate/swap candidate representations, observe mask behavior) rather than correlational probing.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: causal interventions will show object identity is carried by a low-rank subspace of the mask-token pathway (swapping it transfers masks between objects; ablating it deletes specific objects while preserving scene features) - promptable models ARE object-centric in a strong causal sense, and the object subspace's dimensionality measures how many objects the model can simultaneously individuate (predicting multi-object interference limits).
why_important: Resolves a foundational representation question with a measurable capacity constant (simultaneous-object limit) that predicts practical failure in crowded scenes.
why_possibly_novel: Causal object-representation surgery on promptable segmenters is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Implement token/subspace swap-and-ablate interventions on SAM's decoder pathway, quantify mask-transfer and deletion specificity, estimate object-subspace rank.
main_risk: Interventions may push activations off-manifold, producing artifacts misread as structure; use manifold-constrained interventions.

one_liner: Transformers' low-frequency bias caps boundary precision architecturally: same-data CNN-vs-ViT boundary spectroscopy.
problem: Spectral-bias theory says different architectures preferentially learn different frequency bands; boundary precision is a high-frequency output property, so architecture-level frequency bias should produce measurable boundary-quality differences at matched data and training - a clean theory-to-practice test never run for segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched data/compute/parameters, boundary-error spectra (error energy vs spatial frequency along contours) show architecture-specific cutoffs consistent with spectral-bias theory (ViTs attenuate high-frequency boundary detail more than CNNs at equal aggregate mIoU), the difference persists across scale, and hybrid stems (conv early, attention late) inherit the CNN cutoff - architecture choice imposes a measurable boundary-frequency ceiling independent of learning.
why_important: Would ground the CNN-vs-ViT debate in a measurable, property-specific law rather than aggregate benchmarks, guiding architecture choice for boundary-critical applications.
why_possibly_novel: Boundary-spectral architecture comparison at matched budgets is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train matched CNN/ViT/hybrid segmenters on identical data, compute boundary error spectra (using the physical-GT stimuli for precision), compare cutoffs.
main_risk: Matched training across architecture families is never perfectly fair; sweep learning configurations and report robustness.

one_liner: Segmentation as retrieval at scale: how does non-parametric mask transfer scale with memory size, and does it ever beat parametric knowledge?
problem: A segmentation system could store millions of labeled region exemplars and segment by retrieval+transfer, scaling knowledge by growing memory rather than retraining - the scaling behavior of memory size versus parametric capacity for dense tasks (retrieval's sweet spots, its ceiling) is uncharted.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: retrieval-based segmentation accuracy scales log-linearly with memory size well past the point where matched-parameter models plateau (memory beats parameters for tail classes and rare configurations), with retrieval's advantage concentrated in the frequency tail while parametric models retain the head - implying optimal systems are frequency-split hybrids, and the crossover frequency is measurable and stable.
why_important: Memory-augmented architectures are rising everywhere else (LLM RAG); establishing the dense-prediction scaling equivalent would guide the next architecture generation.
why_possibly_novel: Memory-scaling laws for dense prediction are UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build exemplar-memory segmenter over frozen features, scale memory across orders of magnitude, compare per-frequency-bin against parametric models at matched total footprint.
main_risk: Retrieval latency and memory engineering may dominate practicality; the science stands regardless of deployment economics.

one_liner: If all strong models converge, ensembles die: test whether dense-model ensemble gains are collapsing generation by generation.
problem: Ensembling assumes error diversity; if foundation-era models increasingly share data, objectives, and representations (monoculture convergence), ensemble gains should be measurably shrinking over model generations - a trend with major implications that nobody has tracked.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: measuring ensemble gain (over best member) across model cohorts by era shows monotonic decline for dense tasks (error-diversity collapse as lineages share SA-1B/LAION-descended data), the decline is steeper than in the classification ecosystem (dense labels are scarcer, forcing more sharing), and remaining diversity concentrates in models with genuinely disjoint data (medical vs web) - quantifying the ecosystem's convergence tax on reliability engineering.
why_important: Safety-critical systems rely on ensembling/redundancy; if diversity is evaporating ecosystem-wide, redundancy-based safety arguments weaken - better to know now, with numbers.
why_possibly_novel: Longitudinal ensemble-gain trend analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble model cohorts by era (2019-2025), measure ensemble gains and error correlations on fixed benchmarks, regress against lineage-overlap measures.
main_risk: Era confounds with scale and performance level; normalize gains by member accuracy and test scale-matched cohorts.

one_liner: Did SA-1B swallow the test sets? Measure foundation-training contamination of segmentation benchmarks with near-duplicate forensics.
problem: Foundation models train on web-scale corpora that plausibly contain benchmark test images (or near-duplicates); for segmentation this contamination has never been quantified, though it silently converts zero-shot claims into memorization measurements.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: near-duplicate detection between foundation training sets (SA-1B, LAION-derived) and standard segmentation test sets (COCO, ADE20K, DAVIS) will find nontrivial contamination rates, per-image zero-shot performance is measurably higher on contaminated items (memorization signal), and decontaminated re-scoring shrinks published zero-shot gaps between foundations - benchmark contamination is a live confounder in dense prediction, not just NLP.
why_important: Zero-shot segmentation claims underpin the foundation-model narrative; contamination-corrected numbers are the ones that matter.
why_possibly_novel: Dense-benchmark contamination forensics is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (NLP contamination studies are KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Run scalable near-dup detection (embedding + hash) between public shards of SA-1B/LAION and test sets, stratify model performance by contamination status.
main_risk: Only public shards are checkable; report bounds, not point estimates, for closed corpora.

one_liner: Correct the test sets: estimate dense-label error rates on major benchmarks and measure how repairs reorder the leaderboards.
problem: KNOWN: classification test sets contain pervasive label errors (Northcutt et al.). Dense benchmarks likely contain region- and boundary-level errors at higher rates (harder annotation), but error-rate estimates and leaderboard sensitivity to repairs do not exist for segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: model-consensus-guided expert re-audit will find pixel-level label fault rates of several percent on major benchmarks (concentrated in occlusion boundaries and class confusions), repairing them changes top-model rankings in a measurable fraction of comparisons, and - critically - the models that gain most from repair are those trained WITHOUT the benchmark's sibling training set (label errors currently favor style-matched models).
why_important: Leaderboards steer the field; if their references are faulty in a direction that favors in-ecosystem models, progress measurement is structurally biased.
why_possibly_novel: Repair-sensitivity analysis of dense leaderboards is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Consensus-flag suspicious regions on 2 benchmarks, expert-adjudicate 3k regions, re-score public models on repaired references.
main_risk: Adjudication of genuinely ambiguous regions; use the three-state protocol (decidable-error vs ambiguous) to keep claims clean.

one_liner: The polygon ceiling: COCO's coarse polygons impose a measurable upper bound on learnable and measurable boundary quality.
problem: COCO masks average few vertices per object; both training signal and evaluation reference inherit this coarseness. The exact ceiling it imposes - on what models can learn and on what evaluation can detect - has not been quantified, though COCO remains the field's central training source.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: comparing COCO polygons against high-fidelity re-annotations will yield a per-size boundary-error floor (the polygon artifact spectrum), models trained on COCO plateau AT this floor (their boundary style measurably mimics polygon geometry - straight-segment artifacts detectable in predictions), and boundary-metric differences between models evaluated on COCO below the floor are meaningless - one number (the ceiling) reframing hundreds of comparisons.
why_important: Establishes when 'better boundaries on COCO' can even be a real claim, and quantifies the training tax of polygon supervision that the ecosystem inherits.
why_possibly_novel: Polygon-artifact ceiling quantification with mimicry detection is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: High-fidelity re-annotation of 500 COCO objects, compute artifact spectra, test for straight-segment mimicry in model predictions, derive the evaluable floor.
main_risk: Re-annotation cost; 500 objects suffice for the spectrum but per-class claims need more.

one_liner: Class definitions drift across dataset versions and papers: 'road' 2016 is not 'road' 2024 - measure semantic versioning debt.
problem: Long-lived benchmarks evolve through relabeling campaigns, errata, and papers' preprocessing choices; the same class name can denote drifting pixel sets across versions, corrupting longitudinal comparisons that the field reads as progress.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: diffing dataset versions and reconstructing papers' actual evaluation pixel-sets will reveal class-definition drift large enough to explain measurable fractions of reported multi-year 'progress' on affected classes, and papers citing the same benchmark differ silently in effective test sets (preprocessing forks) at a rate that makes a subset of published comparisons non-comparable - the field lacks semantic versioning and pays for it in phantom progress.
why_important: Longitudinal progress claims are the field's self-narrative; auditing their consistency is basic metrology.
why_possibly_novel: Version-drift accounting for segmentation benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Diff Cityscapes/ADE versions and 20 papers' preprocessing forks, recompute a fixed model's score under each effective test set, tabulate the spread.
main_risk: Reconstructing papers' exact pipelines is laborious; prioritize the most-cited comparison chains.

one_liner: Effective headroom estimation: how much of each benchmark's remaining error is model-fixable versus reference noise - the saturation audit.
problem: Benchmarks near saturation reward noise-fitting, but the field lacks a standard estimate of each benchmark's effective headroom (remaining error that a correct model could actually reduce), so effort allocation across benchmarks is blind.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: decomposing residual error on major benchmarks (via multi-annotation, model consensus, and ambiguity measurement) will show several popular benchmarks have effective headroom below 2 points (further gains are style-fitting), while others retain large real headroom concentrated in specific classes - and publishing per-benchmark headroom would measurably shift where new methods report results (a testable sociological prediction).
why_important: Effort follows benchmarks; headroom accounting redirects the field's marginal week of work toward real problems.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic headroom estimation across dense benchmarks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Apply the decomposition to 6 benchmarks using existing multi-annotation where available plus targeted re-annotation, publish headroom table.
main_risk: Headroom estimates depend on ambiguity modeling assumptions; report ranges under stated models.

one_liner: Within-benchmark duplication inflates scores: near-duplicate test images act as multipliers on style-matched models.
problem: Test sets assembled from web sources contain internal near-duplicates (same scene, same event, burst shots); metrics implicitly weight duplicated content multiply, favoring models that happen to fit the duplicated styles - the duplication structure of dense benchmarks is unmapped.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: near-duplicate clustering of major test sets will find measurable duplication (several percent of images with intra-set near-dups), deduplicated re-scoring changes method rankings in close comparisons, and duplication is topic-biased (certain scene types over-weighted), meaning current scores encode hidden topical weightings nobody chose deliberately.
why_important: A cheap, definitive hygiene audit; close SOTA races are exactly where duplicate-weighting artifacts decide outcomes.
why_possibly_novel: Intra-benchmark duplication analysis for dense tasks is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Run embedding-based near-dup clustering on 5 test sets, re-score public models deduplicated, report rank sensitivity.
main_risk: Near-dup thresholds are judgment calls; report across threshold sweeps.

one_liner: Segmentation performance by geography of image origin: dense prediction has an unmeasured global-equity profile.
problem: KNOWN: object recognition performs worse on images from lower-income regions (Facebook's Dollar Street analyses). For segmentation - where infrastructure, vehicles, and household objects differ even more visually - the geographic performance profile has not been measured, though these models deploy globally.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: mainstream segmentation models show substantial performance gradients across image-origin geography (worse boundary AND recognition quality in under-represented regions), the gradient persists for supposedly universal classes (person, food, bed) not just region-specific ones, and gradient magnitude correlates with training-corpus geo-distribution estimates - making the data-origin ledger an actionable fairness instrument for dense prediction.
why_important: Segmentation increasingly gates real services (medical triage, agricultural tools, AR); an unmeasured geographic performance cliff is an equity failure waiting to surface.
why_possibly_novel: Geographic stratification of dense-prediction quality is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Annotate geo-diverse image samples (Dollar-Street-style) with masks, evaluate model zoo, regress performance on region and corpus-representation estimates.
main_risk: Annotation quality must be uniform across regions to avoid reproducing the artifact under audit; use one centralized expert team.

one_liner: The sensor gap: benchmarks are smartphone/DSLR photos, deployments are industrial/scientific sensors - quantify the unbenchmarked capture-hardware shift.
problem: Public benchmarks overwhelmingly sample consumer camera output (processed, sharpened, tone-mapped), while deployments run on machine-vision cameras, line-scan sensors, and scientific detectors with alien noise/optics profiles - a capture-hardware distribution gap that no benchmark measures.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models transferred from consumer-photo training to industrial-sensor imagery degrade substantially even for identical scene content (verifiable with dual-capture rigs: consumer + machine-vision camera imaging the same scenes), the degradation localizes to texture- and noise-sensitive classes, and simple sensor-simulation augmentation (noise/optics models) recovers a large fraction - the gap is real, measurable, and cheaply mitigable once acknowledged.
why_important: Industrial vision is a huge deployment share served by benchmarks that never sampled its input distribution; the dual-capture measurement would ground years of anecdotal complaints.
why_possibly_novel: Dual-capture sensor-gap quantification is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Build dual-camera rig, capture 300 matched scenes, evaluate models cross-sensor, test sensor-simulation recovery.
main_risk: One industrial camera does not represent all; use 3 sensor types to bound diversity.

one_liner: PQ's 0.5-IoU matching cliff makes panoptic rankings noise-sensitive: measure how many published gaps live at the threshold.
problem: Panoptic Quality matches predictions to GT at a hard IoU>0.5 threshold; instances near the threshold flip between matched and unmatched under tiny changes, injecting discontinuous noise into scores - the fraction of published PQ differences attributable to near-threshold instances is unknown.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: perturbation analysis (jittering predictions/GT within annotation noise) shows PQ variance is dominated by near-threshold instances, a smooth-matching variant (soft credit around the threshold) reduces ranking noise substantially while preserving interpretation, and re-scoring recent panoptic literature with the smooth variant erases a measurable fraction of published gaps - the metric's discontinuity has been manufacturing significance.
why_important: Metric-induced noise wastes the field's effort ratifying phantom differences; a validated smooth variant is a drop-in repair.
why_possibly_novel: Threshold-cliff noise accounting for PQ is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Jitter-based variance decomposition of PQ on COCO-panoptic across models, implement smooth matching, re-score and compare rank stability.
main_risk: Any new metric fights adoption inertia; position as diagnostic first, replacement second.
